p.seg: Qín raised an army and approached Zhōu to demand the Jiǔ Dǐng.
The Lord of Zhōu was distressed by this
and informed Yán Shuài.
Yán Shuài said,
"May Your Majesty not worry.
I request to go east to borrow aid from Qí."
Yán Shuài arrived in Qí
and said to the King of Qí,
"Qín's conduct is without the Way;
it wishes to raise troops, approach Zhōu, and demand the Jiǔ Dǐng.
The ruler and ministers of Zhōu
have internally exhausted their plans;
rather than giving them to Qín,
they believe it better to bestow them upon your Great State.
Saving a state in peril
is a beautiful reputation;
obtaining the Jiǔ Dǐng
is a profound treasure.
I hope Your Majesty will consider this."
The King of Qí was greatly pleased,
dispatched fifty thousand troops,
and sent Chén Chén Sī to lead them to save Zhōu,
whereupon the Qín army withdrew.
Qí then sought to demand the Jiǔ Dǐng,
and the Lord of Zhōu was again distressed by this.
Yán Shuài said,
"May Your Majesty not worry;
I request to go east and resolve this."
Yán Shuài arrived in Qí
and said to the King of Qí,
"Zhōu relied on the righteousness of your Great State
to allow its ruler and ministers, fathers and sons, to protect one another.
We wish to offer the Jiǔ Dǐng,
but I do not know what route your Great State will follow to bring them to Qí?"
The King of Qí said,
"I intend to request passage through Liáng."
Yán Shuài said,
"That is not possible.
The ruler and ministers of Liáng have desired to obtain the Jiǔ Dǐng
and have plotted for them beneath the Huī Tái
and upon the Shǎo Hǎi
for a long time now.
Once the cauldrons enter Liáng,
they will certainly not come out."
The King of Qí said,
"I intend to request passage through Chǔ."
He replied,
"That is not possible.
The ruler and ministers of Chǔ have desired to obtain the Jiǔ Dǐng
and have plotted for them within the Yè Tíng
for a long time now.
If they enter Chǔ,
the cauldrons will certainly not come out."
The King said,
"Then what route will I ultimately follow
to bring them to Qí?"
Yán Shuài said,
"My humble state has indeed privately worried about this for Your Majesty.
As for the Jiǔ Dǐng,
they are not like vinegar jars or sauce pots
that can be carried in the arms or held in the hands to reach Qí;
nor are they like birds gathering or crows flying,
or hares rising or horses galloping,
that could suddenly stop in Qí.
Formerly, when Zhōu attacked Yīn
and obtained the Jiǔ Dǐng,
ninety thousand men were required to pull a single cauldron,
and for all nine, nine times eighty-one, or eight hundred and ten thousand men were needed.
The soldiers and laborers,
the equipment and supplies,
all the preparations were in proportion to this.
Now, even if Your Majesty has the men,
what route will you follow for them to exit?
I have privately worried about this for Your Majesty."
The King of Qí said,
"The many times you have come
is still just a way of not giving them to me."
Yán Shuài said,
"I would not dare deceive your Great State.
Once you quickly determine the route they shall follow,
my humble state will move the cauldrons to await your command."
The King of Qí then desisted.
Qín attacked Yíyáng.
The Lord of Zhōu said to Zhào Lèi,
"What do you think of this?"
He replied,
"Yíyáng will certainly be captured."
The Lord said,
"The city of Yíyáng is eight lǐ square,
with one hundred thousand talented soldiers,
and grain to last several years.
Gōng Zhòng's army is two hundred thousand,
and Jǐng Cuì, with the masses of Chǔ,
is approaching the mountains to save it.
Qín will surely have no success."
He replied,
"Gān Mào
is a traveler in a foreign land.
If he attacks Yíyáng and has success,
then he is like Zhōu Gōng Dàn;
if he has no success,
he will leave no trace in Qín.
The King of Qín disregarded the counsel of his ministers and kinsmen to attack Yíyáng;
if Yíyáng is not captured,
the King of Qín will be shamed.
Therefore, I say it will be captured."
The Lord said,
"If you were to plan for me,
what should be done?"
He replied,
"Your Lordship should say to Jǐng Cuì:
'Your rank is that of a Zhí Guī
and your office is that of Zhù Guó.
If you fight and win,
nothing can be added to your status;
if you do not win,
then you will die.
It would be better to turn your back on Qín and support Yíyáng.
If you advance your troops,
Qín will fear that you will take advantage of their exhaustion
and will certainly use treasures to serve you.
Gōng Zhòng will admire you for taking advantage of Qín on his behalf
and will also certainly exhaust his treasures on you.'"
Qín captured Yíyáng,
and Jǐng Cuì indeed advanced his troops.
Qín was afraid
and immediately surrendered Zhǔzǎo,
and the Hán clan indeed also offered heavy treasures.
Jǐng Cuì obtained a city from Qín
and received treasures from Hán,
and was grateful to Dōngzhōu.
Dōngzhōu and Xīzhōu were at war,
and Hán was saving Xīzhōu.
On behalf of Dōngzhōu, one said to the King of Hán,
"Xīzhōu
is the state of the former Son of Heaven,
and it has many famous vessels and heavy treasures.
If you restrain your troops and do not go out,
you can make Dōngzhōu feel indebted to you,
and the treasures of Xīzhōu can be completely exhausted."
Dōngzhōu and Xīzhōu were in conflict;
Xīzhōu wished to make peace with Chǔ and Hán.
Qí Míng said to the Lord of Dōngzhōu,
"I fear that Xīzhōu will give treasures to Chǔ and Hán
and order them to demand land from Dōngzhōu on their behalf.
It would be better to say to Chǔ and Hán:
'Xīzhōu's desire to offer treasures
is wavering between two ends.
If Dōngzhōu's troops do not press Xīzhōu,
the treasures of Xīzhōu will not enter Chǔ or Hán.
If Chǔ and Hán wish to obtain the treasures,
they should urge us to attack Xīzhōu.
When Xīzhōu's treasures are given out,
it will be we who have obtained the treasures for Chǔ and Hán
to make them indebted to us,
and Xīzhōu will be weakened.'"
Dōngzhōu wished to plant rice,
but Xīzhōu would not release the water;
Dōngzhōu was distressed by this.
Sū Zǐ said to the Lord of Dōngzhōu,
"I request to make Xīzhōu release the water; is that acceptable?"
He then went to see the Lord of Xīzhōu and said,
"Your Lordship's plan is in error!
By not releasing the water now,
you are making Dōngzhōu wealthy.
Now their people are all planting wheat,
and no other crop.
If Your Lordship wishes to harm them,
it would be better to release the water for once
to ruin what they have planted.
If you release the water,
Dōngzhōu will certainly plant rice again;
when they have planted rice, you can then withhold it from them again.
If it is like this,
then the people of Dōngzhōu can be made to look only to Xīzhōu
and receive their orders from Your Lordship."
The Lord of Xīzhōu said,
"Excellent."
He then released the water.
Sū Zǐ also received gold from both states.
Zhāo Xiàn was in Yángzhái;
the Lord of Zhōu was going to order the Chancellor to go there,
but the Chancellor did not wish to go.
Sū Lì spoke on his behalf to the Lord of Zhōu, saying,
"When the King of Chǔ and the King of Wèi met,
Your Lordship ordered Chén Fēng to go to Chǔ
and ordered Xiàng Gōng to go to Wèi.
When Chǔ and Hán met,
Your Lordship ordered Xǔ Gōng to go to Chǔ
and ordered Xiàng Gōng to go to Hán."
Now, Zhāo Xiàn is not a ruler of men,
yet my Lord commands the Chancellor to go to him;
if their King were in Yángdí,
whom would my Lord command to go then?"
The Lord of Zhōu said,
"Good."
He then stopped the journey.
Qín requested passage through Zhōu to attack Hán.
Zhōu feared that granting it would offend Hán,
while not granting it would offend Qín.
Shǐ Yǎn said to the Lord of Zhōu,
"Why does my Lord not send someone to say to Gōngshū of Hán:
'The reason Qín dares to cross the passes to attack Hán
is because they trust Dōngzhōu.
Why do you not give land to Zhōu,
and send a high-ranking envoy to Chǔ?
Qín will certainly become suspicious
and no longer trust Zhōu;
thus Hán will not be attacked.'
Then also say to the King of Qín:
'Hán is forcibly giving land to Zhōu
in order to make Qín suspicious of Zhōu,
and I did not dare refuse it.'
Qín will certainly have no excuse and will command Zhōu not to accept it;
in this way, land is obtained from Hán while obeying Qín."
Chǔ attacked Yōngshì,
and Zhōu provided grain to Qín and Hán.
The King of Chǔ was angry with Zhōu,
and the Lord of Zhōu was worried about it.
Someone spoke to the King of Chǔ on behalf of Zhōu, saying:
"With your Majesty’s strength to be angry at Zhōu,
Zhōu is terrified
and will surely unite its state with those to whom it gave grain;
this will strengthen your Majesty’s enemies.
Therefore, it would be better for your Majesty to quickly relieve Zhōu’s fear;
having previously offended and later being pardoned,
they will surely serve your Majesty generously."
Zhōu Zuì said to Shí Lǐ:
"Why do you not use Qín to attack Qí?
I shall ask Qí to make you Chancellor;
if you use Qí to serve Qín,
there will certainly be no place for trouble.
You can then have Zhōu Zuì reside in Wèi to assist in this;
thus the world will be controlled by you.
You will be honored in the east by Qí
and respected in the west by Qín;
if Qín and Qí unite,
then you will always be honored."
The Chancellor of Zhōu, Lǚ Cāng,
presented a guest to the Lord of Zhōu.
The former Chancellor, Gōngshī Jiè, feared the guest would harm him,
so he sent someone to say to the Lord of Zhōu:
"This guest
is a persuasive orator,
but the reason he is unsuitable
is that he enjoys slandering others."
Lord Wén of Zhōu dismissed the official Gōngshī Jiè
and made Lǚ Cāng Chancellor,
but the people of the state were not pleased.
The Lord felt deep concern.
Someone said to Lord Wén of Zhōu:
"A state must have criticism and praise;
a loyal minister causes the criticism to fall upon himself
and the praise to go to the superior.
The Lord of Sòng took away the people's farming time to build a terrace,
and the people criticized him
because there was no loyal minister to cover for him.
Zǐhǎn gave up the Chancellorship to become the Minister of Works;
the people criticized Zǐhǎn and thought well of their Lord.
Duke Huán of Qí had seven markets within his palace
and seven hundred brothels;
the people of the state criticized him.
Guǎn Zhòng therefore established the Sānguī residence
to cover for Duke Huán;
was this not harming his own reputation among the people?
The *Chūnqiū* records ministers assassinating their lords by the hundreds,
and all were high officials who were highly praised.
Therefore, when high officials receive praise,
it is not a benefit to the state.
Thus, the masses form a force,
and accumulated bits make a mountain."
The Lord of Zhōu thus did not dismiss him.
A man from Wēn went to Zhōu,
but Zhōu would not admit him.
The guest immediately replied:
"I am a host."
When asked about his alley, he did not know it,
so the officials imprisoned him.
The Lord sent someone to ask him:
"You are not a man of Zhōu,
yet you say you are not a guest, why?"
He replied:
"When I was young, I recited the *Shī*;
the *Shī* says:
'Under the vast sky,
all is the King’s land;
along the shores of the land,
all are the King’s subjects.'
Now since the Lord of Zhōu rules the world,
then I am a subject of the Son of Heaven;
how then could I be a guest?
Therefore I said I am a host."
The Lord then ordered the officials to release him.
Someone spoke to Jīn Tóu on behalf of Zhōu Zuì, saying:
"Qín uses Zhōu Zuì’s presence in Qí to make the world suspicious,
and they also know that Zhào finds it difficult to fight the people of Qí;
fearing that if Qí and Hán unite,
they will certainly first unite with Qín.
If Qín and Qí unite,
then your state will be empty.
It would be better for you to save Qí,
and then assist Qín in attacking Hán and Wèi;
Shàngdǎng and Zhǎngzǐ will then be possessed by Zhào
entirely.
You can collect treasures from Qí in the east,
take land from Hán in the south,
and Wèi will follow suit;
slowly moving towards the east,
then there will be an alliance."
Zhōu Zuì said to Jīn Tóu:
"You are mistakenly ordering Qín to fight with the strong Qí.
If they win the battle,
Qín will take over Qí
and grant fiefs there,
ensuring there are no excessive cessions,
and dictate the battles of the world;
if they do not win,
the state will be greatly harmed,
and will have no choice but to obey Qín.
Qín will take all of Hán and Wèi’s Shàngdǎng and Tàiyuán,
and in the west, what Qín already possesses will be finalized.
Qín’s land
will be half of the world,
controlling the fates of Qí, Chǔ, and the Sānjìn;
then the state and your own person will be in danger;
what kind of strategy is this?"
Shí Xíngqín said to the Dàliángzào:
"If you wish to secure the reputation of a Hegemon or King,
it would be best to prepare the persuasive and wise men of the two Zhōus."
He said to the Lord of Zhōu:
"My Lord, you should command your persuasive and wise men
to contend on your behalf in Qín."
Someone said to the Lord of Xuē:
"Zhōu Zuì was close to the King of Qí,
yet he was expelled;
the King listens to Zhù Fú
and makes Lǚ Lǐ Chancellor
because he wishes to win over Qín.
If Qín and Qí unite,
Zhù Fú and Lǚ Lǐ will be honored.
Having both Zhōu and Qí,
Qín will certainly look down on you.
You should quickly send troops north to Zhào to join with Qín and Wèi,
bring in Zhōu Zuì to follow in the rear;
this will overturn the King of Qí’s trust
and also stop the alliance of the world.
When Qí is without Qín,
and the world is resolute,
Zhù Fú will surely flee;
with whom then will the King of Qí manage his state?"
Qí listened to Zhù Fú
and excluded Zhōu Zuì.
Someone said to the King of Qí:
"Expelling Zhōu Zuì,
listening to Zhù Fú,
and making Lǚ Lǐ Chancellor
are done because you wish to win over Qín deeply.
If Qín gains control of the world,
then its attack on Qí will be severe.
When Qí unites with others,
then Zhào fears being attacked,
so it hurriedly shows its military to Qín.
Qín, seeing Zhào's attack,
will join Qí in attacking Zhào;
the reality and the principle are the same,
things will certainly not remain settled.
Therefore, employing Zhù Fú
is indeed the logic of the world."
Sū Lì, on behalf of Zhōu Zuì, said to Sū Qín:
"My Lord, you should have the King listen to Zhōu Zuì,
to use land to unite with Wèi and Zhào,
and certainly provoke an alliance with Qí;
this way, you use the alliance with Qí and strong Chǔ to employ Chǎn Zǐ.
If you wish to take advantage of Zhōu Zuì’s situation,
then the one who unites Qí
is you;
while the one who cedes the land
is Zhōu Zuì."
Someone said to Zhōu Zuì:
"Qiú Hè is serving as the Prime Minister of Sòng.
He intends to observe how Qín responds to Zhào and Sòng
in order to defeat the Three Kingdoms.
If the Three Kingdoms are not defeated,
he will join Zhào and Sòng with the Eastern powers to isolate Qín.
He will also observe Hán and Wèi's attitude toward Qí.
If they are not firm,
he will join Sòng to defeat the Three Kingdoms;
otherwise, he will sell out Zhào and Sòng to the Three Kingdoms.
Why do you not send someone to tell the Kings of Hán and Wèi:
'Do you wish for Qín and Zhào to sell each other out?
Why not join together to make Zhōu Zuì the Prime Minister of both states?
When they see that you cannot be separated,
Qín and Zhào will surely sell each other out
to align with Your Majesties.'"
On behalf of Zhōu Zuì, a speaker said to the King of Wèi:
"Qín knows that Zhào finds it difficult to fight Qí
and fears an alliance between Qí and Zhào,
so Qín will surely secretly encourage Zhào.
Zhào dares not fight,
fearing that Qín will not support them,
so they will first align with Qí.
When Qín and Zhào contend for Qí,
if Your Majesty has no representative there,
it will be unacceptable.
If Your Majesty does not dismiss Zhōu Zuì
but instead joins with and receives Qí,
and then uses the urgency of your troops to attack Qí,
you will have no pretext for your actions."
A speaker said to Zhōu Zuì:
"The King of Wèi has entrusted the state to you, Sir,
because he values an alliance with Qín to attack Qí.
Lord Xuē was your former master;
he lightly forgot his own Xuē
and disregarded the tombs of his ancestors.
Yet you alone maintain empty loyalty to perform noble deeds,
making it clear to the other ministers that you hold to your former master
and will not participate in the attack on Qí.
This will basically only anger powerful Qín and is unacceptable.
You should instead say to the King of Wèi and Lord Xuē:
'I request to enter Qí on behalf of the King.
The world cannot harm Qí.
If a change occurs,
I request to save it;
if no change occurs,
the King may then attack it.
Furthermore, if I were to act as a servant of Qí
and thus burden the King's relations with the world,
it would be unacceptable.
The King's favors to me are generous;
if I enter Qí,
the King will also be free from the burden of Qí.'"
Zhào seized the sacrificial lands of Zhōu.
The Lord of Zhōu was distressed by this
and spoke to Zhèng Zhāo.
Zhèng Zhāo said:
"Do not be distressed, My Lord.
I request thirty pieces of gold to retrieve them for you."
The Lord of Zhōu gave them to him.
Zhèng Zhāo presented them to the Great Diviner of Zhào
and informed him about the matter of the sacrificial lands.
When the King fell ill,
he had the Diviner perform a divination.
The Great Diviner blamed it, saying:
"The sacrificial lands of Zhōu are causing a curse."
Zhào then returned them.
Dù Hè wished to make Jǐng Cuì important in Zhōu.
He said to the Lord of Zhōu:
"Your state is small.
If you exhaust your noble treasures and gems to serve the feudal lords,
you must examine the consequences.
It is like a bird-catcher:
if he sets his net where there are no birds,
he will get nothing all day;
if he sets it where there are many birds,
he will startle them away.
He must set it where there might or might not be birds;
only then can he catch many.
Now if you bestow gifts upon great men,
they will look down on you;
if you bestow them upon petty men,
they have nothing you can ask for,
and it only wastes your wealth.
You must bestow them upon the currently poor scholars
who are destined to become great men;
thus you will achieve your desires."
When the Crown Prince of Zhōu Gòng died,
there were five sons by concubines
whom he loved equally,
but no legal heir had been established.
Sīmǎ Jiǎn said to the King of Chǔ:
"Why not enfeoff Gōngzǐ Jiù
and request that he be made the Crown Prince?"
Zuǒ Chéng said to Sīmǎ Jiǎn:
"If the Lord of Zhōu does not listen,
then your wisdom will be seen as lacking and your relations with Zhōu will be severed.
It is better to say to the Lord of Zhōu:
'Whom do you wish to establish?
Secretly inform Jiǎn,
and Jiǎn will have the King of Chǔ provide him with land.'
If you wish to become the Crown Prince,
then send someone to tell the Prime Minister Yù Zhǎn Zǐ and the attendant Qiáng Fū Kōng:
'The King seems to want to make him the heir.
He is a capable man;
for him to remain in Chǔ is not convenient for the Prime Minister.'"
The Prime Minister then ordered him to be made the Crown Prince.
When the Three Kingdoms pressured Qín,
Zhōu ordered its Prime Minister to go to Qín.
Because Qín treated him lightly,
he delayed his journey.
Someone said to the Prime Minister:
"Whether Qín is influential or not
is not yet known.
Qín wants to know the situation of the Three Kingdoms.
You should go see the King of Qín and say:
'I request to tell the King of the arrangements of the Eastern states.'
Qín will surely value you.
In this way, you will be valued by Zhōu,
and use your standing in Zhōu to win over Qín.
Qí is influential and thus has Zhōu as an ally;
if you have already won over Qí,
then Zhōu will never lose its alliance with powerful states."
Chāng Tā fled Xī Zhōu
and went to Dōng Zhōu,
where he revealed all of Xī Zhōu's secrets to Dōng Zhōu.
Dōng Zhōu was greatly pleased,
and Xī Zhōu was greatly enraged.
Féng Dàn said:
"I can kill him."
The Lord gave him thirty jin of gold.
Féng Dàn sent a man with the gold and a letter.
He secretly sent the letter to Chāng Tā, saying:
"To Chāng Tā:
if the matter can be accomplished,
strive to complete it;
if it cannot be accomplished,
hurry back at once, back at once!
If the matter lingers, it will leak,
and you will cause your own death."
He then sent someone to tell the border guards of Dōng Zhōu:
"Tonight, a traitor will be entering."
The guards caught him and presented him to Dōng Zhōu,
and Dōng Zhōu immediately executed Chāng Tā.
Zhāo Jiǎn was on bad terms with Dōng Zhōu.
Someone said to Zhāo Jiǎn:
"I will devise a secret plan for you."
Zhāo Jiǎn asked:
"What is it?"
"Xī Zhōu hates Dōng Zhōu very much
and once wanted Dōng Zhōu to be on bad terms with Chǔ.
Xī Zhōu will surely send an assassin to kill you
and then declare that Dōng Zhōu did it,
relying on Xī Zhōu's influence with the King."
Zhāo Jiǎn said:
"Good.
But I also fear that Dōng Zhōu will assassinate me
to slight Xī Zhōu and make Chǔ hate them."
He immediately made peace with Dōng Zhōu.
The Yán clan committed an assassination,
and Yáng Shù was an accomplice.
They passed through Zhōu.
The Lord of Zhōu detained them for fourteen days,
then provided them with a carriage and four horses and sent them on their way.
Hán sent a messenger to rebuke Zhōu.
The Lord of Zhōu was distressed.
A guest said to the Lord:
"Tell them directly:
'I knew the Yán clan committed the assassination
and that Yáng Shù was with them,
so I detained them for fourteen days to await your instructions.
A small state is not large enough to harbor assassins;
since Your Majesty's messenger did not arrive,
I sent them away.'"
Lord Xuē used Qí on behalf of Hán and Wèi to attack Chǔ,
and also joined Hán and Wèi to attack Qín;
he then borrowed troops and requested provisions from Xī Zhōu.
Hán Qìng spoke to Lord Xuē on behalf of Xī Zhōu:
"You used Qí for Hán and Wèi to attack Chǔ.
In nine years, you took the lands north of Wǎn and Yè to strengthen Hán and Wèi.
Now you attack Qín again to benefit them further.
When Hán and Wèi have no worries of Chǔ to the south
and no trouble from Qín to the west,
their territory will be broad and their influence will increase,
and Qí will surely be diminished.
Since the root and the branch alternate in prosperity,
and emptiness and fullness have their times,
I privately fear for your safety."
It would be better for you to have our humble state secretly align with Qín while you refrain from attacking,
and also neither borrow troops nor request provisions.
You should approach Hángǔ without attacking
and have our humble state say to the King of Qín on your behalf:
“Xuē Gōng is determined to crush Qín to expand Hán and Wèi.
The reason he advances his troops
is that he wants Your Majesty to order Chǔ to cede its eastern lands to Qí.”
If the King of Qín releases the King of Chǔ to make peace,
and you have our humble state demonstrate this loyalty to Qín,
Qín will avoid being crushed
and will use Chǔ’s eastern lands to save itself;
it will surely desire this.
Once the King of Chǔ is released,
he will certainly be grateful to Qí.
Qí will obtain the eastern lands and grow stronger,
and Xuē will be without worry for generations.
Qín will not be significantly weakened
and will remain to the west of the Sān Jìn,
so the Sān Jìn will surely hold Qí in high esteem.”
Xuē Gōng said,
“Excellent.”
He then ordered Hán Qìng to enter Qín,
caused the three states not to attack Qín,
and made it so they did not borrow troops or request provisions from Xī Zhōu.
Qín attacked the Wèi general Xī Wǔ’s army at Yī Quē,
then advanced its troops to attack Zhōu.
For the sake of Zhōu, Zhōu Zuì said to Lǐ Duì:
“It would be better for you to forbid Qín from attacking Zhōu.
The best plan for Zhào
is to make Qín and Wèi fight again.
Now if Qín attacks Zhōu and succeeds,
then its multitude will surely suffer many casualties.
If Qín wants to wait for the acquisition of Zhōu,
it will certainly not attack Wèi;
if Qín attacks Zhōu and does not succeed,
then having the fatigue of the previous victory over Wèi
and the subsequent defeat of attacking Zhōu,
it will also certainly not attack Wèi.
Now if you forbid it,
while Qín has not yet made peace with Wèi,
and the whole of Zhào orders it to stop,
it will surely not dare to disobey.
This way, you will have repelled Qín and stabilized Zhōu.
Once Qín leaves Zhōu,
it will certainly attack Wèi again.
Wèi will not be able to hold out
and will surely seek peace through you,
so you will be held in high esteem.
If Wèi does not seek peace
and struggles to hold out,
then you will have preserved Zhōu while Qín and Wèi fight.
All the influence will then rest with Zhào.”
Qín ordered Chū Lǐ Jí to enter Zhōu with one hundred chariots.
The Lord of Zhōu welcomed him with soldiers
and was very respectful.
The King of Chǔ was angry
and rebuked Zhōu
because it showed such honor to the Qín guest.
Yóu Téng said to the King of Chǔ:
“In the past, Zhì Bó wanted to invade Qiú Yóu,
so he sent them a large bell
carried on a broad chariot,
then followed behind it with troops;
Qiú Yóu was ultimately destroyed
because it had no defenses.
When Huán Gōng attacked Cài,
he publicly claimed to be attacking Chǔ,
but in reality he launched a surprise attack on Cài.
Now Qín
is a state of tigers and wolves,
and it has the intent to swallow Zhōu;
it sent Chū Lǐ Jí into Zhōu with one hundred chariots.
The Lord of Zhōu was terrified of this,
and taking warning from the examples of Cài and Qiú Yóu,
he placed soldiers with long weapons in the front
and strong crossbowmen in the rear.
It was called escorting Chū Lǐ Jí,
but in reality he was imprisoning him.
How could the Lord of Zhōu not love his state?
He feared its destruction at any moment
and was worried for Your Majesty.”
The King of Chǔ was then pleased.
During the campaign at Yōng Shì,
Hán requisitioned armor and grain from Zhōu.
The Lord of Zhōu was troubled by this
and told Sū Dài.
Sū Dài said,
“Why be troubled?
I can ensure that Hán does not requisition armor and grain from Zhōu,
and also obtain Gāo Dū for you.”
The Lord of Zhōu was greatly pleased and said,
“If you can truly do this,
I shall place the state at your disposal.”
Sū Dài then went to see the Chancellor of Hán, Gōng Zhōng, and said,
“Have you not heard of Chǔ’s plan?
Zhāo Yìng said to the King of Chǔ:
‘Hán is exhausted by the war,
its granaries are empty,
and it has no means to defend its cities.
I shall wear them down with hunger,
and in no more than a month, we will surely take them.’
Now you have besieged Yōng Shì for five months without being able to take it;
this shows Chǔ is distressed.
The King of Chǔ began to doubt Zhāo Yìng’s plan.
But now you are requisitioning armor and grain from Zhōu;
this is announcing Hán’s own distress to Chǔ.
If Zhāo Yìng hears of this,
he will surely urge the King of Chǔ to increase his troops and maintain the siege at Yōng Shì,
and Yōng Shì will surely fall.”
Gōng Zhōng said,
“Excellent.
However, my messengers have already departed.”
Sū Dài said,
“Why not give Gāo Dū to Zhōu?”
Gōng Zhōng said angrily,
“I have already refrained from requisitioning armor and grain from Zhōu,
which is already a lot.
Why should I give them Gāo Dū?”
Sū Dài said,
“If you give them Gāo Dū,
Zhōu will certainly turn and align with Hán.
When Qín hears of this, it will surely be greatly enraged
and will burn Zhōu’s diplomatic tallies
and cut off its messengers.
Thus, by using a worn-out Gāo Dū, you will gain a secure Zhōu;
why not give it?”
Gōng Zhōng said,
“Excellent.”
He did not requisition armor and grain from Zhōu and gave them Gāo Dū.
Chǔ ultimately failed to take Yōng Shì and withdrew.
The Lord of Zhōu went to Qín.
It was said to Zhōu Zuì:
“It would be better to praise the filial piety of the King of Qín
and then offer Yìng as a garden for the Queen Mother’s sustenance.
The King of Qín and the Queen Mother will surely be delighted,
and this will mean you have won over Qín.
If relations are good,
the Lord of Zhōu will surely attribute it to your merit;
if relations turn sour,
those who urged the Lord of Zhōu to enter Qín
will surely be held at fault.”
Sū Lì said to the Lord of Zhōu:
“The one who defeated Hán and Wèi,
killed Xī Wǔ,
attacked Zhào,
and took Lìn, Lí Shí, and Qí
was Bái Qǐ.
This is because he is skilled in the use of troops
and also has the mandate of Heaven.
Now he is attacking Liáng;
Liáng will surely fall.
If it falls, then Zhōu will be in danger.
You had better stop him.
Say to Bái Qǐ:
‘In Chǔ there was a man named Yǎng Yóu Jī
who was a skilled archer.
He could hit a willow leaf from a hundred paces away,
hitting it a hundred times in a hundred shots.
Everyone around him said he was excellent.
One person passed by and said,
“A fine archer indeed,
but he can still be taught
how to shoot.” Yǎng Yóu Jī said,
“Everyone else says I am excellent;
why do you say I can still be taught?
Why don’t you try shooting in my place?”
The guest said,
“I cannot teach you how to position your left arm or bend your right.
But a man who shoots willow leaves,
hitting a hundred times in a hundred shots,
if he does not know when to rest,
soon his strength will flag,
his bow will warp and his arrows will curve,
and if just one shot misses,
all his previous merit will be lost.”
Now you have defeated Hán and Wèi,
killed Xī Wǔ,
and attacked Zhào in the north,
taking Lìn, Lí Shí, and Qí;
all this was your doing.
Your merits are many.
Now you are leading Qín’s troops out of the passes,
passing the two Zhōu,
crossing Hán to attack Liáng.
If one attack fails,
your previous merits will all be wiped out.
It would be better for you to claim illness and not go out.’”
The Chǔ troops were south of the mountains.
Wú Dé was about to direct the King of Chǔ’s anger towards Zhōu.
Someone said to the Lord of Zhōu:
“It would be better to have the Crown Prince and General Zhèng welcome Wú Dé at the border,
while you yourself welcome him in the outskirts,
so that everyone in the world will know how much you value Wú Dé.”
Therefore, the matter was leaked to Chǔ,
saying:
"The vessels with which the Lord of Zhōu serves me
must be named 'Plotting against Chǔ'."
"The King will surely demand them,
and since my gains cannot be produced as evidence,
the King will surely punish him."
Chǔ requested passage through the area between the two Zhōu states
in order to confront Hán and Wèi.
The Lord of Zhōu was distressed by this.
Sū Qín said to the Lord of Zhōu:
"If you clear a path connecting to the Hé River,
Hán and Wèi will surely loathe it.
Qí and Qín, fearing that Chǔ will take the Nine Tripods,
will surely rescue Hán and Wèi and attack Chǔ.
If Chǔ cannot defend the area outside of Fāngchéng,
how can they pass through the area between the two Zhōu states?
If the four states do not loathe it,
even if you do not wish to grant it,
Chǔ will surely take it for themselves."
Sīkòu Bù, on behalf of Zhōu Zuì, said to the Lord of Zhōu:
"Your Lordship sent someone to tell the King of Qí that Zhōu Zuì is unwilling to become the Crown Prince;
I believe your Lordship should not have done this.
Hányěshì bought an excellent sword for Tàigōng of Qí,
but the Duke did not recognize its quality;
he returned the sword and demanded his gold back.
A man of Yuè requested to buy it for a thousand pieces of gold,
but he broke it rather than sell it.
When he was about to die,
he instructed his son, saying:
'You must not be the only one who knows value.'
Now, your Lordship's making Zuì the Crown Prince
is a secret pact known only to you;
no one in the world believes it yet.
I fear the King of Qí thinks your Lordship has actually established Guǒ
but is pretending to abdicate in favor of Zuì
so as to palm him off onto Qí.
Your Lordship is considered full of artifice,
and Zuì is considered full of deceit.
Why does your Lordship not buy credibility?
Show no stinginess in providing for Zuì's upkeep,
and let the whole world see it."
Qín summoned the Lord of Zhōu,
but the Lord of Zhōu found it difficult to go.
Someone, on behalf of the Lord of Zhōu, said to the King of Wèi:
"Qín has summoned the Lord of Zhōu
intending to make him attack Nányáng in Wèi.
Why does Your Majesty not send troops out to Hénán?
When the Lord of Zhōu hears of this,
he will use it as an excuse to Qín and not go.
If the Lord of Zhōu does not enter Qín,
Qín will surely not dare to cross the Hé River to attack Nányáng."
After Wǔ was defeated at Yīquē,
the Lord of Zhōu went to Wèi to seek help,
but the King of Wèi declined, citing the emergency at Shàngdǎng.
On his return, the Lord of Zhōu
saw the Liáng Garden and was delighted by it.
Qímǔ Huī said to the Lord of Zhōu:
"The Wēn Garden is no less than this,
and it is closer.
I can obtain it for you."
Returning to see the King of Wèi,
the King asked:
"Does the Lord of Zhōu resent me?"
He replied:
"He does not resent you.
Moreover, who would resent Your Majesty?
I am concerned about a calamity for Your Majesty.
The Lord of Zhōu
is a master of strategy.
He had planned to use his state to defend against Qín for Your Majesty,
but Your Majesty did not provide him with the means to defend.
I see that he will surely use his state to serve Qín;
Qín will mobilize all troops from beyond the passes
and join with the masses of Zhōu to attack Nányáng,
and the two Shàngdǎng regions will be cut off."
The King of Wèi said:
"If so, then what should be done?"
Qímǔ Huī said:
"The Lord of Zhōu appears not to care for small gains,
but in serving Qín, he actually covets small gains.
If Your Majesty now grants him a garrison of thirty thousand men along with the Wēn Garden,
the Lord of Zhōu will have an excuse to give to his kinsmen and people,
and taking the Wēn Garden as a pleasure,
he will surely not align with Qín.
I have heard that the profit from the Wēn Garden
is eighty pieces of gold annually;
if the Lord of Zhōu obtains the Wēn Garden,
the amount he will use to serve Your Majesty
will be one hundred and twenty pieces of gold annually;
thus, for every trouble in Shàngdǎng, you gain forty pieces of gold."
The King of Wèi therefore sent Mèng Mǎo to present the Wēn Garden to the Lord of Zhōu and granted him the garrison.
When Hán and Wèi exchanged land,
Xīzhōu found it disadvantageous.
Fán Yú said to the King of Chǔ:
"Zhōu will surely perish.
In the land exchange between Hán and Wèi,
Hán gains two counties,
and Wèi loses two counties.
The reason they are doing this
is to completely envelop the two Zhōu states;
this is worth more than two counties,
for the Nine Tripods are located there.
Furthermore, if Wèi possesses Nányáng, the Zhèng lands, and Sānchuān while enveloping the two Zhōu states,
then the area outside of Chǔ's Fāngchéng will be in danger;
if Hán annexes both Shàngdǎng regions to confront Zhào,
then Zhào's Yángcháng and the areas above it will be in danger.
Therefore, when the exchange is completed,
both Chǔ and Zhào will be marginalized."
The King of Chǔ was afraid
and relied on Zhào to stop the exchange.
Qín wished to attack Zhōu,
and Zhōu Zuì said to the King of Qín:
"For one planning Your Majesty's national strategy,
they would not attack Zhōu.
Attacking Zhōu actually provides no benefit to the state,
yet the reputation of doing so would terrify the world.
When the world is terrified of Qín's reputation,
they will surely unite in the east with Qí.
If your troops are worn out at Zhōu
while the world unites with Qí,
then Qín will be isolated and unable to rule as king.
It is because the world wishes to exhaust Qín
that they encourage Your Majesty to attack Zhōu.
If Qín and the rest of the world are both exhausted,
then your commands will no longer hold sway over Zhōu."
Gōng Tā said to the Lord of Zhōu:
"Yuǎn relied on Qín and slighted Jìn;
when Qín suffered a famine, Yuǎn perished.
Zhèng relied on Wèi and slighted Hán;
when Wèi attacked Cài, Zhèng perished.
Zhū and Jǔ perished at the hands of Qí;
Chén and Cài perished at the hands of Chǔ.
These all occurred because they relied on distant supporting states and slighted nearby enemies.
Now your Lordship relies on Hán and Wèi and slights Qín;
I fear the state will be harmed.
Your Lordship would do better to have Zhōu Zuì secretly align with Zhào to prepare against Qín;
then you will not be destroyed."
Someone said to the King of Qí:
"Why does Your Majesty not grant land to Zhōu Zuì to make him the Crown Prince?"
The King of Qí ordered Sīmǎ Hàn to use bribes to promote Zhōu Zuì's standing in Zhōu.
Zuǒ Shàng said to Sīmǎ Hàn:
"If Zhōu does not listen,
this will show your wisdom is exhausted and your relations with Zhōu will be severed.
You would do better to say to the Lord of Zhōu:
'Whom do you wish to appoint?
Have someone secretly inform Hàn,
and Hàn will request the King to promote him with a gift of land.'"
Zuǒ Shàng gained employment through this.
When the three states returned from attacking Qín,
Xīzhōu feared that Wèi would borrow a passage through their territory.
On behalf of Xīzhōu, someone said to the King of Wèi:
"Chǔ and Sòng are not pleased that Qín is indebted to the three states;
they are about to attack Your Majesty's supply depots to benefit Qín."
The King of Wèi was afraid
and ordered the army to set up quarters and move quickly to the east.
After Wǔ was defeated,
Zhōu sent Zhōu Zú to Qín.
Someone said to Zhōu Zú:
"Why not say to the Lord of Zhōu:
'If I go to Qín,
the relations between Qín and Zhōu will surely sour.
Among your Lordship's ministers,
there are those whom Qín respects and wishes to make Chancellor;
they will surely slander me in Qín,
and I will be unable to carry out the mission.
I wish to be dismissed before I go.
Your Lordship should then appoint him as Chancellor;
once he becomes Chancellor,
he will no longer slander Zhōu to Qín.'
The Lord respects Qín,
which is why he sends the Chancellor;
if you are dismissed after leaving,
it would be slighting Qín;
therefore, you surely will not be dismissed.
If you say this and then go,
and relations with Qín are good,
then it will be your success;
if relations with Qín are bad,
then it was not good for you, and you would have been executed anyway."
Wèi Yāng fled from Wèi and entered Qín;
Duke Xiào made him Chancellor,
enfeoffed him at Shāng,
and he was titled the Lord of Shāng.
When the Lord of Shāng governed Qín,
the laws and decrees were fully implemented;
he was fair and selfless,
punishments did not avoid the powerful and great,
and rewards were not biased toward those close to him,
The law reached the Tàizǐ,
and his tutors were punished with tattooing and nose-cutting.
After a full year,
things lost on the road were not picked up,
the people did not take things improperly,
the military became very strong,
and the feudal lords were terrified.
However, Shāng Jūn was harsh and lacked kindness,
using only force to make them submit.
Xiào Gōng had practiced this for eight years
when he became so ill he could not get up;
he wished to pass the state to Shāng Jūn,
but Shāng Jūn declined and would not accept.
Once Xiào Gōng had died,
Huì Wáng succeeded him;
after he had been in power
for a short time,
Shāng Jūn requested leave to return home.
Someone persuaded Huì Wáng, saying:
"When high officials are too powerful, the state is in danger;
when those close to the ruler are too intimate, his person is in danger.
Now in Qín, even women and infants all speak of Shāng Jūn’s laws,
but none speak of Your Majesty’s laws.
Thus Shāng Jūn has instead become the master,
and Your Majesty has instead become the subject.
Furthermore, Shāng Jūn
is truly Your Majesty’s enemy;
I hope Your Majesty will take measures against him."
When Shāng Jūn returned,
Huì Wáng had him torn asunder by chariots,
but the people of Qín did not pity him.
When Sū Qín first intended to use the Horizontal Alliance
to persuade Qín Huì Wáng, he said:
"Your Majesty’s state,
to the west has the advantages of Bā, Shǔ, and Hànzhōng;
to the north has the utility of the Húhé and the horses of Dài;
to the south has the barriers of Wū Shān and Qiánzhōng;
and to the east has the strongholds of Yáo and Hán.
The fields are fertile and beautiful,
the people are numerous and wealthy;
you have ten thousand war chariots,
a million valiant soldiers,
fertile plains for a thousand lǐ,
and abundant stores of provisions;
the terrain is advantageous.
This is what is called a heavenly storehouse,
the most powerful state in the world.
With Your Majesty’s worthiness,
the multitude of your people,
the use of your chariots and cavalry,
and the training in the arts of war,
you can annex the feudal lords,
swallow the whole world,
and rule as Emperor.
I hope Your Majesty will pay a little attention,
and I beg to present its effectiveness."
Qín Wáng said:
"I have heard
that those whose feathers are not full cannot fly high;
those whose laws and regulations are not completed cannot carry out punishments;
those whose virtue is not deep cannot employ the people;
and those whose governance and education are not smooth cannot trouble the high officials.
Now you, sir, have come with dignity from a thousand lǐ away
to instruct me in my court;
I wish to do so another day."
Sū Qín said:
"I indeed suspected that Your Majesty would be unable to use my plan.
In the past, Shénnóng attacked Bǔsuì;
Huáng Dì attacked Zhuōlù and captured Chīyóu;
Yáo attacked Huāndōu;
Shùn attacked the Sānmiáo;
Yǔ attacked Gònggōng;
Tāng attacked the Xià;
Wén Wáng attacked Chóng;
Wǔ Wáng attacked Zhòu;
and Qí Huán relied on war to become Hegemon of the world.
Looking at it from this perspective,
how could anyone not resort to war?
In ancient times, chariots were made to collide and race,
and words were used to bind alliances
until the world became one;
Vertical and Horizontal Alliances were formed,
and weapons were never put away;
literary scholars embellished their words together,
and the feudal lords were confused and deluded;
ten thousand schemes arose at once,
so many they could not be managed;
once the laws and clauses were prepared,
the people showed much deceit;
writings and strategies became dense and chaotic,
and the common people were impoverished;
those above and those below grieved together,
and the people had nothing to rely on;
though words were explicated and principles clarified,
weapons and armor arose even more;
though there were eloquent speeches and grand attire,
battles and attacks did not cease;
though rhetoric was frequently used,
the world remained ungoverned;
tongues were worn out and ears became deaf,
yet no success was seen;
though righteousness was practiced and good faith pledged,
the world did not become close.
Thereupon,
literary pursuits were discarded and martial ones were employed;
brave warriors were generously maintained,
armor was repaired and weapons sharpened,
and victory was sought on the battlefield.
To gain profit while doing nothing
and expand territory while sitting peacefully—
even the ancient Wǔ Dì, Sān Wáng, and Wǔ Bà,
the enlightened rulers and worthy kings,
always desired to achieve it while sitting,
but the situation made it impossible,
so they followed up with war.
When there was distance, the two armies attacked each other;
when they were close, they struck each other with spears and halberds;
only then could great achievements be established.
Therefore, military victory was won abroad,
and righteousness was strengthened within;
authority was established above,
and the people were submissive below.
Now, if you wish to annex the world,
overpower the great states,
subdue enemy nations,
control the realm within the seas,
treat the common people as your children,
and make subjects of the feudal lords,
it is impossible without military force!
Present-day successor rulers
neglect the supreme way;
they are all muddled regarding education,
confused regarding governance,
lost in talk,
bewildered by words,
submerged in debates,
and drowned in rhetoric.
Judging by this,
Your Majesty indeed cannot carry it out."
He submitted ten memorials to the Qín Wáng to persuade him, but his persuasion was not followed.
His sable fur coat was worn out,
his hundred catties of gold were spent,
his resources were exhausted,
and he left Qín to return home.
With thin leggings and straw sandals,
carrying his books and shouldering a pack,
his appearance was haggard,
his face was dark and sallow,
and he looked defeated.
When he arrived home,
his wife did not stop her weaving,
his sister-in-law would not cook for him,
and his parents would not speak to him.
Sū Qín sighed deeply and said:
"My wife does not regard me as her husband,
my sister-in-law does not regard me as her brother-in-law,
and my parents do not regard me as their son;
this is all the fault of Qín."
Thereupon, at night he opened his books,
displaying dozens of chests,
and found the stratagems of the Tàigōng Yīnfú;
he bent over and recited them,
refining them for his analysis.
When he grew sleepy while reading,
he would take an awl and stab his own thigh,
until the blood flowed down to his feet.
He said:
"How could there be anyone who persuades a ruler
but cannot make him part with his gold, jade, silks, and embroideries,
nor attain the honor of a minister or chancellor?"
After a full year, his study was complete,
and he said:
"This truly can be used to persuade the rulers of this age!"
Thereupon, he approached the Yànwūjí Gate,
and met to persuade Zhào Wáng in his magnificent hall,
clapping his hands as he spoke.
Zhào Wáng was greatly pleased,
and enfeoffed him as Wǔ’ān Jūn.
He received the seal of the Chancellor,
one hundred chariots,
one thousand bolts of silk and embroidery,
one hundred pairs of white jade discs,
and ten thousand yì of gold,
all following behind him,
as he formed the Vertical Alliance and dissolved the Horizontal Alliance
in order to restrain the powerful state of Qín.
Therefore, Sū Qín served as Chancellor in Zhào,
and the passes were not opened.
At this time,
despite the greatness of the world,
the multitude of the people,
the majesty of the kings and marquises,
and the power of the strategic advisors,
all wished to be decided by Sū Qín's strategies.
Without spending a peck of grain,
without troubling a single soldier,
without a single warrior fighting,
without a single bowstring snapping,
without a single arrow breaking,
the feudal lords became close to one another,
more virtuous than brothers.
When a worthy man is present, the world submits;
when one man is employed, the world follows.
Therefore it is said:
"Govern by administration,
not by bravery;
govern within the court,
not beyond the four borders."
During the height of Qín,
ten thousand measures of gold were at his disposal.
Carriages rolled and horses followed in succession,
shining brilliantly upon the roads.
The states east of the mountains
submitted like the wind,
making Zhào of great importance.
Furthermore, Sū Qín was merely a scholar from a poor alley and a broken gate, with doors of mulberry and pivots of bent wood,
yet leaning on his carriage rail and holding the reins,
he traversed the world,
persuading the kings of the feudal lords in their courts,
silencing the mouths of their attendants,
such that no one in the world could rival him.
When he was about to persuade the King of Chǔ,
he passed through Luòyáng.
His parents heard of this,
cleaned the house and cleared the road,
arranged music and set out drinks,
welcoming him thirty lǐ into the suburbs.
His wife looked at him with askance eyes,
listening with tilted ears;
his sister-in-law crawled like a snake and prostrated herself,
bowing four times and kneeling to apologize.
Sū Qín said:
"Sister-in-law,
why were you so arrogant before and so humble now?"
The sister-in-law said:
"Because Jìzǐ's position is honorable
and he has much gold."
Sū Qín said:
"Alas!
When one is poor, even parents do not treat him as a son;
when one is rich and noble, even relatives are fearful.
For a man living in the world,
power, status, wealth, and honor,
can they indeed be ignored?"
Qín Huì Wáng said to Hánquánzǐ:
"Sū Qín has deceived me.
He wished to use the wisdom of one man
to manipulate the lords of the eastern mountains
into an alliance to deceive Qín.
Zhào surely relied on its multitudes,
so it first sent Sū Qín to bind the feudal lords with silk and gifts.
The feudal lords cannot be unified;
it is as clear as the fact that chickens tied together cannot all stay on a perch.
I am indignant,
having harbored anger for a long time.
I wish to send Wǔānzǐ to go and convey my intentions."
Hánquánzǐ said:
"That is not possible.
For attacking cities and toppling towns,
please use Wǔānzǐ.
For making our state's relations good and acting as an envoy to the feudal lords,
please use the guest minister Zhāng Yí."
Qín Huì Wáng said:
"I respectfully receive your command."
Lìng Xiàng said to the King of Qín:
"I wished to use Qí to serve the King
by having it attack Sòng.
If Sòng is broken,
the state of Jìn will be in danger,
and Ānyì will belong to the King.
Yàn and Zhào will detest the alliance between Qí and Qín,
and will surely cede land to associate with the King.
Qí will certainly value the King,
so my having them attack Sòng
was also to frighten Qí and make it value the King.
Why does the King dislike my having them attack Sòng?
I thought the King's wisdom had already known this,
so I did not speak of it."
Zhāng Yí persuaded the King of Qín, saying:
"Your servant has heard
that to speak without knowing is unwise,
and to know without speaking is disloyal.
As a subject, to be disloyal deserves death,
and to speak without scrutiny also deserves death.
Even so,
your servant wishes to speak all that he has heard;
let the Great King judge the crime.
Your servant has heard
that the world plans to connect Yàn in the north and Wèi in the south,
link Jīng and secure Qí,
and gather the remnants of Hán to form the Vertical Alliance,
intending to move southwest to trouble Qín.
Your servant secretly laughs at this.
There are three ways to ruin in the world,
and if the world possesses them,
this must be what is meant!
Your servant has heard it said,
'He who attacks order with chaos will be ruined;
he who attacks the upright with the wicked will be ruined;
he who attacks the compliant with the rebellious will be ruined.'
Now the treasuries of the world are not full,
and the granaries are empty.
They mobilize all their soldiers and people,
deploying armies of millions,
with naked blades in front
and execution blocks behind,
yet they all flee,
unable to face death.
To blame their people for being unable to die is wrong;
it is their superiors who are unable to make them kill.
When rewards are spoken of, they are not given;
when punishments are spoken of, they are not carried out.
Because rewards and punishments are not carried out,
the people will not die for them.
Now Qín issues orders and executes rewards and punishments,
and not attacking unless there is merit is how affairs are conducted.
People leave the embrace of their parents
having never seen an enemy in their lives,
yet upon hearing of war, they stomp their feet and bare their arms,
facing naked blades,
treading on glowing coals,
and dying before one another in succession.
Facing death and seeking life are not the same,
yet the people do so because they value courage.
One can defeat ten,
ten can defeat a hundred,
a hundred can defeat a thousand,
a thousand can defeat ten thousand,
and ten thousand can defeat the world.
Now as for Qín's terrain,
cutting the long to mend the short,
it is several thousand lǐ square,
with millions of famous soldiers.
Qín's orders, rewards, and punishments,
and its geographical advantages,
are unmatched in the world.
With this to confront the world,
the world is not enough to be annexed and possessed.
Thus it is known that Qín never fights without winning,
never attacks without taking,
and never faces an enemy without breaking them.
Opening thousands of lǐ of land
is indeed a great achievement.
However, the armor and weapons are worn out,
the soldiers and people are weary,
the stores are exhausted,
the fields are desolate,
and the granaries are empty.
The neighboring feudal lords do not submit,
and the title of Hegemon-King is not established.
This is for no other reason
than the strategic advisors not exhausting their loyalty.
Your servant dares to speak of the past.
Formerly, Qí broke Jīng to the south,
broke Sòng in the middle,
subdued Qín to the west,
broke Yàn to the north,
and commanded the rulers of Hán and Wèi in the middle.
Its land was vast and its army strong.
It won every battle and took every city,
commanding the world.
It possessed the Jǐhé, the Qīnghé, and the Zhuóhé
as boundaries,
and the Great Wall and Jùfáng
as barriers.
Qí
was a state of five battles;
failing in one battle, there was no more Qí.
Thus, looking at it from this perspective,
war is the life or death of a state of ten thousand chariots.
Furthermore, your servant has heard it said:
"Cut down the trunk and dig up the roots;
do not live as a neighbor to calamity,
and then calamity will not exist."
Qín fought with the people of Jīng,
greatly defeated Jīng,
attacked Yǐng,
and took Dòngtíng, Wǔdū, and Jiāngnán.
The King of Jīng fled in exile,
hiding in the east at Chén.
At that time,
had you followed Jīng with troops,
then Jīng could have been taken.
If Jīng were taken,
then its people would have been sufficient for plunder,
and its land would have been sufficient for profit.
To the east, you could have strengthened yourself against Qí and Yàn;
in the center, you could have dominated the Sānjìn.
Thus, with one stroke, the name of Hegemon-King could have been achieved,
and the feudal lords of the four neighbors could have been made to pay court.
But the planning ministers did not do this;
they led the army to retreat
and made peace with the people of Jīng.
Now the people of Jīng have reclaimed their lost state,
gathered their scattered people,
established the altars of the soil,
set up their ancestral temples,
and led the world westward to cause trouble for Qín.
This is certainly the first instance of missing the way of the Hegemon-King.
The world had a unified will
and camped their armies below Huà.
Your Majesty used deception to defeat them.
When the troops reached the outer walls of Liáng
and besieged Liáng for several weeks,
then Liáng could have been captured.
If Liáng were captured,
then Wèi could have been taken.
If Wèi were taken,
then the ambitions of Jīng and Zhào would have been cut off.
If the ambitions of Jīng and Zhào were cut off,
then Zhào would be in danger.
If Zhào were in danger, Jīng would be isolated.
To the east, you could have strengthened yourself against Qí and Yàn;
in the center, you could have dominated the Sānjìn.
Thus, with one stroke, the name of Hegemon-King could have been achieved,
and the feudal lords of the four neighbors could have been made to pay court.
But the planning ministers did not do this;
they led the army to retreat
and made peace with the House of Wèi.
This allowed the House of Wèi to reclaim its lost state,
gather its scattered people,
establish the altars of the soil,
and set up their ancestral temples.
This is certainly the second instance of missing the way of the Hegemon-King.
Previously, when Rànghóu governed Qín,
he used the troops of one state
but wished to achieve the merits of two states.
Therefore, the troops were exposed to the elements outside for their entire lives,
and the soldiers and people were exhausted and ill within.
The name of Hegemon-King was not achieved.
This is certainly the third instance of missing the way of the Hegemon-King.
The House of Zhào
is a state in the center,
where diverse people reside.
Its people are frivolous and difficult to use,
their orders are not well-regulated,
rewards and punishments are not trusted,
the terrain is inconvenient,
and those above cannot fully utilize the people's strength.
They truly have the form of a doomed state,
yet they do not worry for the common people,
but exhaust all their soldiers and people
to camp below Chángpíng
to contest Hán’s Shàngdǎng.
Your Majesty used deception to defeat them
and captured Wǔ'ān.
At that time,
those above and below in the House of Zhào were not close to each other,
and the noble and the base did not trust each other.
Thus, Hándān could not have been defended.
If Hándān were captured
and Héjiān secured,
and then you led the army away
to attack Xiūwǔ to the west,
crossed Yángcháng,
and made Dài and Shàngdǎng surrender.
The thirty-six counties of Dài
and the seventeen counties of Shàngdǎng,
without using a single suit of armor
or troubling a single citizen,
would all have been possessed by Qín.
Dài and Shàngdǎng
would have belonged to Qín without a fight,
Dōngyáng and Héwài would have instead returned to Qí without a fight,
and the area north of the Zhōnghūchí would have belonged to Yàn without a fight.
Thus, if Zhào were taken, Hán would surely perish;
if Hán perished, then Jīng and Wèi could not stand alone.
If Jīng and Wèi could not stand alone,
then with one stroke you would destroy Hán,
undermine Wèi,
coerce Jīng,
weaken Qí and Yàn to the east,
breach the mouth of Báimǎ,
and flood the House of Wèi.
With one stroke, the Sānjìn would perish,
and the Vertical Alliance members would be defeated.
Your Majesty would only have to fold your hands and wait,
and the world everywhere would follow and submit,
and the name of Hegemon-King could be achieved.
But the planning ministers did not do this;
they led the army to retreat
and made peace with the House of Zhào.
With Your Majesty's brilliance,
the strength of Qín's troops,
and the enterprise of a Hegemon-King,
a position of great respect was not obtained,
and instead you were deceived by a doomed state;
this is the clumsiness of the planning ministers.
Moreover, when Zhào should have perished but did not,
and Qín should have become Hegemon but did not,
the world certainly gauged Qín's planning ministers as the first failing.
Then you again exhausted all your troops to attack Hándān
and could not capture it;
you abandoned armor and weapons in anger,
trembled and retreated.
The world certainly gauged Qín's strength as the second failing.
The army then retreated
and combined at Lǐxià.
Your Majesty again combined the army to engage them in battle,
but you were not able to achieve a decisive victory,
and both sides were exhausted and retreated.
The world certainly gauged Qín's strength as the third failing.
Internally, they gauge our planning ministers;
externally, they have tested the limits of our military strength.
Viewing it from this,
for your servant to handle the world's Vertical Alliance,
how could it be difficult?
Internally, our armor and weapons are worn out,
the soldiers and people are ill,
stores and accumulations are exhausted,
the fields are overgrown,
and the granaries are empty.
Externally, the unified will of the world is very firm.
I hope Your Majesty will consider this.
Furthermore, your servant has heard:
be fearful and trembling,
and be more cautious day by day.
If one is cautious in their way,
the world can be possessed.
How do we know this is so?
Formerly, when Zhòu was the Son of Heaven,
he led a million armored troops of the world;
the left drank from the Qí Gǔ,
and the right drank from the Huán Shuǐ.
The Qí Shuǐ was exhausted and the Huán Shuǐ ceased to flow,
as he caused trouble for Zhōu Wǔ.
King Wǔ led three thousand soldiers in plain armor,
fought for one day,
broke the state of Zhòu,
captured him personally,
occupied his land,
and possessed his people,
and the world did not fail to be moved.
Zhì Bó led the masses of three states
to attack Zhào Xiāngzhǔ at Jìnyáng.
He diverted the water to flood it;
for three years,
the city was about to be captured.
Lord Xiāng scorched a tortoise shell
and counted the divining stalks to observe the omens
to see the benefits and harms,
and which state might surrender;
then he sent Zhāng Mèngtán.
Thereupon, he secretly crept out,
turned back the agreement of Zhì Bó,
obtained the masses of the two states,
and used them to attack the state of Zhì Bó,
captured him personally,
and thus achieved the merit of Xiāngzǐ.
Now Qín's territory, cutting the long to supplement the short,
is several thousand lǐ square,
with millions of renowned troops.
Qín's orders, rewards, and punishments,
and the advantages and disadvantages of its terrain,
are unsurpassed in the world.
Using this against the world,
the world can be gathered and possessed.
Your servant risks death in the hope of seeing Your Majesty
to speak of how to break the Vertical Alliance of the world,
take Zhào and destroy Hán,
make subjects of Jīng and Wèi,
and befriend Qí and Yàn,
in order to achieve the name of Hegemon-King
and the way of making the feudal lords of the four neighbors pay court.
"May the Dàwáng try listening to this proposal:
if with one action the alliance of the world is not broken,
Zhào is not captured,
Hán is not destroyed,
Jīng and Wèi do not submit as ministers,
Qí and Yàn do not become close allies,
the title of Bàwáng is not established,
and the Zhūhóu of the four neighbors do not pay court,
then execute your servant as a public example to the state,
as one who was disloyal in advising his lord."
Zhāng Yí wished to borrow Qín troops to save Wèi.
Zuǒ Chéng said to Gān Mào:
"You should not give them to him.
If Wèi does not return the Qín troops,
Zhāng Zǐ will not return to Qín.
If Wèi does return the Qín troops,
and Zhāng Zǐ achieves his ambitions in Wèi,
he will not dare to turn against Qín.
If Zhāng Zǐ does not leave Qín,
Zhāng Zǐ will surely hold you in high esteem."
Sīmǎ Cuò and Zhāng Yí debated before Qín Huì Wáng.
Sīmǎ Cuò wished to attack Shǔ,
but Zhāng Yí said:
"It is better to attack Hán."
The King said:
"I would like to hear your explanation."
He replied:
"Befriend Wèi and treat Chǔ well,
lead troops down to Sānchuān,
block the mouth of Huànyuán and Gōushì,
and occupy the road to Túnliú.
Wèi will be cut off from Nányáng,
Chǔ will approach Nánzhèng,
and Qín will attack Xīnchéng and Yíyáng,
to reach the outskirts of the Èr Zhōu states.
Punish the crimes of the Lord of Zhōu
and invade the lands of Chǔ and Wèi.
Zhōu will know it cannot be saved,
and the Jiǔ Dǐng and precious vessels will surely be surrendered.
By possessing the Jiǔ Dǐng,
taking hold of the maps and registers,
and controlling the Tiānzǐ to command the world,
no one in the world will dare not to obey.
This is the work of a King.
Now as for Shǔ,
it is a remote western state
and the leader of the Róng Dí.
To weary the troops and toil the masses is not enough to make a name,
and gaining its land is not enough to bring profit.
Your servant has heard:
'Those who compete for fame do so at court;
those who compete for profit do so at the market.'
Now Sānchuān and the House of Zhōu
are the market and court of the world,
yet Your Majesty does not compete there,
but instead competes with the Róng Dí;
this is far from the work of a King."
Sīmǎ Cuò said:
"It is not so.
Your servant has heard
that those who wish to enrich their state
must strive to broaden its territory;
those who wish to strengthen their military
must strive to enrich their people;
and those who wish to be Kings
must strive to broaden their virtue.
When these three resources are prepared,
kingship follows.
Now Your Majesty's land is small and your people are poor,
so your servant wishes to attend to what is easy.
As for Shǔ,
it is a remote western state
and the leader of the Róng Dí,
yet it has the chaos of Jié and Zhòu.
Using Qín to attack it
is like sending jackals and wolves to chase a flock of sheep.
Taking its territory
is enough to broaden the state;
obtaining its wealth
is enough to enrich the people.
Repairing the military will not harm the masses,
and they will already have submitted.
Thus, you can uproot a state
without the world considering it violent;
you can gain all the profit of the Xīhǎi
without the Zhūhóu considering it greedy.
In this way, with one action, both name and reality are gained,
and you also have the reputation of suppressing violence and rectifying chaos.
Now to attack Hán and kidnap the Tiānzǐ—
kidnapping the Tiānzǐ
is an evil reputation
and is not necessarily profitable;
moreover, it brings a reputation for unrighteousness,
and attacking what the world does not desire
is dangerous!
Permit me to state the reason:
Zhōu is the ancestral house of the world;
Qí is an ally of Hán and Zhōu.
When Zhōu knows it will lose the Jiǔ Dǐng
and Hán knows it will lose Sānchuān,
then the two states will surely combine their strength and plans
to rely on Qí and Zhào
and seek help from Chǔ and Wèi.
They will give the tripods to Chǔ
and land to Wèi,
which Your Majesty cannot prevent.
This is what your servant calls 'dangerous';
it is not as secure as attacking Shǔ."
Qín Huì Wáng said:
"Excellent! I will listen to you."
He finally raised troops to attack Shǔ,
captured it in ten months,
and thus pacified Shǔ.
The ruler of Shǔ changed his title to Marquis,
and Chén Zhuāng was made Prime Minister of Shǔ.
Once Shǔ was subordinated,
Qín became even stronger, wealthier, and more prosperous,
and looked down upon the Zhūhóu.
Zhāng Yí harbored ill will toward Chúlí Jí,
but treated him with honor and sent him to Chǔ.
He then had the Chǔ Wáng
request that he be made Prime Minister in Qín.
Zhāng Zǐ said to the King of Qín:
"The reason I honored Chúlí Jí and sent him
was to manage the state's diplomacy.
Now that he is in Chǔ,
the Chǔ Wáng has consequently requested that he be made Prime Minister in Qín.
I have heard his words, saying:
'Does the King wish to exhaust Zhāng Yí in Qín?
I request to help the King.'
The Chǔ Wáng believed this was so,
and therefore requested the chancellorship for him.
Now if Your Majesty indeed listens to this,
he will certainly serve the Chǔ Wáng with our state's affairs."
The King of Qín was greatly enraged,
and Chúlí Jí fled.
Zhāng Yí wished to give Hànzhōng to Chǔ and
requested of the King of Qín:
"Possessing Hànzhōng
is a burden. For those who plant trees but do not dwell there,
others will surely damage them;
if a family has unsuitable wealth,
it harms their foundation.
Hànzhōng borders Chǔ to the south and is beneficial to them;
it is a burden to our state."
Gān Mào said to the King:
"Do those with large territories
naturally have many worries?
If there is a change in the world's situation,
Your Majesty could cede Hànzhōng to make peace with Chǔ,
and Chǔ would surely abandon the world to join Your Majesty.
If Your Majesty gives Hànzhōng to Chǔ now,
then when there is a change in the world,
what will Your Majesty use to bargain with Chǔ?"
Chǔ attacked Wèi.
Zhāng Yí said to the King of Qín:
"It is better to aid Wèi to strengthen them.
If Wèi is victorious,
they will again obey Qín
and will surely cede the lands beyond the Xīhé;
if they are not victorious,
Wèi will be unable to defend itself,
and Your Majesty will surely take it."
The King followed Zhāng Yí's advice
and took ten thousand soldiers from Píshì
and one hundred chariots
to give to Wèi.
Xīshǒu defeated Chǔ Wēi Wáng,
and the Wèi troops were exhausted.
Fearing Qín,
they indeed offered the lands beyond the Xīhé.
Tián Shēn, on behalf of Chén Zhěn, said to Qín Huì Wáng:
"Your servant fears that Your Majesty will be like Guō Jūn.
Jìn Xiàn Gōng wished to attack Guō,
but he was wary that Zhōu Zhī Qiáo was there.
Xún Xī said:
'The Zhōu Shū says,
"Beautiful women break tongues."'
He then sent female musicians to him
to throw his government into chaos.
Zhōu Zhī Qiáo remonstrated but was not listened to,
and so he left.
Consequently, Jìn attacked Guō
and destroyed it.
He also wished to attack Yú,
but was wary that Gōng Zhī Qí was there.
Xún Xī said:
'The Zhōu Shū says,
"Beautiful men break the elderly."'
He then sent beautiful men to him
and taught them to make the ruler dislike Gōng Zhī Qí.
Gōng Zhī Qí remonstrated but was not listened to,
and so he fled."
Consequently, they attacked Yú,
and subsequently took it.
Now Qín considers itself kingly,
but the state that can harm a kingly state
is Chǔ.
Chǔ knows that Héng Jūn is skilled at military command,
and that command combined with the wisdom of Chén Zhěn is formidable,
therefore it made Zhāng Yí arrogant by means of the five states.
When he comes,
he will surely speak ill of these two men.
I hope the King will not listen to him."
Zhāng Yí indeed came to take his leave,
and consequently spoke against Chén Zhěn,
but the King was angry and did not listen.
Zhāng Yí again slandered Chén Zhěn to the King of Qín,
saying:
"Zhěn gallops between Chǔ and Qín;
now Chǔ does not show favor to Qín but shows favor to Zhěn,
and if so, then Zhěn is acting for himself and not for the state.
Moreover, Zhěn wishes to leave Qín and go to Chǔ;
why does the King not listen to this?"
The King said to Chén Zhěn:
"I have heard that you wish to leave Qín and go to Chǔ;
is this true?"
Chén Zhěn said:
"Yes."
The King said:
"The words of Zhāng Yí are indeed trustworthy."
He said:
"It is not only Zhāng Yí who knows this;
all the people on the road know it.
They say:
'Xiào Jǐ loved his parents,
and the whole world wanted him as a son;
Zǐ Xū was loyal to his ruler,
and the whole world wanted him as a minister.
Those whose servants and concubines are bought when sold in the local lanes
are good servants and concubines;
a divorced wife who remarries within her own village
is a good wife
If I were not loyal to my lord,
how would Chǔ consider Zhěn to be loyal?
If I am loyal yet still rejected,
and if I do not go to Chǔ,
where else should I go?"
The King of Qín said:
"Good."
Thus he indeed went there.
Chén Zhěn left Chǔ and went to Qín.
Zhāng Yí said to the King of Qín:
"Chén Zhěn is your Majesty's minister,
yet he constantly transmits the state's intelligence to Chǔ.
I cannot work with him;
I hope your Majesty will expel him.
If he goes to Chǔ again,
I hope your Majesty will kill him."
The King said:
"How would Zhěn dare to go to Chǔ?"
The King summoned Chén Zhěn and told him:
"I can listen to your words;
where do you wish to go?
I request to prepare a carriage for you."
He replied:
"Your servant wishes to go to Chǔ."
The King said:
"Zhāng Yí thought you would go to Chǔ,
and I myself know you are going to Chǔ.
If you do not go to Chǔ,
where else would you go!"
Zhěn said:
"When I leave,
I will surely go to Chǔ on purpose,
in order to follow the strategy of your Majesty and Zhāng Yí,
and to clarify whether I am going to Chǔ or not.
There was a man from Chǔ who had two wives.
Someone flirted with the elder one,
and she scolded him;
he flirted with the younger one,
and the younger one consented.
After a short while,
the man with two wives died.
A guest asked the flirtatious man:
'Will you take the elder one
or the younger one?'
'I will take the elder one.'
The guest said:
'The elder one scolded you,
while the younger one responded to you;
why do you take the elder one?'
He said:
'While she was in that other person's place,
I wanted her to consent to me.
Now that she is to be my wife,
I want her to scold others for my sake.'
Now, the King of Chǔ is an enlightened ruler,
and Zhāo Yáng is a worthy prime minister.
If I, Zhěn, as a minister,
constantly gave away state secrets to the King of Chǔ,
the King would certainly not keep me,
and Zhāo Yáng would not work with me.
By this, it is clear whether I am going to Chǔ or not."
Zhěn went out,
Zhāng Yí came in,
and asked the King:
"Where did Chén Zhěn actually go?"
The King said:
"Zhěn is a debater of the world.
He looked intently at me and said:
'Zhěn must go to Chǔ.'
I consequently could do nothing about it.
I then asked:
'If you must go to Chǔ,
then the words of Zhāng Yí are indeed trustworthy!'
Zhěn said:
'It is not only the words of Zhāng Yí;
all the people on the road know it.
In the past, Zǐ Xū was loyal to his ruler,
and the whole world wanted him as a minister;
Xiào Jǐ loved his parents,
and the whole world wanted him as a son.
Therefore, those whose servants and concubines are bought without leaving the neighborhood
are good servants and concubines;
a divorced wife who marries in the neighborhood
is a good wife.
If I were not loyal to your Majesty,
what would Chǔ do with me?
If my loyalty is still met with rejection,
and if I, Zhěn, do not go to Chǔ,
where else should I go?'"
The King thought this was correct
and consequently treated him well.
Qí assisted Chǔ in attacking Qín
and took Qǔwò.
After that,
Qín wished to attack Qí,
but the relations between Qí and Chǔ were good.
Huì Wáng was troubled by this
and said to Zhāng Yí:
"I wish to attack Qí,
but Qí and Chǔ are currently friendly;
consider this for me,
what can be done?"
Zhāng Yí said:
"May the King prepare a carriage
together with gifts for your servant;
I beg to go and try."
Zhāng Yí went south to see the King of Chǔ
and said:
"Of those whom the King of my humble state likes the most,
none is greater than your Majesty;
among those whom I, Zhāng Yí, most desire to serve as a minister,
also none is greater than your Majesty.
Of those whom the King of my humble state hates the most,
none comes before the King of Qí;
among those whom I, Zhāng Yí, hate the most,
also none is greater than the King of Qí.
Now the crimes of the King of Qí
against the King of my humble state are very serious;
my humble state wishes to attack him,
but your great state is on friendly terms with him,
and thus the King of my humble state cannot serve your commands,
and I, Zhāng Yí, cannot be your minister.
If your Majesty could close the borders and break off relations with Qí,
I request to have the King of Qín offer the lands of Shāngyú,
six hundred square lǐ.
If this is done,
Qí will surely be weakened,
and once Qí is weak, it will surely be at your Majesty's service.
Thus, you will weaken Qí to the north,
create an obligation from Qín to the west,
and personally gain the lands of Shāngyú as a profit;
then this one plan will bring three benefits at once."
The King of Chǔ was very pleased
and announced it to the court,
saying:
"I have obtained the lands of Shāngyú, six hundred square lǐ."
All the ministers who heard and saw this offered their congratulations.
Chén Zhěn saw him later
and alone did not offer congratulations.
The King of Chǔ said:
"I have not troubled a single soldier,
nor injured a single person,
yet I have obtained six hundred lǐ of the Shāngyú lands;
I consider myself wise!
The various officials all congratulate me,
yet you alone do not,
why is that?"
Chén Zhěn replied:
"I see that the lands of Shāngyú cannot be obtained,
and trouble will surely arrive,
therefore I do not dare to offer reckless congratulations."
The King said:
"Why?"
He replied:
"The reason Qín regards Your Majesty with importance
is that Your Majesty has Qí as an ally.
Now, the land has not yet been obtained,
and yet ties with Qí are severed first;
this leaves Chǔ isolated.
Why should Qín value an isolated state?
Moreover, to have Qín first give up the land and then sever ties with Qí—the Qín planners would surely not do it.
If you sever ties with Qí first and demand the land afterward,
you will certainly be deceived by Zhāng Yí.
If you are deceived by Zhāng Yí,
Your Majesty will certainly regret it.
This will create trouble with Qín in the west
and sever the alliance with Qí in the north;
then the armies of both states will surely arrive."
The King of Chǔ would not listen and
said:
"My affairs are going well!
You should just shut your mouth and say no more;
wait for my success."
The King of Chǔ sent someone to break ties with Qí;
before the messenger had even returned,
he sent another to break ties again emphatically.
Zhāng Yí returned,
and Qín sent an envoy to Qí;
the alliance between Qí and Qín was secretly joined.
Chǔ then sent a general to receive the land from Qín.
When Zhāng Yí arrived,
he claimed illness and did not attend court.
The King of Chǔ said:
"Does Master Zhāng think that I have not truly broken ties with Qí?"
He then sent a brave man to go and insult the King of Qí.
Knowing that Chǔ had severed ties with Qí,
Zhāng Yí came out to see the envoy and said:
"From such-and-such a point to such-and-such a point,
the width and length are six lǐ."
The envoy said:
"I heard it was six hundred lǐ;
I have not heard of six lǐ."
Zhāng Yí said:
"I am but a person of lowly status;
how could I have six hundred lǐ?"
The envoy returned and reported to the King of Chǔ.
The King of Chǔ was greatly enraged
and wanted to raise an army to attack Qín.
Chén Zhěn said:
"May I speak now?"
The King said:
"You may."
Chén Zhěn said:
"Attacking Qín is not a good plan.
It would be better for Your Majesty to bribe them with a famous city,
and join them in attacking Qí.
In this way, what I lose to Qín, I will compensate for by taking from Qí.
Chǔ will not suffer a total loss.
Now that Your Majesty has already broken ties with Qí
and is being deceived by Qín,
this will cause the union of Qí and Qín;
we will certainly suffer great injury."
The King of Chǔ would not listen
and ultimately raised troops to attack Qín.
Qín joined with Qí,
and the Hán Shì followed them.
The Chǔ army was soundly defeated at Dùlíng.
Therefore, it was not that Chǔ's territory or people were weakened,
but they were barely able to save themselves from destruction
because the plan failed with Chén Zhěn
and they wrongly listened to Zhāng Yí.
After Chǔ broke with Qí,
Qí raised an army to attack Chǔ.
Chén Zhěn said to the King of Chǔ:
"It would be better for Your Majesty to cede land in the east to reconcile with Qí
and negotiate peace in the west with Qín."
The King of Chǔ sent Chén Zhěn to Qín.
The King of Qín said to Chén Zhěn:
"You are a man of Qín,
and I have an old friendship with you.
I am not talented
and cannot manage the affairs of state personally;
therefore, you left me to serve the King of Chǔ.
Now Qí and Chǔ are attacking each other;
some say it is advantageous to save them,
while others say it is not.
Can you not loyally plan for your own master
and use what is left for me?"
Chén Zhěn said:
"Has Your Majesty not heard of the man of Wú who stayed in Chǔ?
The King of Chǔ loved him dearly.
When he fell ill,
the king sent someone to ask him,
saying:
'Are you truly ill?
Or is it that you are homesick?'
Those close to him said:
'We do not know if he is homesick or not,
but if he is truly homesick, he will surely sing in the Wú dialect.'
Now I shall sing in the Wú dialect for Your Majesty.
Has Your Majesty not heard the words of Guǎn Yǔ?
There were two tigers
fighting over a person.
Guǎn Zhuāngzǐ was about to stab them,
but Guǎn Yǔ stopped him, saying:
'Tigers
are fierce beasts;
a human
is sweet bait.
Now that two tigers are fighting over a person,
the smaller one will surely die
and the larger one will surely be wounded.
If you wait for the tigers to be wounded before stabbing them,
then in one move you will secure both tigers.
Without the effort of stabbing one tiger,
you will have the fame of having stabbed two.'
Qí and Chǔ are fighting now;
in a fight, there must be a defeat.
When they are defeated,
Your Majesty can raise troops to save them.
You will have the benefit of saving Qí
without the harm of attacking Chǔ.
Regarding whose plans to listen to and knowing success from failure,
only Your Majesty can decide.
Planning
is the root of affairs;
listening
is the turning point of survival and destruction.
When planning fails and listening is erroneous,
those who can keep their state are few.
Therefore it is said:
'When plans are coherent,
it is hard to go wrong;
when listening does not lose track of the whole,
it is hard to be deluded.'"
When Qín Hùiwén Wáng died,
Gōngsūn Yǎn wanted to drive Zhāng Yí into a corner.
Lǐ Chóu said to Gōngsūn Yǎn:
"It would be better to summon Gān Mào from Wèi,
summon Gōngsūn Xiǎn from Hán,
and bring Chūlǐ Zǐ out from within the state.
These three men
are all enemies of Zhāng Yí.
If you employ them,
then the feudal lords will surely see that Zhāng Yí no longer has the support of Qín!"
When the Lord of Yìqú went to Wèi,
Gōngsūn Yǎn said to the Lord of Yìqú:
"The way is far,
and I may not be able to visit you again;
please allow me to state the truth of the situation."
The Lord of Yìqú said:
"I wish to hear it."
He replied:
"If the Middle Kingdom has no business with Qín,
then Qín will burn and plunder your state;
if the Middle Kingdom has business with Qín,
