and makes it impossible to supply enough provisions and transport.
This is a path toward self-destruction while sitting idle;
it is not what I, Dān,
would do.
I have heard that
the armies of the Emperors and Kings
used no more than thirty thousand men,
and yet the whole world submitted.
Now the General must rely on masses of one hundred thousand or two hundred thousand before acting;
this is what I, Dān, find unconvincing.”
Mǎfú said:
“You not only fail to understand military matters,
but you also do not grasp the conditions of the times.
Take a sword of Wú or Gàn:
if tested on flesh, it can sever cows and horses;
if tested on metal, it can cut through basins and ewers.
But if you lean it against a pillar and strike it,
it will snap into three pieces;
if you place it on a stone and strike it,
it will shatter into a hundred.
Now, using thirty thousand troops to meet the armies of a powerful state
is like leaning a sword against a pillar or striking a stone.
Furthermore, even with the material of a Wú or Gàn sword,
without the thickness of a spine,
the point would not penetrate;
without the thinness of the edge, the blade would not cut.
Even if it has both,
if it lacks the convenience of a guard, pommel, and grip,
and you grasp the blade itself to thrust,
your own hand would be severed before it even entered.
If you do not have one or two hundred thousand troops
to serve as these guards, pommels, and grips,
but instead traverse the world with only thirty thousand,
how can you succeed?
Furthermore, in ancient times,
within the four seas,
the land was divided into ten thousand states.
A city, though large, did not exceed three hundred *zhàng*;
the people, though numerous,
did not exceed three thousand families.
With a concentrated force of thirty thousand men,
how could it be difficult to resist such states?
Now, taking what were once ten thousand states,
they have been divided into the seven Warring States,
each able to raise several hundred thousand soldiers
for campaigns that last a long time,
even several years—
just like your own state of Qí.
Qí used two hundred thousand men to attack Jīng
and only stopped after five years.
Zhào used two hundred thousand men to attack Zhōngshān
and only returned after five years.
Nowadays,
when Qí and Hán face each other
and a state is besieged and attacked,
could anyone dare to say,
‘I will use thirty thousand men to rescue them’?”
"Now, when thousand-fathom walls
and cities of ten thousand households face each other,
and you seek with a host of thirty thousand
to besiege a thousand-fathom wall,
without even capturing a single corner
while being insufficient for field battles,
where do you intend to go with this?"
Dūpíng Jūn sighed deeply and said,
"[Tián] Dān was right!"
Zhào sent Jī Hǎo to Qín
to request making Wèi Rǎn the chancellor.
Sòng Tū said to Jī Hǎo,
"If Qín does not listen,
Lóu Huǎn will surely resent you.
It would be better to secretly say to Lóu Huǎn:
'Please do not press the King of Qín.'
When the King of Qín sees that Zhào is not pressing for the chancellorship of Wèi Rǎn,
and moreover does not listen to your words,
even if this matter is not successful,
Wèi Rǎn will surely be grateful to you."
Qí defeated Yàn,
and Zhào wished to preserve it.
Yuè Yì said to the King of Zhào,
"If we attack Qí now without a treaty,
Qí will surely treat Zhào as an enemy.
It would be better to request to exchange Hédōng for the lands of Yàn with Qí.
Zhào will have Héběi,
and Qí will have Hédōng;
then Yàn and Zhào will surely not fight.
This will make the two countries close.
By strengthening Qí with the lands of Hédōng,
and having Yàn and Zhào assist it,
the world will detest it,
and everyone will surely serve Your Majesty to attack Qí.
This is using the whole world to break Qí."
The King said,
"Excellent."
He then exchanged Hédōng with Qí.
Chǔ and Wèi detested this,
and ordered Nào Huá and Huì Shī to go to Zhào
to request attacking Qí and preserving Yàn.
Qín attacked Zhào,
and Lìn, Líshí, and Qí were taken.
Zhào sent Gōngzǐ Wú as a hostage to Qín,
and requested to hand over the cities of Jiāo, Lí, and Niúhú
in exchange for Lìn,
Líshí, and Qí to be returned to Zhào.
Zhào betrayed Qín
and did not give up Jiāo, Lí, and Niúhú.
The King of Qín was angry
and ordered Gōngzǐ Zēng to request the land.
The King of Zhào then ordered Zhèng Zhū to reply, saying:
"Indeed, the lands of Lìn,
Líshí, and Qí
are vast and far from Zhào,
but close to your Great State.
It was through the brilliance of the former kings and the efforts of former ministers
that we were able to possess them.
Now I am not equal to them,
and I cannot even care for the state altars;
how could I take care of Lìn,
Líshí, and Qí?
I have a disobedient official
who actually caused this matter,
and it is not something I dared to know."
In the end, he double-crossed Qín.
The King of Qín was greatly enraged
and ordered Wèi Húyì to attack Zhào,
besieging Èyǔ.
Zhào Shē led troops to rescue it.
Wèi ordered Gōngzǐ Jiù with elite troops to reside in Ānyì
to pressure Qín.
Qín was defeated at Èyǔ,
and in return attacked Wèi’s Jī.
Lián Pó rescued Jī
and greatly defeated the Qín army.
Fù Dīng wished to align Zhào with Qí and Wèi,
while Lóu Huǎn wished to align Zhào with Qín and Chǔ.
Fù Dīng feared that the Zhǔfù would listen to Lóu Huǎn and align with Qín and Chǔ.
Sīmǎ Qiǎn spoke on behalf of Fù Dīng to the Zhǔfù, saying:
"It would be better to go along with Qí.
If we do not now go along with Qí to attack Qín,
Qín and Chǔ will surely unite and attack Hán and Wèi.
When Hán and Wèi report the emergency to Qí,
if Qí does not wish to attack Qín,
it will surely use Zhào as an excuse,
then the one attacking Qín will be Zhào,
and Hán and Wèi will surely resent Zhào.
If the troops of Qí do not move west,
Hán will surely listen to Qín and turn against Qí.
Turning against Qí to become close to Qín,
their troops will surely be turned against Zhào.
Now, if we go along and Qí does not move west,
Hán and Wèi will surely break with Qí;
once they break with Qí, they will all serve us.
Moreover, if I go along with Qí,
Qí will have no choice but to go west.
In the past,
Lóu Huǎn stayed in Wèi for three months
but could not break the relations between Qí and Wèi.
Now if we go along and Qí and Wèi indeed go west,
this will exhaust Qí and weary Qín,
and Zhào will surely become a preeminent state in the world."
The Zhǔfù said,
"If I attack Qín with the three states,
we will all be weary."
[Sīmǎ Qiǎn] said,
"Not so.
We can make an agreement with the three states and tell Qín
that it is because we have not yet settled matters with Zhōngshān.
If the three states are determined to attack Qín,
they will surely listen to us
and wish to make peace with us.
If Zhōngshān listens to it,
then Your Majesty will take territory by using the wealth of Zhōngshān.
If Zhōngshān does not listen,
the three states will surely cut them off,
and thus Zhōngshān will be isolated.
Even if the three states cannot make peace with us, just sending out a few troops will be fine.
I will divide the troops to isolate and make sport of Zhōngshān;
Zhōngshān will surely perish.
Once we have destroyed Zhōngshān,
we can then use the remaining troops to join the three states in attacking Qín.
This is to take territory from both Qín and Zhōngshān in one stroke."
Wèi, because of Fù Dīng, was about to align with Qín.
Zhào was afraid
and requested to present land to Wèi and listen to Xuē Gōng.
Jiào Zǐkài said to Lǐ Duì,
"Zhào fears the horizontal alliance,
so it wishes to present land to Wèi and listen to Xuē Gōng.
You would be better off having the Zhǔfù use land to support Zhōu Zuì
and request to make him the chancellor of Wèi.
Zhōu Zuì is one who has shamed Qín before the world.
If he is now the chancellor of Wèi,
Wèi and Qín will surely become estranged.
Although Qí and Wèi are strong,
without Qín they cannot harm Zhào.
If the King of Wèi listens, it shows he treats Qí lightly. Even if Qín and Wèi are strong, without Qí they cannot get Zhào. This is beneficial for Zhào and convenient for Zhōu Zuì."
Wèi sent someone through Píngyuán Jūn to request a vertical alliance with Zhào.
Three times it was mentioned,
but the King of Zhào did not listen.
Upon going out, he met Yú Qīng and said,
"When you enter, you must speak of the alliance."
Yú Qīng entered,
and the King said,
"Just now, Píngyuán Jūn requested an alliance for Wèi,
but I did not listen.
What is your opinion on this?"
Yú Qīng said, "Wèi is mistaken."
The King said,
"So it is,
which is why I did not listen."
Yú Qīng said, "Your Majesty is also mistaken."
The King said,
"Why?"
He said, "Whenever the strong and the weak take action,
the strong receive the benefit,
and the weak receive the harm.
Now Wèi seeks an alliance,
but Your Majesty does not listen;
this is Wèi seeking harm
and Your Majesty declining benefit.
Therefore I said Wèi is mistaken,
and Your Majesty is also mistaken."
Píngyuán Jūn asked Féng Jì,
"I wish to go on a northern expedition to Shàngdǎng
and send troops to attack Yàn;
what do you think?"
Féng Jì replied, "It cannot be done.
When the Qín general, Wǔ'ān Jūn Gōngsūn Qǐ, took advantage of the prestige of seven victories
and fought with the son of Mǎfú below Chángpíng,
he greatly defeated the Zhào army.
He then used his remaining troops
to besiege the city of Hándān.
Zhào used the remnants of the defeat
to gather the broken army for a weary defense,
and while Qín was exhausted below Hándān,
Zhào held firm and could not be taken,
because attacking is difficult and defending is easy.
Now Zhào does not have the prestige of seven victories,
and Yàn does not have the disaster of Chángpíng.
Now the disaster of the seven defeats has not yet been recovered from,
yet you wish to use an exhausted Zhào to attack a strong Yàn.
This is to make the weak Zhào the attacker of a strong state,
and to make the strong Yàn the defender against a weak Zhào.
While the strong Qín rests its troops and waits for Zhào's exhaustion—
this was the reason the strong Wú perished
and the weak Yuè became hegemon.
Therefore I do not see that Yàn can be attacked."
Píngyuán Jūn said,
"Excellent!"
Píngyuán Jūn said to Píngyáng Jūn:
"Gōngzǐ Móu was traveling in Qín,
and was about to go east.
He went to take leave of Yìng Hóu.
Yìng Hóu said: 'You are about to depart,
do you have no teaching for me?'
He said:
'Even if your lordship had not commanded me to speak,
I would have offered something to you anyway.
Now, high rank does not make an appointment with wealth,
yet wealth arrives;
wealth does not make an appointment with fine grain and meat,
yet fine grain and meat arrive;
fine grain and meat do not make an appointment with arrogance and extravagance,
yet arrogance and extravagance arrive;
arrogance and extravagance do not make an appointment with death and ruin,
yet death and ruin arrive.
Before past generations,
there have been many who fell because of this.'
Yìng Hóu said:
'What you have taught me is profound indeed.'
I happened to hear this,
and I have not forgotten it in my heart.
I hope that you will not forget it either."
Píngyáng Jūn said: "I respectfully agree."
Qín attacked Zhào at Chángpíng,
decisively defeated them,
and then withdrew its troops and returned.
Consequently, they sent someone to demand six cities from Zhào in exchange for a peace settlement.
Zhào's plan was not yet settled.
Lóu Huǎn had recently come from Qín,
and Zhào Wáng discussed the plan with Lóu Huǎn, saying:
"What would happen if we give the cities to Qín?
And what would happen if we do not?"
Lóu Huǎn declined, saying:
"This is not something a subject like me can know."
The King said: "Even so,
try to speak your private thoughts."
Lóu Huǎn said:
"Have you also heard about the mother of Gōngfǔ Wénbó?
Gōngfǔ Wénbó served as an official in Lǔ and died of illness.
Sixteen of his women committed suicide in their chambers for him.
When his mother heard of this,
she refused to weep.
Her steward said:
'Is there a case of a son dying and the mother not weeping?'
The mother said: 'Kǒngzǐ
was a worthy man,
yet when he was expelled from Lǔ,
this son did not follow him.
Now that he is dead,
there are sixteen women who died for him.
If he was like this,
does it not mean he was cold toward his elders
but deep in his affections for women?'
Therefore, from the mother's words,
she is considered a worthy mother;
but from the women's words,
she would surely not escape being called a jealous woman.
Thus, although the words are the same,
when the speakers are different,
then the human heart's perception changes.
Now I have recently come from Qín,
so if I say 'do not give,'
then it would not be a wise plan;
if I say 'give them,'
then I fear Your Majesty will think I am acting on behalf of Qín.
Therefore, I did not dare to answer.
If I were allowed to plan for Your Majesty,
it would be better to give them."
The King said: "Agreed."
Yú Qīng heard of this,
entered to see the King,
and the King told him Lóu Huǎn's words.
Yú Qīng said:
"This is a deceptive argument."
After Qín lifted the siege of Hándān,
Zhào Wáng went to pay court to Qín,
and sent Zhào Hǎo to negotiate with Qín,
to cede six counties for peace.
The King said: "What do you mean?"
Yú Qīng said: "When Qín attacked Zhào,
did they return because they were exhausted?
Or does Your Majesty think that their strength was still able to advance,
but they loved Your Majesty and thus did not attack?"
The King said: "When Qín attacked us,
they spared no effort;
they must have returned because they were exhausted."
Yú Qīng said:
"Qín used its strength to attack what it could not take
and returned exhausted.
If Your Majesty then provides them with what their strength could not take,
this is helping Qín to attack yourself.
Next year, when Qín attacks Your Majesty again,
Your Majesty will have no means of salvation."
The King then told Yú Qīng's words to Lóu Huǎn.
Lóu Huǎn said:
"Can Yú Qīng fully know the limits of Qín's strength?
If we truly knew that Qín's strength would not reach us,
then even a pellet-sized piece of land
we still should not give.
But if Qín comes to attack Your Majesty again next year,
will you not have to cede territory from the interior to make peace?"
The King said: "If I truly listen to you and cede territory,
can you guarantee that Qín will not attack us again next year?"
Lóu Huǎn replied:
"This is not something I dare to guarantee.
In the past, when the Sān Jìn states associated with Qín,
they were friendly with one another.
Now Qín has let Hán and Wèi alone and attacks only Your Majesty;
the way Your Majesty serves Qín must not be as good as Hán and Wèi.
Now I am resolving for Your Majesty the attack that stems from neglecting kinship,
opening the passes and establishing communication,
and aligning your relations with Hán and Wèi.
When next year comes and Your Majesty alone does not obtain terms from Qín,
the way Your Majesty serves Qín
will surely be behind Hán and Wèi.
This is not something I dare to guarantee."
The King told Lóu Huǎn's words to Yú Qīng.
Yú Qīng said:
"Lóu Huǎn says if we do not make peace, and next year Qín attacks Your Majesty again,
will we not have to further cede the interior to make peace.
Now if we do make peace,
Lóu Huǎn still cannot guarantee that Qín will not attack again.
Although we cede territory, what is the benefit?
If they attack again next year,
we would again be ceding what their strength could not take to make peace;
this is the path to self-exhaustion.
It is better not to make peace.
Although Qín is good at attacking,
they could not take the six cities;
although Zhào was unable to defend,
it did not come to the point of losing the six cities.
When Qín returned exhausted,
its troops were surely weary.
If I use five cities to recruit the world to attack the weary Qín,
then although I lose them to the world,
I would obtain compensation from Qín.
Our state values benefit;
how does this compare to sitting still and ceding territory,
weakening ourselves to strengthen Qín?
Now Lóu Huǎn says:
'The reason Qín is friendly with Hán and Wèi but attacks Zhào
must be that Your Majesty's service to Qín is not as good as Hán and Wèi.'
This is making Your Majesty serve Qín with six cities every year;
thus we will sit until our land is exhausted.
Next year, if Qín again seeks ceded land,
will Your Majesty give it to them?
If you do not give it,
then you abandon the previous high price paid and provoke a disaster from Qín;
if you do give it, then you will have no land left to provide.
As the saying goes: 'The strong are good at attacking,
while the weak are unable to defend themselves.'
Now if we sit and listen to Qín,
Qín's troops will not be exhausted yet they will gain much land;
this is strengthening Qín and weakening Zhào.
By adding to an ever-stronger Qín
while ceding territory from an ever-weaker Zhào,
their plan will certainly not stop.
Furthermore, Qín
is a state of tigers and wolves;
it has no heart for ritual or righteousness.
Its demands are endless,
but Your Majesty's land is finite.
To use finite land
to supply endless demands,
the situation will surely lead to there being no Zhào left.
Therefore I say:
this is a deceptive argument.
Your Majesty must not give it."
The King said: "Agreed."
Lóu Huǎn heard of this,
entered to see the King,
and the King again told him Yú Qīng's words.
Lóu Huǎn said: "It is not so.
Yú Qīng has grasped one point
but does not yet know the second.
Now, when Qín and Zhào are in conflict,
the whole world is pleased. Why?
They say,
'I will take advantage of the strong and prey upon the weak.'
Now that Zhào's troops are hard-pressed by Qín,
those in the world who congratulate the combatants
will surely all be on Qín's side.
Therefore, it is better to quickly cede territory and seek peace
to cast doubt among the world
and soothe Qín's heart.
Otherwise,
the world will take advantage of Qín's anger
and the exhaustion of both Qín and Zhào to carve us up like a melon.
Zhào will then perish; what then of your plans against Qín?
Your Majesty should decide based on this
and do not deliberate further."
Yú Qīng heard of this,
and again entered to see the King, saying:
“It is dangerous,
what Lóu Zǐ is doing for Qín!
Now, Zhào’s troops are hard-pressed by Qín,
and if you also cede land for peace,
this will further increase the world’s suspicions;
how would that satisfy the heart of Qín?
Does this not also greatly demonstrate weakness to the world?
Furthermore, when I said not to give it,
it was not simply for the sake of not giving.
Qín demands six cities from Your Majesty;
Your Majesty should bribe Qí with five cities.
Qí is a bitter enemy of Qín;
if they receive Your Majesty’s five cities,
they will combine forces and attack Qín in the west.
Qí’s compliance with Your Majesty
will not even wait for your speech to conclude.
Thus, what Your Majesty loses to Qí, you will regain from Qín;
in one move, you will establish friendship with three states
and reverse your situation relative to Qín.”
The King of Zhào said, “Excellent.”
He then dispatched Yú Qīng east to see the King of Qí
to plot against Qín with him.
Before Yú Qīng had returned,
the envoys of Qín were already in Zhào.
Lóu Huǎn heard of this
and fled.
Qín attacked Zhào;
Píngyuán Jūn sent someone to request aid from Wèi.
Xìnlíng Jūn dispatched troops to the walls of Hándān,
and the Qín troops withdrew.
Yú Qīng requested an increase of land for Píngyuán Jūn,
saying to the King of Zhào:
“Now, without a single soldier fighting,
or a single halberd being blunted,
to have resolved the crisis of two states
was the effort of Píngyuán Jūn.
To use someone’s effort
yet forget their merit
is not permissible.”
The King of Zhào said, “Excellent.”
He intended to increase his land.
Gōngsūn Lóng heard of this,
and saw Píngyuán Jūn, saying:
“Your Lordship has no merit of destroying armies or killing generals,
yet you were enfeoffed with Dōngwǔ Chéng.
Most of the heroic and outstanding men of the state of Zhào
rank above your lordship,
yet your lordship serves as Chancellor only because of your kinship.
Your lordship accepted the fief of Dōngwǔ Chéng without declining despite having no merit,
and wore the Chancellor’s seal of Zhào without refusing despite a lack of ability.
Now, having once resolved a national crisis,
you wish to seek more land;
this would be a relative receiving enfeoffment
while the people of the state calculate merit.
In planning for your lordship,
it would be better not to accept it.”
Píngyuán Jūn said, “I respectfully receive your instruction.”
He then did not accept the enfeoffment.
Qín and Zhào fought at Chángpíng;
Zhào was not victorious
and lost a commandant.
The King of Zhào summoned Lóu Chāng and Yú Qīng and said:
“The army is not victorious in battle,
and a commandant has died.
I shall order the troops to roll up their armor and rush them; what do you think?”
Lóu Chāng said, “It is of no use;
it is better to send a high envoy to seek peace.”
Yú Qīng said, “Now, those who speak of peace
think that without peace the army will surely be destroyed,
but the power to grant peace lies with Qín.
Furthermore, in Your Majesty’s estimation of Qín,
does it wish to destroy Your Majesty’s army?
Or does it not?”
The King said, “Qín has spared no effort;
it surely intends to destroy the Zhào army.”
Yú Qīng said, “If Your Majesty will just listen to me,
send envoys with precious treasures to win over Chǔ and Wèi.
When Chǔ and Wèi desire Your Majesty’s treasures,
they will surely admit our envoys.
Once Zhào’s envoys enter Chǔ and Wèi,
Qín will surely suspect a world-wide alliance
and will surely be afraid.
In this way,
peace can then be sought.”
The King of Zhào did not listen;
he sought peace through Píngyáng Jūn,
and dispatched Zhèng Zhū to enter Qín.
Qín admitted him.
The King of Zhào summoned Yú Qīng and said:
“I sent Píngyáng Jūn to seek peace with Qín,
and Qín has already admitted Zhèng Zhū;
what do you think of this?”
Yú Qīng said:
“Your Majesty will surely not obtain peace,
and the army will surely be destroyed;
those who congratulate the victor are all in Qín.
Zhèng Zhū
is a nobleman of Zhào,
and when he enters Qín,
the King of Qín and the Marquis of Yìng will surely treat him with great honor to show the world.
When Chǔ and Wèi believe that Zhào is making peace,
they will surely not rescue Your Majesty.
When Qín knows the world will not rescue Your Majesty,
then peace cannot be achieved.”
Zhào ultimately did not obtain peace,
and the army was indeed greatly defeated.
The King entered Qín,
and Qín detained the King of Zhào before granting him peace.
Qín besieged Hándān of Zhào.
Wèi Ānlí Wáng sent General Jìn Bǐ to rescue Zhào.
Fearing Qín, he stopped at Dàngyīn
and did not advance.
The King of Wèi sent the guest general Xīnyuán Yǎn to enter Hándān secretly
and, through Píngyuán Jūn, said to the King of Zhào:
“The reason Qín is so urgently besieging Zhào
is that previously it vied for power with Qí Mǐn Wáng to be Emperor,
but then relinquished the title because of Qí.
Now Qí Mǐn Wáng has become even weaker.
At present, only Qín dominates the world;
this is not necessarily because it covets Hándān,
its intention is to seek to be Emperor.
If Zhào were truly to send an envoy to honor Qín Zhāo Wáng as Emperor,
Qín would surely be pleased
and withdraw its troops and depart.”
Píngyuán Jūn hesitated and had not yet made a decision.
At this time, Lǔ Zhònglián happened to be traveling in Zhào,
and it coincided with Qín’s siege of Zhào.
Hearing that Wèi intended to have Zhào honor Qín as Emperor,
he then saw Píngyuán Jūn and said:
“How are matters going?”
Píngyuán Jūn said, “How can Shèng dare to speak of matters?
A force of a million was broken abroad,
and now Hándān is besieged from within and we cannot drive them away.
The King of Wèi sent General Xīnyuán Yǎn to command Zhào to acknowledge Qín as Emperor.
Now that man is here;
how can Shèng dare to speak of matters?”
Lǔ Lián said, “At first I considered your lordship to be a worthy scion of the world,
but only now do I know your lordship is not a worthy scion of the world.
Where is the guest from Liáng, Xīnyuán Yǎn?
I ask to rebuke him for your lordship and send him back.”
Píngyuán Jūn said:
“Shèng asks to summon him and present him to you, Sir.”
Píngyuán Jūn then saw Xīnyuán Yǎn and said:
“In the eastern lands there is a Master Lǔ Lián,
that man is here;
Shèng asks to introduce him
and present him to the General.”
Xīnyuán Yǎn said:
“I have heard of Master Lǔ Lián;
he is a noble gentleman of the state of Qí.
I, Yǎn, am a minister; I have duties in my mission.
I do not wish to see Master Lǔ Lián.”
Píngyuán Jūn said:
“Shèng has already revealed your presence.”
Xīnyuán Yǎn consented.
Lǔ Lián saw Xīnyuán Yǎn but said nothing.
Xīnyuán Yǎn said:
“I see those who dwell within this besieged city
are all those who have requests of Píngyuán Jūn.
Now I see your noble appearance, Sir;
you are not one who has requests of Píngyuán Jūn.
Why have you stayed long within this besieged city and not departed?”
Lǔ Lián said:
“The world thinks that Bào Jiāo died because he lacked composure;
they are all wrong.
If they let the masses be ignorant,
then they care only for themselves.
That state of Qín
is a state that abandons ritual and righteousness and prizes the merit of taking heads.
It uses its scholars with power
and treats its people as slaves.
If they should recklessly become Emperor
and consequently establish their rule over the world,
then I, Lián, would cast myself into the Eastern Sea and die.
I cannot bear to be its subject!
The reason I see the General
is that I wish to help Zhào.”
Xīnyuán Yǎn said:
“How will you help them, Sir?”
Lǔ Lián said:
“I shall have Liáng and Yàn help them.
Qí and Chǔ are already helping them.”
Xīnyuán Yǎn said:
“As for Yàn, I accept your word.
But as for Liáng,
I am a man of Liáng;
how can you, Sir, make Liáng help them?”
Lǔ Lián said:
"It is because Liáng has not yet seen the harm of Qín claiming the title of Emperor.
If Liáng were to see the harm of Qín claiming the title of Emperor,
then they would surely assist Zhào."
Xīnyuán Yǎn said:
"What would the harm of Qín claiming the title of Emperor be like?"
Lǔ Zhònglián said:
"In the past, King Wēi of Qí once practiced benevolence and righteousness
and led the feudal lords of the world to pay homage to Zhōu.
Zhōu was poor and weak,
and none of the feudal lords paid homage,
but Qí alone paid homage to them.
After more than a year passed,
King Liè of Zhōu passed away,
and the feudal lords all came to offer condolences,
but Qí arrived late.
Zhōu was angry
and sent word to Qí, saying:
'The heavens have collapsed and the earth has split,
and the Son of Heaven is lying on a mourning mat.
The official of the eastern border, Tián Yīngqí, arrived late;
let him be executed.'
King Wēi flared up in anger and said:
'Ha!
Your mother was a servant girl!'
In the end, he became the laughingstock of the world.
Thus, while they were alive, he paid homage to Zhōu,
but when they died, he cursed them,
truly because he could not bear their demands.
That the Son of Heaven acts this way is inherent;
it is not at all surprising."
Xīnyuán Yǎn said:
"Sir, have you alone not seen those servants?
For ten men to follow one man,
is it because their strength is insufficient
or because their wisdom is not as great?
It is because they fear him."
Lǔ Zhònglián said:
"So, is Liáng's relationship to Qín like that of a servant?"
Xīnyuán Yǎn said:
"Indeed."
Lǔ Zhònglián said:
"In that case, I shall cause the King of Qín to boil and mince the King of Liáng."
Xīnyuán Yǎn was displeased and resentful, saying:
"Hmph,
these are too extreme,
the words of the gentleman!
How can you, sir, cause the King of Qín to boil and mince the King of Liáng?"
Lǔ Zhònglián said:
"Certainly,
let me explain.
In the past,
the Marquis of Guǐ, the Marquis of È, and King Wén
were the three high officials of Zhòu.
The Marquis of Guǐ had a daughter who was beautiful,
so he presented her to Zhòu.
Zhòu thought her ugly
and minced the Marquis of Guǐ.
The Marquis of È argued vehemently
and protested sharply,
so Zhòu had the Marquis of È dried into jerky.
King Wén heard of this
and sighed deeply,
so Zhòu detained him in the prison of Yǒulǐ,
and for a hundred days intended to let him die there.
Why should one call someone 'Emperor' alongside others,
only to end up being made into jerky or minced meat?
King Mǐn of Qí was going to Lǔ,
and Yíwéizǐ followed him holding his whip
and said to the people of Lǔ:
'How will you receive my lord?'
The people of Lǔ said:
'We shall receive your lord with ten sets of the three sacrificial animals.'
Yíwéizǐ said:
'By what ritual do you come to receive my lord?
That lord of mine
is the Son of Heaven.
When the Son of Heaven makes a tour of inspection,
the feudal lords must vacate their palaces,
hand over the keys,
gather their robes and carry his armrests,
and oversee his meals from below the hall;
once the Son of Heaven has finished eating,
then he can retire to hear matters of court.'
The people of Lǔ threw down their keys
and did not admit him.
Unable to enter Lǔ,
he intended to go to Xuē,
requesting passage through Zōu.
At that time, the ruler of Zōu had died,
and King Mǐn wished to enter to offer condolences.
Yíwéizǐ said to the orphaned heir of Zōu:
'When the Son of Heaven offers condolences,
the host must turn his back on the coffin
and set a place facing north on the south side,
and only then may the Son of Heaven face south to offer condolences.'
The officials of Zōu said:
'If it must be like this,
we would rather fall on our swords and die.'
Therefore, he did not dare to enter Zōu.
The officials of Zōu and Lǔ,
while alive, could not serve or nourish him,
and after his death, could not perform the ritual of putting grain in his mouth.
Yet he still wanted to impose the rituals of the Son of Heaven upon the officials of Zōu and Lǔ,
and they did not admit him.
Now Qín is a state of ten thousand chariots,
and Liáng is also a state of ten thousand chariots.
Both possess states of ten thousand chariots,
and both have the title of King;
because they won one battle,
you wish to follow them and make them Emperor;
this is to make the high ministers of the Three Jìn inferior to the servants and concubines of Zōu and Lǔ.
Furthermore, if Qín becomes Emperor without ceasing,
they will surely change the high ministers of the feudal lords.
They will take away those they call unworthy
and give positions to those they call worthy;
they will take away those they hate
and give positions to those they love.
They will also make their daughters and slanderous concubines the consorts and ladies of the feudal lords,
placing them in the palaces of Liáng.
How could the King of Liáng then live in peace?
And how could you, General, maintain your former favor?"
Thereupon, Xīnyuán Yǎn rose,
bowed twice and apologized, saying:
"At first, I took you, sir, for an ordinary man,
but today I know that you are a scholar of the world
indeed.
I beg to leave,
and I dare not speak again of Qín being Emperor."
The Qín general heard of this
and withdrew his army fifty lǐ.
It happened that the Prince of Wèi, Wújì, seized the army of Jìn Bǐ
to rescue Zhào and attack Qín,
and the Qín army retreated and left.
Thereupon, Lord Píngyuán wished to enfeoff Lǔ Zhònglián.
Lǔ Zhònglián declined three times
and ultimately refused to accept.
Lord Píngyuán then held a banquet,
and when they were mellow with wine,
he rose and stepped forward to offer a thousand gold pieces for Lǔ Lián's longevity.
Lǔ Lián laughed and said:
"What is valued in a scholar of the world
is that he removes troubles for others,
relieves hardships, and resolves confusion without taking anything for it.
If one takes something,
then one is a merchant,
which Zhònglián cannot bear to be."
He then took leave of Lord Píngyuán and departed,
never to see him again for the rest of his life.
He spoke to Prime Minister Zhāng, saying:
"How can you look down upon the people of Zhào
yet expect the people of Zhào to respect you?
How can you hate the people of Zhào
yet expect the people of Zhào to love you?
Glue and lacquer
are extremely sticky,
yet they cannot join what is distant;
a swan's feather
is extremely light,
yet it cannot lift itself.
But when blown by a fresh breeze,
it travels across the four seas.
Therefore, there are matters where the action is simple but success is achieved,
because one follows the natural course.
Now Zhào is a powerful state of ten thousand chariots,
with the Zhāng and Fǔ rivers in front,
Chángshān on its right,
Héjiān on its left,
and Dài to its north;
with a million armored soldiers,
it once suppressed the powerful Qí,
and for more than forty years Qín has been unable to get what it wants.
From this perspective,
Zhào's position in the world is not light.
Now you disparage the powerful Zhào of ten thousand chariots
and long for the small Liáng which cannot be obtained;
I humbly suggest this is not a course you should take."
The Lord said: "Good."
From then on,
in the midst of large gatherings of people,
he never failed to speak of the strengths of the people of Zhào,
and never failed to speak of the goodness of Zhào's customs.
Zhèng Tóng went north to have an audience with Zhào Wáng.
Zhào Wáng said:
"You are a renowned scholar from the south.
What do you have to teach me?"
Zhèng Tóng said:
"I am but a rustic and lowly man from the south.
How am I worthy of your questioning?
Nevertheless,
since Your Majesty has brought me before you,
how would I dare not respond?
When I was young,
my father once taught me about military affairs."
Zhào Wáng said:
"I do not like military affairs."
Zhèng Tóng then clapped his hands, looked up to the sky, laughed and said:
"Military affairs are indeed what the world is most fond of.
I suspected that Your Majesty would not like them.
I also once used military affairs to persuade Wèi Zhāo Wáng.
Zhāo Wáng also said:
'I do not like them.'
I said:
'Can Your Majesty's conduct be like that of Xǔ Yóu?
Xǔ Yóu was free from the burdens of the world,
so he did not accept it.
Now that Your Majesty has already received the inheritance of your ancestors,
do you desire the peace of the ancestral temple,
that your territory not be reduced,
and that the blood sacrifices of the state continue?'
The King said: 'Indeed.'
Now, if someone were to carry the Pearl of Suí Hóu,
hold the Jade Ring of Hé Qiū,
and possess wealth worth ten thousand pieces of gold,
and were to spend the night in the wild,
having neither the might of Mèng Bèn
nor the decisiveness of Jīng Qìng within,
and without the protection of bows and crossbows without,
before a single night passed,
people would surely put him in danger.
Now there are powerful and greedy states
bordering Your Majesty's territory,
demanding Your Majesty's land.
To inform them with reason is ineffective;
to persuade them with righteousness is ignored.
If Your Majesty does not have the means for war and defense in this Warring States period,
how will you resist them?
If Your Majesty has no military,
the neighboring states will have their way."
Zhào Wáng said: "I beg to receive your instruction."
Jiàn Xìn Jūn was honored in the state of Zhào.
Gōngzǐ Wèi Móu passed through Zhào.
Zhào Wáng welcomed him.
Looking back as he returned to his seat,
there was a foot of silk before him,
and he was about to order a craftsman to make it into a cap.
The craftsman saw a guest arrive
and thus withdrew.
Zhào Wáng said:
"The Prince has driven his carriage from afar
to favor me with his presence.
I wish to hear how to govern the world."
Wèi Móu said:
"If Your Majesty can value Your Majesty's kingdom as much as this foot of silk,
then Your Majesty's kingdom will be well-governed."
Zhào Wáng was displeased,
which showed in his expression,
and he said:
"You do not realize that I am unworthy,
and have been made to serve the state.
How could I dare to treat the kingdom as lightly as this?"
Wèi Móu said: "Do not be angry, Your Majesty.
Please allow me to explain it to Your Majesty."
He said:
"Your Majesty has this foot of silk;
why not order the attendants before you to make it into a cap?"
The King said: "The attendants do not know how to make caps."
Wèi Móu said: "If a cap is ruined,
how does it diminish Your Majesty's kingdom?
Yet Your Majesty must wait for a craftsman before employing them.
Now, regarding the 'craftsmen' of the world,
some are unfit,
causing the state to become a wasteland
and the former kings to receive no blood sacrifices.
Yet Your Majesty does not give the task to experts,
but instead gives it to the young and inexperienced.
Moreover, Your Majesty's predecessors
harnessed Xī Shǒu as the lead and Mǎ Fú as the side-horse
to compete with Qín.
Qín at that time
met its match in their sharpness.
Now Your Majesty is wavering
and uses Jiàn Xìn to compete with powerful Qín.
I fear Qín will break Your Majesty's carriage shafts."
Wèi Líng Gōng was close to Yōng Jǔ and Mǐzǐ Xiá.
These two men
monopolized the ruler's power to block those around him.
Fùtú Zhēn said to the ruler:
"Yesterday I dreamed of you, my lord."
The ruler said:
"What did you dream?"
He said:
"I dreamed of the Kitchen God, Zào Jūn."
The ruler angrily changed his expression and said:
"I have heard that those who dream of a ruler
dream of the sun.
Now you say you dreamed of the Kitchen God to represent your ruler.
If you have an explanation, it is fine;
if you have no explanation, you shall die."
He replied:
"The sun
shines upon everything under heaven;
not a single thing can block it.
But a stove is not like that;
if the person in front is basking in its warmth,
then the person behind has no way to see it.
Now I suspect there are people basking in Your Majesty's warmth,
and that is why I dreamed of the Kitchen God."
The ruler said: "Good."
Thereupon,
he dismissed Yōng Jǔ and Mǐzǐ Xiá
and appointed Sīkōng Gǒu.
Someone said to Jiàn Xìn:
"The means by which you serve the King
is beauty. Qiě's
means by which he serves the King
is wisdom.
Beauty ages and declines,
while wisdom ages and increases.
Using wisdom that increases daily
to displace beauty that is declining and deteriorating,
you will surely be in difficulty."
Jiàn Xìn Jūn said: "What should I do?"
He said:
"Those who run alongside a fine steed
will be exhausted after five li;
but if one mounts the steed and drives it,
one does not tire and covers many roads.
You should let him ride the carriage of sole responsibility
and handle the power of sole decision-making
while residing in Hándān.
Let him manage the internal affairs of the state
and deal with the feudal lords externally.
Then there will be matters he does not report.
You can then speak to the King and hold him heavily accountable.
Qiě's axle will then be broken."
Jiàn Xìn Jūn
bowed twice and accepted the advice.
He went in and spoke to the King,
entrusting him heavily with matters based on his ability and holding him to strict accountability.
Before a year had passed, Qiě fled and went into exile.
Kǔchéng Cháng said to Jiàn Xìn Jūn:
"The world has formed a Vertical Alliance,
yet only Zhào is on bad terms with Qín.
Why is this?
Wèi killed Lǚ Yí,
and the world allied with them.
Now you take Héjiān;
how is this different from the killing of Lǚ Yí?
You should simply set aside these false pretenses.
Even Wén Xìn already knows this.
If following the alliance leads to success,
why worry about not taking Héjiān?
If following the alliance leads to no success,
what benefit is there in taking Héjiān?"
Xī Xiè had an audience with Jiàn Xìn Jūn.
Jiàn Xìn Jūn said:
"The Marquis of Wén Xìn's treatment of me
is very rude.
When Qín sent people to serve here,
I gave them the office of Chancellor
and the rank of Five Grandmasters.
The Marquis of Wén Xìn's treatment of me
is exceedingly rude."
Xī Xiè said:
"I believe those currently in power
are not as good as merchants."
Jiàn Xìn Jūn said indignantly:
"Do you disparage those in power and exalt merchants?"
He said:
"Not so.
A good merchant does not compete with others over the price of buying and selling,
but carefully observes the timing.
Buying when things are cheap,
though it is expensive later, it was already cheap;
selling when things are expensive,
though it is cheap later, it was already expensive.
In the past,
Wén Wáng was imprisoned in Yǒulǐ,
and Wǔ Wáng was restrained at Yùmén,
yet they eventually cut off Zhòu's head and hung it from the Tàibái flag.
This was the achievement of Wǔ Wáng.
Now you cannot match the Marquis of Wén Xìn in power,
yet you blame the Marquis of Wén Xìn for a lack of etiquette.
I privately believe this is not the right course for you."
Wèi Gà said to Lord Jiànxìn:
"There was once a person who set a foot trap and caught a tiger.
The tiger was enraged
and tore off its paw to escape.
As for the tiger’s nature, it was not that it did not love its paw.
However, not allowing a paw of a few inches
to harm a body of seven feet
is a matter of weighing priorities.
Now, possessing a state
is more than just a seven-foot body.
And Your Excellency’s relationship to the King
is more than a paw of a few inches.
I hope Your Excellency will maturely consider this."
Qín attacked Zhào,
and the sound of drums and bells was heard in the Northern Hall.
Xī Bēi said:
"Qín’s attack on Zhào
should not be as urgent as this.
This is a summons to arms.
There must be a high minister who wishes to join the Horizontal Alliance.
If the King wishes to know who it is,
tomorrow morning, present the various ministers and consult them;
the first to speak of the Horizontal Alliance
is the person."
Lord Jiànxìn indeed spoke of the Horizontal Alliance first.
Lǐ Bó of Qí went to see King Xiàochéng.
King Xiàochéng was pleased with him
and made him Governor of Dài Commandery.
After he had stayed there for only a short time,
people reported that he was rebelling.
King Xiàochéng was just eating a meal
and did not drop his food.
After a short time,
the reporters came again,
but King Xiàochéng did not respond.
Later,
he sent an envoy to say:
"Qí has raised troops to strike Yàn.
I feared they would use striking Yàn as a pretext
and use their troops to surprise Zhào,
so I deployed troops to prepare our defense.
Now Yàn and Qí have united.
I request to exploit their weariness,
and much land can be carved away."
From this time onward,
among those who served King Xiàochéng abroad,
none felt suspicion from the court.
On behalf of Qí, a letter was presented to the King of Zhào,
by the envoy Fù Chǒu, who said:
"With one audience,
I can make the King sit while the world brings famous treasures to him.
Yet I privately wonder why the King does not try to see me
and instead leaves me in straits.
The various ministers must surely consider me incompetent,
and that is why the King delays seeing me.
Those who consider me incompetent
are none other than those
who wish to use the King’s troops
to achieve their own private ends.
If not that,
then their diplomatic relations are biased;
if not that,
then their wisdom is insufficient;
if not that,
then they wish to use the weight of the world to intimidate the King
and get their way with the King.
If I use Qí to serve the King,
the King can destroy Yàn,
can destroy Hán and Wèi,
can attack Qín,
and can isolate Qín.
If I use Qí to bring a venerable name to the King,
who in the world would dare not bring a venerable name to the King?
If I use Qí to bring land to the King,
who in the world would dare not bring land to the King?
If I use Qí to seek prestige for the King from Yàn, Hán, and Wèi,
who would dare refuse?
My ability can be seen from what has gone before.
If Qí values the King first,
then the whole world will value the King;
without Qí,
the whole world will surely despise the King.
The strength of Qín
values the King only because of the absence of Qí;
Yàn and Wèi themselves value the King because of the absence of Qí.
Now, if the King is without Qí, how can he alone avoid being disregarded by the world?
Therefore, those who advise the King to be without Qí
either have insufficient wisdom
or are disloyal.
If not that,
then they wish to use the King’s troops to achieve their private ends;
if not that,
then they wish to belittle the King using the weight of the world
and get their way with the King;
if not that,
then they are those in high positions who are capable of acting lowly.
I hope the King will maturely consider the advantages and disadvantages of being without Qí."
Qí wished to attack Sòng,
but Qín ordered Qǐ Jiǎ to forbid it.
Qí then came to the aid of Zhào to attack Sòng.
The King of Qín was angry
and directed his resentment at Zhào.
Lǐ Duì made a covenant with five states to attack Qín,
but it was without merit; he kept the world’s troops at Chénggǎo
while he secretly negotiated with Qín.
He also wished to join Qín in attacking Wèi
to resolve their resentment and obtain a fief there.
The King of Wèi was not pleased.
An envoy went to Qí
and said to the King of Qí:
"I said to the King of Wèi on your behalf:
'The three Jìn states all suffer from Qín.
This current attack on Qín
is for the sake of Zhào.
If five states attack Zhào,
Zhào will surely perish.
If Qín expels Lǐ Duì,
Lǐ Duì will surely die.
This current attack on Qín
is to save Master Lǐ from death.
Now Zhào keeps the world’s armor at Chénggǎo
and secretly bargains with Qín.
Once they have come to terms,
they will order Qín to attack Wèi to complete his private fief.
What does the King gain by serving Zhào?
Furthermore, the King once crossed the Zhāng River
and personally went to court in Hándān,
holding Yīn and Chéng,
and carrying Hāo, Gé, and Bì on his back,
to act as a shield for Zhào,
yet Zhào has done nothing for the King.
Now they use Héyáng and Gūmì to enfeoff their son,
and then order Qín to attack the King
so as to easily take Yīn.
Since people are like this, one can then know whether they are worthy or not.
If the King were to use half of what he uses to serve Zhào to win over Qí,
would anyone in the world dare to plot against the King?
If the King serves Qí,
there will be no shame of entering their court,
and no expense of carving away land.
For the King’s sake, Qí emptied
its state before Yàn and Zhào, and used its troops two thousand lǐ away.
Therefore, in attacking cities and in field battles,
it has never failed to face arrows and stones first on the King’s behalf.
Having obtained two capitals
and carving away Hédōng,
it handed them all over to the King.
From this time on,
whenever Qín attacked Wèi,
Qí’s armor never failed to arrive at the King’s borders every year.
May I ask what the King has used to repay Qí?
Hán Mǐn stays in Zhào,
three thousand lǐ away from Qí,
and the King uses this to doubt Qí,
saying they have secret ties with Qín.
Now the King also holds the former Lord of Xuē as Chancellor,
treats Hán Xú well as a top associate,
and honors Yú Shāng as a great guest.
Can the King indeed turn around and doubt Qí?'
When the King of Wèi heard these words, he was greatly humbled,
and his desire to serve the King was very submissive.
He felt resentment toward Zhào.
I hope the King will daily hear of Wèi without needing to see ill will;
I request to shift his resentment onto Zhào on the King’s behalf.
I hope the King will secretly value Zhào,
but do not let Qín see that the King values Zhào.
If Qín sees it, they will also value Zhào.
If Qí and Qín both value Zhào,
I will surely see Yàn, Hán, and Wèi also valuing Zhào,
and none will dare to contend with Zhào.
If five states serve Zhào,
and Zhào follows the Vertical Alliance to unite against Qín,
it will surely be high for the King.
Therefore, I wish for the King to partially intimidate the world
and privately sweeten them all.
Let the King use me with Hán, Wèi, and Yàn to intimidate Zhào,
and let Dān sweeten it;
use Zhào to intimidate Hán and Wèi,
and let me sweeten it;
use the three Jìn to intimidate Qín,
and let Shùn sweeten it;
use the world to intimidate Chǔ,
and let Mǐn sweeten it.
Then the world will all pressure Qín to serve the King
and not dare to have private dealings with each other.
Once the alliances are fixed,
then the King may choose among them."
Qí was about to attack Sòng,
but Qín and Chǔ forbade it.
Qí therefore wished to join with Zhào,
but Zhào would not listen.
Qí then ordered Gōngsūn Yǎn to persuade Lǐ Duì to attack Sòng and secure a fief there.
Lǐ Duì then said to the King of Qí:
"The reason I strengthened the Sān Jìn to attack Qín
was not because I thought Qí would benefit from the destruction of Qín,
but because I wanted to make it possible to attack Sòng.
However, Sòng has established the Crown Prince as King;
those below are close to those above, and their defense is firm.
Therefore, I wanted you to quickly return and let your soldiers and people rest.
Now the Crown Prince has fled,
and those who favored the Crown Prince
are all determined to die.
If you attack them again,
their state will surely fall into chaos,
and with the Crown Prince being away,
this is also the time to seize Sòng.
"I sent Gōngsūn Yǎn on your behalf to persuade Fèngyáng Jūn, saying: 'You are already old;
your fief must be established early.
In considering a fief for you,
none is better than Sòng;
no other state is comparable.
The people of Qín are greedy;
Hán and Wèi are in danger;
Yān and Chǔ are remote;
the land of Zhōngshān is meager.
None is better than Yīn.
If you miss this moment,
it cannot be regained.
Sòng's crimes are heavy;
Qí's anger is deep.
To bring ruin and chaos to Sòng,
gain the favor of great Qí,
and secure your own fief—
this is a once-in-a-hundred-generations opportunity.'
Because Fèngyáng Jūn found this very appealing,
as long as he obtains a large fief,
Qí will face no major opposition.
I wish for you to launch a grand expedition to attack Sòng,
but there is no need to commit troops yet.
Wait until the plowing is finished
to observe how Fèngyáng Jūn responds to you.
Dangle the prospect of Yīn to tempt him,
and maintain influence over Yān to oversee him.
While I wait for the fief of Zhōng,
the matter will surely be a great success.
I also wish for you to provide land to Xiāng'ān Jūn to support me.
If you indeed ruin Sòng,
this will be the time to gain these two lands;
why should you begrudge them?
If you do not achieve your goals in Sòng,
how would the allied states dare to hope for anything?
Use this to support me,
and as I control Yān and observe Zhào,
you will crush the enemy and decide the fate of the world."
The five states attacked Qín without success
and stopped at Chénggāo.
Zhào wanted to make peace with Qín;
Chǔ, Wèi, and Hán were about to respond to this,
but Qín did not desire it.
Sū Dài said to the King of Qí:
"I believe you have seen Fèngyáng Jūn.
I said to Fèngyáng Jūn:
'If the world scatters and serves Qín,
Qín will surely occupy Sòng.
Wèi Rǎn will surely envy your possession of Yīn.
Since the King of Qín is greedy
and Wèi Rǎn is envious,
then Yīn will be unobtainable.
If you do not make peace,
Qí will surely attack Sòng.
If Qí attacks Sòng,
then Chǔ will surely attack Sòng,
Wèi will surely attack Sòng,
and Yān and Zhào will assist them.
When the five states occupy Sòng,
in less than one or two months,
Yīn will surely be obtained.
Once Yīn is obtained and you then make peace,
even if Qín undergoes changes,
you will have no worries.
If you have no choice but to make peace,
then I wish for the five states to again make a firm covenant.
I wish for Zhào to be gained;
then you shall soar like a hero.
Together with the high official of the Hán clan, Dōng Miǎn,
the King of Qí will surely not recall Mǐn.
Let me maintain the covenant;
if there is anyone who betrays the covenant,
attack them with the other four states.
If no one betrays the covenant,
but Qín encroaches upon it,
the five states will again stand firm and resist.
Now Hán and Wèi are suspicious of Qí;
if you do not again make a firm covenant before negotiating peace,
I fear the allied states will fall into great chaos.
Qí and Qín will not reconcile;
one will surely be more powerful than the other.
Whether they reconcile later or one becomes more powerful,
neither is to Zhào's advantage.
Moreover, if the world scatters and serves Qín,
it means Qín will control the world.
If Qín controls the world,
what use will it have for the rest of the world?
I wish for you to plan early.'
'There are six moves for the world to compete for Qín's favor,
all of which are unfavorable to Zhào.
When the world competes for Qín's favor,
the King of Qín accepts the states along the coast,
joins with those who are close relatives,
occupies the Central Plain,
and seeks profit from the Sān Jìn;
this is one of Qín's moves.
If Qín carries out this plan,
it will be unfavorable to Zhào,
and you will ultimately not obtain Yīn; this is the first.
When the world competes for Qín's favor,
the King of Qín installs Hán Mín in Qí,
installs Chéngyáng Jūn in Hán,
makes Wèi Huái the chancellor in Wèi,
re-employs Yǎn,
brings together the two kings,
and the likes of Wáng Bèn and Hán Tā
all arise to take charge of affairs;
this is one of Qín's moves.
If Qín carries out this plan,
it will be unfavorable to Zhào,
and you will again not obtain Yīn; this is the second.
When the world competes for Qín's favor,
the King of Qín accepts Qí and accepts Zhào,
three borders and three relatives,
occupies Wèi and seeks Ānyì;
this is one of Qín's moves.
If Qín carries out this plan,
Qí and Zhào will respond to it;
Wèi will not wait to be attacked
but will offer Ānyì and trust Qín.
Qín will gain the wealth of Ānyì,
Wèi will become a top ally,
and Hán will surely pay court
to Qín, having passed through Zhào and already at Ānyì;
this is one of Qín's moves.
If Qín carries out this plan, it will be unfavorable to Zhào,
and you will surely not obtain Yīn; this is the third.
When the world competes for Qín's favor,
Qín strengthens its ties with Yān and Zhào
to attack Qí,
brings in Chǔ, and joins with Hán Mǐn to attack Wèi;
this is one of Qín's moves.
If Qín carries out this plan,
Yān and Zhào will respond to it.
Yān and Zhào attack Qí,
and once the troops are deployed,
Qín will then take Chǔ and attack Wèi.
In less than one or two months,
Wèi will surely be broken.
Qín will take Ānyì and block Nǚjǐ;
Hán's Tàiyuán will be cut off.
They will go down to Zhǐdào
and Gāo,
and through Nányáng attack Wèi,
isolate Hán,
and encompass the two Zhōu;
then Zhào will naturally wither away.
The state will be dried up by Qín,
and its troops divided in Qí;
this is not to Zhào's advantage.
And you will never in your life obtain Yīn;
this is the fourth.
When the world competes for Qín's favor,
Qín strengthens its ties with the Sān Jìn to attack Qí;
the state will be broken and its resources exhausted,
while its troops are divided to the east in Qí.
Qín will keep its troops ready and attack Wèi
to take Ānyì;
this is one of Qín's moves.
If Qín carries out this plan,
and you move to rescue Wèi,
it will be using troops already worn out from attacking Qí
to fight against Qín;
if you do not rescue it,
how can Hán and Wèi avoid joining the west?
The state will be caught in these schemes,
and you will never in your life obtain Yīn; this is the fifth.
When the world competes for Qín's favor,
Qín acts in the name of righteousness,
preserving those being destroyed and continuing broken lineages,
stabilizing the endangered and supporting the weak,
and establishing guiltless rulers;
it will surely raise up Zhōngshān and Shèng.
If Qín raises up Zhōngshān and Shèng,
then Zhào and Sòng will share the same fate;
what time will there be to speak of Yīn? This is the sixth.
Therefore, I say that you must not negotiate peace;
then Yīn will surely be obtained.'
Fèngyáng Jūn said:
'Excellent.'
He then broke off peace negotiations with Qín
and gathered Qí and Wèi to complete the seizure of Yīn."
Lóu Huǎn was about to be sent as an envoy.
He attended to his duties,
took his leave,
and said to the King of Zhào:
“Though I exhaust my strength and wisdom,
I shall die and never see Your Majesty again.”
The King said: “What kind of talk is this?
I will certainly write letters and send you generous gifts.”
Lóu Zǐ said:
“Has Your Majesty not heard of Gōngzǐ Móuyí in the state of Sòng?
He would not eat if there was no meat.
Wén Zhāng was on good terms with Sòng,
but he disliked Gōngzǐ Móuyí,
and so it truly was.
Now my relationship with Your Majesty is not like that of Sòng with Gōngzǐ Móuyí,
yet those who dislike me are more numerous than Wén Zhāng.
Therefore, I shall die and never see Your Majesty again.”
The King said:
“You must strive on your journey;
I have an oath with you.”
Lóu Zǐ then departed.
Later, he used Zhōngmóu to rebel
and entered Liáng.
Scouts came to report this,
but the King would not listen,
saying:
“I have already given my word to Lóu Zǐ.”
Yú Qīng petitioned the King of Zhào, saying:
“In human sentiment,
is it better to have others pay court to oneself,
or to pay court to others?”
The King of Zhào said:
“One would certainly rather have others pay court to oneself;
for what reason would one prefer to pay court to others?”
Yú Qīng said:
“Now, Wèi is the leader of the Vertical Alliance,
and the one who opposes this is Fàn Zuò.
Now, if Your Majesty can use a hundred lǐ of land,
or a city of ten thousand households,
to request the execution of Fàn Zuò in Wèi,
then if Fàn Zuò dies,
the leadership of the alliance can be moved to Zhào.”
The King of Zhào said:
“Good.”
He then sent a man with a hundred lǐ of land
to request the execution of Fàn Zuò in Wèi.
The King of Wèi agreed
and ordered the Sītú to arrest Fàn Zuò,
but he was not yet killed.
Fàn Zuò presented a letter to the King of Wèi, saying:
“I have heard that the King of Zhào offered a hundred lǐ of land
to request my execution.
To kill the innocent Fàn Zuò
is because I am of little consequence;
but to obtain a hundred lǐ of land
is a great profit.
I privately consider this a fine thing for Your Majesty.
Although this is so,
there is one point:
if the hundred lǐ of land cannot be obtained,
and the dead cannot be brought back to life,
then the sovereign will surely be ridiculed by the world!
I privately think that rather than trading with a dead man,
it is better to trade with a living man to serve you.”
He also sent a letter to the successor Chancellor, Xìnlíng Jūn, saying:
“Now Zhào and Wèi
are rival states at war.
The King of Zhào sent a short letter,
and the King of Wèi lightly executes the innocent Fàn Zuò for him.
Although I am unworthy,
I am the former Chancellor of Wèi.
I once, for the sake of Wèi,
offended Zhào.
If there are no useful ministers within the state,
even if land is gained outside,
the position cannot be held.
There is no one like you, My Lord.
But now, the one who can defend Wèi is no one but you. If the King listens to Zhào and kills me,
then powerful Qín will follow Zhào’s desires
and double Zhào’s cessions,
then how will you stop it?
This will be a burden for you.”
Xìnlíng Jūn said:
“Good.”
He immediately spoke to the King and had him released.
Yān enfeoffed the man from Sòng, Róng Fén, as Gāoyáng Jūn,
making him a general to attack Zhào.
The King of Zhào consequently ceded three cities in Jìdōng, including Lú, Gāotáng, and Píngyuánlíng, and market towns and cities totaling fifty-seven,
and ordered them given to Qí,
in order to seek Ānpíng Jūn to be his general.
Mǎfú Jūn said to Píngyuán Jūn:
“Is the state truly so devoid of men!
You recruit Ānpíng Jūn to be general
and then cede fifty-seven cities and towns in Jìdōng to Qí.
These are what one would expect to obtain from an enemy state
after defeating their army, killing their general, and seizing their land.
Now you give these to Qí
just to seek Ānpíng Jūn to be general—
is the state truly so devoid of men!
And why do you not make me, Zhào Shē, the general?
I once committed a crime and lived in Yān;
Yān made me the Governor of Shànggǔ;
I know the valleys and fortifications of Yān well.
Within a hundred days,
before the world’s armies have gathered,
I would have already taken Yān.
So why do you seek Ānpíng Jūn to be general?”
Píngyuán Jūn said:
“General, let it be.
I have already spoken to my sovereign.
My sovereign was pleased to listen to me.
General, say no more.”
Mǎfú Jūn said:
“You are mistaken!
The reason you seek Ānpíng Jūn
is because Qí’s relationship to Yān
is a blood-feud.
It is not so for me.
If Ānpíng Jūn is foolish,
he certainly cannot withstand Róng Fén;
if Ānpíng Jūn is wise,
he will be unwilling to fight the people of Yān.
Between these two outcomes,
Ānpíng Jūn must fall into one.
Although this is so,
there is another aspect.
If Ānpíng Jūn is wise,
then why would he want Zhào to be strong?
If Zhào is strong, then Qí can no longer be hegemon.
Now, obtaining the troops of a strong Zhào
to block the generals of Yān,
he will delay for years,
letting the strength of the officers and the young men
be exhausted in the trenches and ramparts.
The chariots, armor, and banners will be worn out,
the granaries and treasuries emptied.
Both states will be mutually exhausted,
and then he will lead his troops back.
To exhaust the armies of two states—
nothing is clearer than this.”
In summer,
the army hung their pots to cook.
They took three cities,
but no city wall was larger than a hundred zhì.
It turned out exactly as Mǎfú Jūn had said.
Three states attacked Qín,
and Zhào attacked Zhōngshān,
taking Fúliǔ,
and for five years controlled the Hūtuó River.
The men of Qí, Róng Guō and Sòng Tū, said to Chóu Hǎo:
“It would be better to return all the new lands of Zhōngshān.
Zhōngshān should use these words to Qí, saying,
‘The four states are going to borrow a path through Wèi
to follow the route of Zhāng Zǐ.’
When Qí hears this,
they will surely surrender the city of Gǔ.”
Zhào sent Zhào Zhuāng to form the Vertical Alliance,
intending to attack Qí.
Qí offered to hand over land.
Zhào consequently belittled Zhào Zhuāng.
Qí Míng spoke to the King of Zhào, saying:
“Qí feared the alliance of the Verticalists,
so they offered land.
Now hearing that Zhào Zhuāng is belittled
and Zhāng Qín is honored,
Qí will certainly not hand over the land.”
The King of Zhào said:
“Good.”
He then summoned Zhào Zhuāng and honored him.
Zhái Zhāng came from Liáng
and was very well-received by the King of Zhào.
Three times the King of Zhào invited him to be Chancellor,
but Zhái Zhāng declined and would not accept.
Tián Sì said to the Pillar of State Hán Xiàng:
“I request to assassinate him for you.
If the guest dies,
the King will surely be angry and execute Jiànxìn Jūn.
If Jiànxìn Jūn dies,
then you will surely become Chancellor.
If Jiànxìn Jūn does not die,
you can make it a bond, never failing for life,
and you can thus place Jiànxìn Jūn in your debt.”
Féng Jì spoke on behalf of Lúlíng Jūn to the King of Zhào, saying:
“Your Majesty’s expulsion of Lúlíng Jūn
was for the sake of Yān.”
The King said: “The reason I value them
is not because of Yān or Qín.”
He replied: "Qín has spoken about Yú Qīng three times,
yet Your Majesty does not expel him.
Now Yàn has spoken about Lúlíng Jūn only once,
and Your Majesty expels him.
This means Your Majesty treats strong Qín lightly and treats weak Yàn seriously."
The King said: "I am not doing this for Yàn;
I was already intending to expel him."
"In that case, Your Majesty expels Lúlíng Jūn and yet it is not for the sake of Yàn.
To go through with expelling a beloved younger brother,
while also failing to gain favor with either Yàn or Qín—
your servant privately thinks Your Majesty should not take this course."
Féng Jì requested an audience with the King of Zhào,
and an usher introduced him.
Féng Jì clasped his hands and lowered his head,
wanting to speak but not daring to.
The King asked for the reason,
and he replied:
"There was a guest who introduced someone to Fú Zǐ,
and afterwards asked about his faults.
Fú Zǐ said:
'Your guest has three faults alone:
He looked at me and smiled,
which is over-familiarity;
he spoke without citing a teacher,
which is rebelliousness;
his acquaintance was shallow yet his words were deep,
which is disorder.'
The guest said: 'It is not so.
Now, looking at someone and smiling
is harmony;
speaking without citing a teacher
is a common way of talking;
a shallow acquaintance speaking deeply
is loyalty.
In the past, Yáo met Shùn among the grass and reeds,
sitting on the ridges of the fields and shaded by mulberry trees,
and before the shadows had moved, the rule over the world was handed over.
Yī Yǐn carried a tripod and cutting board to seek an audience with Tāng,
and before his name was even well known, he received the rank of Sāngōng.
If those with shallow acquaintances were not allowed to speak deeply,
then the world would not have been handed over,
and the rank of Sāngōng would not have been obtained.'"
The King of Zhào said: "Very good."
Féng Jì said:
"Now, your humble servant’s acquaintance is shallow, yet I wish to speak deeply;
is it permissible?"
The King said: "Please offer your instruction."
Thereupon Féng Jì spoke.
A guest had an audience with the King of Zhào and said:
"I heard Your Majesty has sent someone to buy horses;
is that true?"
The King said:
"It is true."
"For what reason have you not sent him until now?"
The King said:
"I have not yet found an expert in judging horses."
He replied: "Why does Your Majesty not send Jiànxìn Jūn?"
The King said: "Jiànxìn Jūn has state affairs to attend to,
and he also does not know how to judge horses."
He said:
"Why does Your Majesty not send Jì Jī?"
The King said: "Jì Jī is a woman,
and she does not know how to judge horses."
He replied: "If the horse-buying is done well,
what benefit does it bring to the state?"
The King said: "No benefit to the state."
"If the horse-buying is done poorly,
what danger does it pose to the state?"
The King said: "No danger to the state."
He replied: "In that case, whether the horse-buying is good or bad,
both provide no danger or benefit to the state.
Nevertheless, in Your Majesty's buying of horses,
you will surely wait for an expert.
Now, in governing the world,
if the conduct and measures are incorrect,
the state becomes empty and ruined,
and the Shèjì will receive no blood sacrifices;
yet Your Majesty does not wait for an expert,
but entrusts it to Jiànxìn Jūn.
Why is this?"
The King of Zhào did not respond.
The guest said:
"In the laws of Guō of Yàn,
there is what is called the Sāng Yōng; does Your Majesty know of it?"
The King said: "I have not heard of it."
"What is called Sāng Yōng
refers to the sycophants and attendants close at hand,
as well as the consorts, favorites, and children.
These are all able to take advantage of Your Majesty's intoxication or confusion
to seek what they desire from Your Majesty.
Since they can obtain it within,
the high ministers will then pervert the law for them without.
Thus, while the sun and moon shine without,
their thief is within;
one carefully prepares against what one hates,
yet the calamity lies in what one loves."
Qín attacked Wèi
and took Níngyì;
all the feudal lords offered congratulations.
The King of Zhào sent an envoy to offer congratulations,
but three times they returned without being granted access.
The King of Zhào was worried about this
and said to his attendants:
"With the strength of Qín,
having gained Níngyì,
they can control Qí and Zhào.
All the feudal lords have offered congratulations,
yet I alone sent congratulations and could not gain access.
This means they will surely bring war upon me;
what should be done about it?"
The attendants said: "The reason the envoys went three times and could not gain access
must be that the ones sent were not the right people.
There is a man named Liàng Yì,
who is a persuasive speaker;
Your Majesty might try sending him."
Liàng Yì personally received the order and went.
Upon arriving in Qín,
he presented a letter to the King of Qín, saying:
"Your Majesty has expanded your territory at Níngyì,
and the feudal lords all offer congratulations.
The humble ruler of our meager state also privately rejoiced in it
and did not dare to rest in peace;
he sent his subordinate ministers to bring ritual gifts to Your Majesty’s court three times,
yet the envoys were not granted access.
If the envoys are without fault,
we hope Your Majesty will not cut off our friendship;
if the envoys have faults,
we hope to be informed of them."
The King of Qín sent a messenger to report, saying:
"Regarding those whom I send orders to in the state of Zhào,
if everyone, great and small, obeys my words,
then I will accept the letter and gifts.
If they do not follow my words,
then the envoys may return."
Liàng Yì replied:
"Your humble servant’s coming
was surely with the wish to receive the great state’s intentions;
how would I dare to raise difficulties?
If Your Majesty has any commands,
I request to receive them and carry them out as I travel west,
without daring to have any doubts."
Thereupon the King of Qín granted an audience to the envoy
and said:
"Zhào Bào and Píngyuán Jūn
have several times deceived and trifled with me.
If Zhào can kill these two men,
then it will be fine.
If you cannot kill them,
then I request to lead the feudal lords to receive your orders under the walls of Hǎndān."
Liàng Yì said:
"Zhào Bào and Píngyuán Jūn
are the younger brothers of our ruler’s own mother,
just as Your Majesty has Yèyáng Jūn and Jīngyáng Jūn.
Your Majesty is known throughout the world for governing by filial piety.
You make their clothes comfortable for their bodies,
and their food satisfying to their mouths;
you have never failed to share such things with Yèyáng Jūn and Jīngyáng Jūn.
The carriages, horses, clothes, and furs of Yèyáng Jūn and Jīngyáng Jūn
are all like those of Your Majesty’s own use.
Your servant has heard:
'If nests are overturned and eggs are broken,
the Fènghuáng will not soar;
if wombs are ripped open and the young are burned,
the Qílín will not arrive.'
Now if your servant receives Your Majesty’s command and returns to report it,
the ruler of our humble state,
being fearful, would not dare to not carry it out,
but would this not wound the hearts of Yèyáng Jūn
and Jīngyáng Jūn?"
The King of Qín said:
"Granted.
Do not let them participate in government."
Liàng Yì said:
"The ruler of our humble state
has younger brothers from his own mother whom he could not instruct,
thereby offending your great state.
He requests to dismiss them,
not letting them participate in government affairs,
so as to satisfy your great state."
The King of Qín was then pleased;
he accepted the gifts and treated the envoy with great hospitality.
Zhào sent Yáo Jiǎ to form a treaty with Hán and Wèi,
and Hán and Wèi befriended him.
Jǔ Máo, on behalf of Yáo Jiǎ, said to the King of Zhào:
"Jiǎ
is a loyal minister of the King.
Hán and Wèi want to get him,
so they befriend him,
intending to make the King banish him,
so they can then take him in.
Now if the King banishes him,
this is what Hán and Wèi desire,
and the King’s loyal minister will be wrongly blamed.
Therefore, it is better for the King not to banish him,
to demonstrate the King’s wisdom
and to thwart Hán and Wèi’s attempts to recruit him."
Wèi defeated Chǔ at Jīngshān,
capturing Táng Míng.
The King of Chǔ was afraid
and ordered Zhāo Yìng to escort the Crown Prince to offer peace to Xué Gōng.
Zhǔfù wanted to sabotage this,
so he formed an alliance between Qín, Chǔ, and Sòng,
appointing Qiú Hǎo as Prime Minister of Sòng
and Lóu Huǎn as Prime Minister of Qín.
The King of Chǔ gained the support of Zhào and Sòng,
and the peace settlement of Wèi was finally defeated.
Qín summoned the Marquis of Chūnpíng
and subsequently detained him.
Shì Jūn spoke to the Marquis of Wènxìn on his behalf, saying:
"The Marquis of Chūnpíng
is someone the King of Zhào dearly loves,
but the palace attendants are very jealous of him,
so they plotted together, saying:
'If the Marquis of Chūnpíng enters Qín,
Qín will surely detain him.'
Thus they conspired to have him enter Qín.
Now if you retain him,
you will simply be severing ties with Zhào for nothing,
while the plot of the palace attendants succeeds.
Therefore, it would be better for you to send back the Marquis of Chūnpíng and instead detain the Marquis of Píngdū.
The words and actions of the Marquis of Chūnpíng carry weight with the King of Zhào;
he will surely cede much of Zhào territory to serve you
and redeem the Marquis of Píngdū."
The Marquis of Wènxìn said:
"Good."
He then reached an understanding with him and sent him back.
The Queen Dowager of Zhào had newly taken power
when Qín launched an urgent attack.
The house of Zhào sought help from Qí.
Qí said:
"The Lord of Cháng'ān must be sent as a hostage
before our troops will set out."
The Queen Dowager refused,
even as the ministers strongly remonstrated.
The Queen Dowager explicitly told her attendants:
"If anyone mentions again sending the Lord of Cháng'ān as a hostage,
I, this old woman, will certainly spit in his face."
The Left Minister Chù Zhé requested to see the Queen Dowager.
The Queen Dowager awaited him with a fierce expression.
He entered and walked with short, quick steps,
reaching her and apologizing,
saying:
"Your old servant has a leg ailment
and cannot walk fast,
so I have not seen you for a long time.
I privately excused myself,
but I feared that the Queen Dowager’s health might have some ailment,
so I wished to see the Queen Dowager."
The Queen Dowager said: "I rely on a carriage to get about."
He asked:
"Has your daily intake of food and drink decreased at all?"
She said:
"I rely only on congee."
He said:
"Your old servant lately has quite a lack of appetite,
so I force myself to walk,
three or four lǐ a day,
which slightly increases my appetite
and harmonizes my body."
The Queen Dowager said: "I cannot do that."
The Queen Dowager’s expression softened slightly.
The Left Minister Gōng said: "Your old servant’s humble son Shū Qí
is the youngest and is quite worthless.
Since I am declining, I privately cherish and pity him.
I wish to have him included in the ranks of the black-robed guards
to protect the royal palace;
I risk death to submit this request."
The Queen Dowager said: "I respectfully agree.
How old is he?"
He replied: "Fifteen years old.
Although he is young,
I wish to entrust him to your care before I fill the ditches and ravines."
The Queen Dowager asked:
"Does a man also cherish and pity his youngest son?"
He replied: "More than a woman does."
The Queen Dowager laughed and said:
"Women are quite extreme in this regard."
He replied:
"Your old servant privately thinks that your love for the Queen of Yàn exceeds that for the Lord of Cháng'ān."
She said:
"You are mistaken;
it is not as great as my love for the Lord of Cháng'ān."
The Left Minister Gōng said:
"When parents love their children,
they plan for them with long-term foresight.
When you sent off the Queen of Yàn,
you held her heels and wept for her,
mourning the sorrow of her distance;
it was truly sorrowful.
Once she had departed,
it wasn't that you didn't miss her,
but during sacrifices you would certainly pray for her,
saying: 'Please do not let her return.'
Was this not planning for the long term,
so that her descendants would follow one another as kings?"
The Queen Dowager said: "It is so."
The Left Minister Gōng said:
"From three generations ago
back to the very founding of Zhào,
of those descendants of the Zhào rulers who were enfeoffed as marquises,
are there any whose succession still survives?"
She said: "None."
He said:
"Is it only in Zhào?
Among the various feudal lords, are there any whose descendants are still there?"
She said:
"I have not heard of any."
"This is because those near in time suffer disaster in their own persons,
and those distant suffer it in their descendants.
Is it because the descendants of rulers are necessarily unworthy?
No, it is because they hold high positions without merit,
receive generous stipends without labor,
and possess many precious treasures.
Now you have elevated the Lord of Cháng'ān's position,
enfeoffed him with fertile lands,
and given him many precious treasures,
yet you do not take this opportunity to let him gain merit for the state.
Once the mountain and hills collapse,
how will the Lord of Cháng'ān establish himself in Zhào?
I believe your plan for the Lord of Cháng'ān is short-sighted,
which is why I think your love for him is not as great as for the Queen of Yàn."
The Queen Dowager said: "I agree.
I leave it to you to send him where you will."
Thereupon, she prepared a hundred chariots for the Lord of Cháng'ān to go as a hostage to Qí,
and the troops of Qí then set out.
Zǐyì heard of this and said:
"Even a son of a ruler,
a close blood relative,
still cannot rely on high position without merit,
or stipends without labor,
to preserve the weight of gold and jade;
how much less so for a common official?"
Qín sent Wáng Jiǎn to attack Zhào,
and Zhào sent Lǐ Mù and Sīmǎ Shàng to resist him.
Lǐ Mù repeatedly defeated and drove back the Qín army,
killing the Qín general Huán Yǐ.
Wáng Jiǎn loathed him,
so he gave much gold to the King of Zhào's favored officials such as Guō Kāi,
making them act as double agents
by saying:
"Lǐ Mù and Sīmǎ Shàng want to betray Zhào to Qín
to obtain many fiefs from Qín."
The King of Zhào suspected them,
so he sent Zhào Cōng and Yán Zuì to replace them in command,
executed Lǐ Mù,
and dismissed Sīmǎ Shàng.
Three months later,
Wáng Jiǎn took advantage of this to attack swiftly,
heavily defeating Zhào,
annihilating the Zhào army,
and capturing the King of Zhào, Qiān, and his general Yán Zuì,
thus destroying Zhào.
Zhì Bó demanded land from Wèi Huánzǐ,
but Wèi Huánzǐ would not give it.
Rèn Zhāng said: "For what reason do you not give it?"
Huánzǐ said: "He demands land for no reason,
so I will not give it."
Rèn Zhāng said:
"Demanding land for no reason
will surely make neighboring states afraid;
having heavy desires without being satisfied
will surely make the world fearful.
If you give him the land,
Zhì Bó will certainly become arrogant.
Being arrogant, he will underestimate his enemies,
while the neighboring states will become fearful and draw closer to each other.
By using troops who are close and affectionate
to face a state that underestimates its enemies,
one knows that the life of the Zhì clan will not be long!
The *Zhōu Shū* says:
"If you wish to defeat them,
you must first assist them;
if you wish to take from them,
you must first give to them."
It is better for Your Lordship to give to him,
so as to make Zhì Bó arrogant.
Why would Your Lordship pass up the chance to plot against the Zhì clan with the rest of the world,
and instead alone make our state a hostage for the Zhì clan?"
The Lord said: "Excellent."
He then gave him a city of ten thousand households.
Zhì Bó was greatly pleased.
Consequently, he demanded Cài and Gāoliáng from Zhào.
Zhào would not give them,
so he besieged Jìnyáng.
Hàn and Wèi revolted from the outside,
and the Zhào clan responded from within;
thus the Zhì clan perished.
Hàn and Zhào had a conflict with each other.
Hàn requested troops from Wèi, saying:
"I wish to borrow an army to attack Zhào."
Wèi Wén Hóu said: "I am like a brother to Zhào,
so I dare not comply."
Zhào again requested troops to attack Hàn.
Wén Hóu said: "I am like a brother to Hàn,
so I dare not comply."
The two states did not obtain troops,
and they returned in anger.
Later, they realized that Wén Hóu had brokered peace for them,
and they both paid court to Wèi.
Lè Yáng served as a general for Wèi and attacked Zhōngshān.
His son was in Zhōngshān.
The ruler of Zhōngshān cooked his son and sent him the soup.
Lè Yáng sat beneath his tent and drank it,
finishing a whole cup.
Wén Hóu said to Dǔshī Zàn:
"For my sake, Lè Yáng ate
his own son's flesh."
Zàn replied:
"If he would even eat his own son's flesh,
who then is there whose flesh he would not eat?"
After Lè Yáng had subdued Zhōngshān,
Wén Hóu rewarded his achievement but grew suspicious of his heart.
Xīmén Bào became the Magistrate of Yè,
and took his leave of Wèi Wén Hóu.
Wén Hóu said: "You are going;
you must accomplish your work
