the calamity will surely be a hundred times this.
In former days,
the Vertical Alliance was not successful
because Chǔ and Wèi were suspicious and Hán could not be brought into the treaty.
Now Hán has been under attack for three years;
Qín has harassed them into peace talks.
Hán knows it faces destruction,
yet it still does not listen;
they have sent hostages to Zhào
and requested to lead the world in a battle formation to blunt the enemy’s blades.
From my point of view,
Chǔ and Zhào will surely join them in the attack.
Why is this?
Because they all know that Qín’s greed is boundless,
and unless they destroy all the world's armies
and subjugate the people within the four seas,
they will surely not stop.
Therefore, I wish to serve Your Majesty in this matter;
Your Majesty should quickly accept the treaty with Chǔ and Zhào
and take hostages from Hán and Wèi,
making the preservation of Hán your primary objective.
Then seek your former lands from Hán,
and Hán will surely surrender them.
In this way, the soldiers and people will not be exhausted, yet the former lands will be regained;
the merit of this is greater than attacking Hán together with Qín,
and it avoids the calamity of being neighbors with a powerful Qín.
"To preserve Hán, secure Wèi, and benefit the world—
this is also a great opportunity for Your Majesty.
Connect Hán’s Shàngdǎng to Gòng and Mò;
once the road is open,
then establish a pass there
and tax those who enter and exit.
This is how Wèi can hold Hán hostage through its Shàngdǎng territory.
Sharing in these taxes
is enough to enrich the state.
Hán will surely be grateful to Wèi, love Wèi, respect Wèi, and fear Wèi;
Hán will surely not dare to rebel against Wèi.
Hán will be like a county of Wèi.
If Wèi gains Hán as a county,
then Wèi, Dàliáng, and Héwài will surely be secure.
Now if Hán is not preserved,
then the two Zhōu will surely be in danger,
and Ānlíng will surely be lost.
Chǔ and Zhào will be greatly defeated,
Wèi and Qí will be terrified,
the whole world will turn westward and gallop toward Qín,
and the day they enter the court to become subjects will not be far off."
Lord Yèyáng made an agreement with Wèi,
and the King of Wèi was about to enfeoff his son.
Someone said to the King of Wèi:
"Your Majesty once personally crossed the Zhāng river
to pay homage at Hándān,
offering Gě, Bì, Yīn, and Chéng to be Zhào’s sustenance towns,
yet Zhào has done nothing for Your Majesty in return.
Can Your Majesty now also enfeoff his son at Wènyáng and Gūyī?
I believe Your Majesty should not do this."
The King of Wèi then stopped.
Qín sent Zhào to attack Wèi.
Someone from Wèi said to the King of Zhào:
"Attacking Wèi
is the beginning of the destruction of Zhào.
In the past,
the people of Jìn wished to destroy Yú and thus attacked Guó.
Attacking Guó
was the beginning of the destruction of Yú.
Therefore, Xún Xī used horses and jade to request safe passage through Yú.
Gōng Zhīqí remonstrated, but his advice was not heard,
and passage was ultimately granted to Jìn.
The people of Jìn attacked Guó,
and on their return, they seized Yú.
Thus, the Chūnqiū records this
to blame Duke Yú.
Now, no state is stronger than Zhào,
and it rivals Qí and Qín.
Your Majesty is worthy, and a man of great reputation serves as your minister.
Therefore, the one who is considered a disease of the heart and soul is Zhào.
Wèi
is to Zhào what Guó was to Yú;
Zhào
is to Wèi what Yú was to Guó.
To listen to Qín and attack Wèi
is to act as Yú did.
I hope Your Majesty will consider this carefully."
The Crown Prince of Wèi was in Chǔ.
Someone said to Lóuzǐ at Yānlíng:
"You must wait for Qí and Chǔ to unite
in order to save Píshì.
Now, based on the principles of Qí and Chǔ,
they will surely not unite.
That man Dízi’s dislike within the state
is directed at you.
Those people all want to unite Qí and Qín, excluding Chǔ to belittle you.
You must say to the King of Qí:
'Wèi’s being under attack
was not because Qín actually initiated the invasion;
it is because Chǔ hates that Wèi serves Your Majesty;
therefore they encouraged Qín to attack Wèi.'
The King of Qí originally wanted to attack Chǔ,
and now he is further enraged that they are not on good terms with him;
he will surely order Wèi to yield land to Qín and make peace.
With Zhāngzi’s power
and the weight of Qín and Hán behind him,
the King of Qí dislikes him,
and the King of Wèi dares not rely on him.
Now, with the weight of Qí and Qín
excluding Chǔ to belittle you,
I am concerned for you.
Since giving up land to make peace with Qín is the same in either case,
why not do it through Chǔ?
Qín is rapidly attacking Chǔ;
if Chǔ withdraws its troops,
the King of Wèi will surely be afraid.
You should then use the opportunity to offer Fénběi to Qín and make peace,
uniting in friendship to isolate Qí.
Qín and Chǔ will then value you,
and you will surely become the Prime Minister.
I suspect that the King of Qín and Chūlǐ Jí also desire this;
allow me to speak to them on your behalf."
He then requested Chūlǐzǐ, saying:
"Attacking Píshì
is the King’s primary objective,
but if it cannot be captured,
the world will look down on Qín.
Furthermore, possessing Píshì
is advantageous for attacking Hán and Wèi."
Chūlǐzǐ said:
"I have already reached an agreement with Wèi;
there is no use for it."
He replied:
"I wish to express my humble thoughts to you;
please do not take offense.
Possessing Píshì
is of great benefit to the state,
yet you gave it to Wèi.
You ultimately believed yourself unable to defend it,
so you gave it to Wèi.
Now that your strength is more than sufficient to defend it,
for what reason do you not possess it?"
Chūlǐ Zǐ said:
“What should be done?”
(The reply) said:
“What the King of Wèi (Wèi Wáng) relies on
are Qí and Chǔ;
those he employs
are the powerful Lóu and Zhái Qiáng.
Now the King of Qí (Qí Wáng) says to the King of Wèi:
‘Your talk of wanting to negotiate is merely a pretext for attacking the troops of the King of Qí;
therefore, I will not come to your rescue.’
The King of Chǔ (Chǔ Wáng) is angry that the King of Wèi does not use Lóu Zǐ,
and instead sends Zhái Qiáng to make peace;
thus resentment has already cut them off.
The King of Wèi's fear is that he sees his own downfall;
Zhái Qiáng wants to unite Qí and Qín while excluding Chǔ,
in order to diminish Lóu;
Lóu wants to unite Qín and Chǔ while excluding Qí,
in order to diminish Zhái Qiáng.
You would be better off delaying Wèi's peace negotiations
and sending someone to say to Lóu Zǐ:
‘Can you give us Fénběi?
We request to unite with Chǔ and exclude Qí
to increase your importance;
this is our task.’
Lóu Zǐ and the King of Chǔ will certainly move quickly.
Then say to Zhái Zǐ:
‘Can you give us Fénběi?
We will certainly unite with Qí and exclude Chǔ
to increase your importance.’
Zhái Qiáng and the King of Qí will certainly move quickly.
In this way, externally you will gain the use of Qí and Chǔ,
and internally you will gain Lóu Zhì and Zhái Qiáng as your assistants;
for what reason then could you not possess land in Hédōng?”
A letter was presented to the King of Qín (Qín Wáng) saying:
“In the past, I secretly heard that Your Majesty planned to launch a military operation against Liáng;
I fear this plan did not arise from sound strategy,
and I hope Your Majesty will consider it thoroughly.
Liáng
is the strategic key to Shāndōng.
Suppose there is a snake here:
if you strike its tail,
its head comes to the rescue;
if you strike its head,
its tail comes to the rescue;
if you strike its middle body, both head and tail come to the rescue.
Now the King of Liáng (Liáng Wáng)
is the middle body of All-Under-Heaven.
For Qín to attack Liáng
is to show the world that you intend to sever the spine of Shāndōng;
this is the time when the head and tail of Shāndōng will both rescue the middle body.
When Shāndōng sees its destruction is imminent, they will certainly be afraid;
when afraid, they will certainly form a great alliance.
Since Shāndōng is still strong,
I see that Qín's great sorrow is a certainty that can be expected immediately.
I have secretly planned for Your Majesty;
it would be better to go south.
Launch a military operation in the south;
their troops are weak,
the rest of the world will not be able to rescue them,
territory can be expanded,
the state can be enriched,
the military can be strengthened,
and the ruler can be honored.
Has Your Majesty not heard of Tāng's campaign against Jié?
He first tested the weak Mìxū Shì to use as a military exercise;
by gaining the territory of Mìxū Shì, Tāng then subdued Jié.
Now the State of Qín and Shāndōng are enemies.
If you do not first use the weak as a military exercise,
your army will certainly suffer a great setback,
and the state will certainly face great sorrow.”
Qín indeed attacked Lántián, Yān, and Yǐng to the south.
In the eighth year,
someone said to the King of Wèi (Wèi Wáng):
“In the past, Cáo relied on Qí and treated Jìn lightly;
Qí attacked Lí and Jǔ, and the people of Jìn destroyed Cáo.
Zēng relied on Qí to defy Yuè;
Qí's Hézǐ caused internal chaos, and the people of Yuè destroyed Zēng.
Zhèng relied on Wèi to treat Hán lightly;
while attacking Yúguān, the Hán clan destroyed Zhèng.
Yuán relied on Qín and Zhái to treat Jìn lightly;
Qín and Zhái suffered a major crop failure, and the people of Jìn destroyed Yuán.
Zhōngshān relied on Qí and Wèi to treat Zhào lightly;
Qí and Wèi attacked Chǔ, and Zhào destroyed Zhōngshān.
The reason these five states perished
was all because of what they relied on.
It is not only these five states for whom this is true;
all the fallen states of the world were like this.
There are many reasons why a state cannot be relied upon,
and their changes are too numerous to count.
Some are because administration and education are not cultivated,
and those above and below are not in harmony,
making them unreliable;
some are because of the worries caused by feudal lords and neighboring states,
making them unreliable;
some are because crops do not grow
and reserves are exhausted,
making them unreliable;
some are changed by profit
or associate with calamity.
From this, I know that states cannot be relied upon with certainty.
Now Your Majesty relies on Chǔ's strength
and trusts the words of Lord Chūnshēn (Chūnshēn Jūn);
you use this as a pledge to Qín,
but for how long it will last is unknown.
If Lord Chūnshēn undergoes a change,
then Your Majesty alone will suffer the calamity from Qín.
Even if Your Majesty has a state of ten thousand chariots,
you are placing your life in the heart of one man.
I consider this to be unsound,
and I hope Your Majesty will consider it thoroughly.”
The King of Wèi (Wèi Wáng) asked Zhāng Máo:
“I wish to attack Hán with Qín, how about it?”
Zhāng Máo replied: “Will Hán just sit and wait for destruction?
Or will it cede territory and follow the rest of the world?”
The King said:
“Hán will cede territory and follow the rest of the world.”
Zhāng Máo said:
“Does Hán resent Wèi?
Or does it resent Qín?”
The King said:
“It resents Wèi.”
Zhāng Máo said:
“Does Hán consider Qín stronger?
Or Wèi stronger?”
The King said:
“It considers Qín stronger.”
Zhāng Máo said:
“Will Hán cede territory and follow the one it considers stronger
and whom it does not resent?
Or will it cede territory and follow the one it does not consider stronger
and whom it resents?”
The King said:
“Hán will cede territory and follow the one it considers stronger
and whom it does not resent.”
Zhāng Máo said:
“Regarding the matter of attacking Hán,
Your Majesty knows the answer yourself.”
A guest said to Sīmǎ Yìqí:
“One who has long thought that the world can be unified
is one who does not know the world.
One who wishes to rely solely on Wèi to support Qín
is one who does not know Wèi.
One who says Lord Zī (Zī Gōng) does not know these two things
is one who does not know Lord Zī.
However, Lord Zī advocates for the Vertical Alliance;
what is his reasoning?
If the Alliance is formed, then Lord Zī is important;
if the Alliance is not formed, then Lord Zī is insignificant.
As for Lord Zī's position of importance,
there is no real guarantee for its duration.
Why do you not quickly, while the three states are still firm in their stance,
sell yourself to Qín?
Qín will certainly accept you.
Otherwise,
those of the Horizontal Alliance will use you to reach an agreement with Qín;
this would be taking your resources
to benefit your enemy.”
Wèi and Qín were to attack Chǔ,
but the King of Wèi (Wèi Wáng) did not wish to.
Lóu Huǎn said to the King of Wèi:
“If Your Majesty does not attack Chǔ with Qín,
Chǔ will then attack Your Majesty with Qín.
It is better for Your Majesty to let Qín and Chǔ fight,
while Your Majesty controls them through diplomacy.”
The Marquis of Ráng (Ráng Hóu) attacked Dàliáng
and reached Běiyǐng;
the King of Wèi (Wèi Wáng) was about to submit.
Someone said to the Marquis of Ráng:
“When you attacked Chǔ and gained Wǎn and Ráng to expand Táo,
when you attacked Qí and gained Gāng and Bó to expand Táo,
and when you gained Xǔ and Yānlíng to expand Táo,
the King of Qín did not question it.
Why?
Because Dàliáng had not yet fallen.
If Dàliáng falls today,
Xǔ and Yānlíng will certainly be scrutinized;
once they are scrutinized, you will certainly be in a desperate situation.
In planning for you,
it is more convenient not to attack.”
Bái Guī said to the Lord of Xīnchéng (Xīnchéng Jūn):
“A night traveler can refrain from doing evil,
but he cannot prevent a dog from barking at him.
Likewise, I can refrain from speaking ill of you to the King,
but I cannot prevent others from speaking ill of me to you.”
Qín attacked Guǎn in Hán,
and the King of Wèi dispatched troops to rescue it.
Zhāo Jì said:
"Now Qín is a powerful state,
and Hán and Wèi both border Liáng.
If they do not come out to attack, then that is one thing;
but if they do come out to attack,
if it is not against Hán, it will certainly be against Wèi.
Now, fortunately, it is against Hán;
this is Wèi's good fortune.
If Your Majesty rescues them,
the one who is relieved of the attack
will certainly be Hán's Guǎn;
the one who attracts the attack
will certainly be Wèi's Liáng."
The King of Wèi did not listen,
saying:
"If I do not take this opportunity to rescue Hán,
Hán will resent Wèi;
they will join Qín in the west,
and if Qín and Hán become one,
then Wèi will be in danger."
He then rescued them.
As expected, Qín abandoned Guǎn and attacked Wèi.
The King of Wèi was greatly terrified
and said to Zhāo Jì:
"I did not use your plan and disaster has arrived.
What should be done about it?"
Zhāo Jì then went to see the King of Qín on his behalf and said:
"I have heard that when an enlightened ruler listens,
he does not conduct government based on personal grudges;
this is to act with broad observation.
I wish for Your Great Majesty not to attack Wèi,
and to listen to me."
The King of Qín said:
"Why is that?"
Zhāo Jì said:
"The Cóng alliance of Shāndōng
sometimes joins and sometimes separates;
why is that?"
The King of Qín said:
"I do not know."
Zhāo Jì said:
"The reason the world unites
is because Your Majesty's [actions] are not certain;
the reason they separate
is because Your Majesty's [actions] are certain.
Now you attack Hán's Guǎn;
that state is in danger.
Before finishing that, you move your troops to Liáng.
To unite the Cóng alliance of the world,
there is no better way than this.
It will be thought that Qín's demands
will surely be unbearable.
Therefore, in planning for Your Majesty,
nothing is better than dealing with Qí and Zhào.
Once Qín has controlled Zhào,
then Yān will not dare not to serve Qín,
and Jīng and Qí cannot form the Cóng alliance alone.
When the whole world competes to be the enemy of Qín,
then Qín is weakened."
The King of Qín then stopped.
Qín and Zhào had a conflict and fought.
[Someone] said to the King of Wèi:
"It is better to reconcile Qí and Zhào with Qín.
If Your Majesty does not reconcile Zhào,
Zhào will not seek reconciliation through its own destruction;
but if you reconcile them with Qín,
Zhào will certainly fight again
and will certainly value Wèi;
this is a matter of controlling both Qín and Zhào.
If Your Majesty wishes to win over Qí and Zhào to attack Jīng,
or if you wish to win over Jīng and Zhào to attack Qí,
you must wait for the outcome in the east."
During the campaign of Chángpíng,
Píngdū Jūn persuaded the King of Wèi, saying:
"Why does Your Majesty not join the Cóng alliance?"
The King of Wèi said:
"Qín has promised me Yuányōng."
Píngdū Jūn said:
"I consider Yuányōng to be an empty cession."
The King of Wèi said:
"What do you mean?"
Píngdū Jūn said:
"Qín and Zhào have long held each other at bay below Chángpíng without a resolution.
If the world joins with Qín,
then there will be no Zhào;
if they join with Zhào,
then there will be no Qín.
Qín fears Your Majesty's change of heart,
so they use Yuányōng as bait for Your Majesty.
If Qín wins the battle against Zhào,
would Your Majesty dare to demand the cession of Yuányōng?"
The King said,
"I would not dare."
"If Qín does not win the battle against Zhào,
can Your Majesty command Hán to give up the cession of Yuányōng?"
The King said,
"I cannot."
"Therefore I said,
Yuányōng is an empty cession."
The King of Wèi said:
"Excellent."
Lóu Wú made an agreement between Qín and Wèi
and was about to have the King of Qín meet [the King of Wèi] at the border.
He said to the King of Wèi:
"If you meet without a Chancellor,
Qín will certainly appoint a Chancellor for you.
If you do not listen to them,
then relations with Qín will sour;
if you do listen to them,
then in the future Your Majesty's ministers
will all strive to serve those capable of commanding from above Your Majesty among the feudal lords.
Furthermore, to meet with Qín and have Qín appoint the Chancellor
is to have no Qí,
and Qín will surely belittle Your Majesty's strength.
Since you have Qí,
it is better to appoint [a person from Qí] as Chancellor;
Qí will surely be pleased.
Thus, to meet with Qín while having Yōng,
Qín will surely value Your Majesty."
Ruì Sòng wished to break the diplomatic relations between Qín and Zhào,
so he had the Wèi clan reclaim the support-lands of the Qín Queen Dowager from the King of Qín in Qín.
Ruì Sòng said to the King of Qín:
"Wèi entrusted its state to Your Majesty,
but Your Majesty did not accept it;
therefore they entrusted the state to Zhào.
Lǐ Hǎo said to me:
'You say there is no Qín,
yet you support the Queen Dowager of Qín with land;
this is deceiving me.
Therefore our humble city has taken it back.'"
The King of Qín was angry
and subsequently broke relations with Zhào.
On behalf of Wèi, [someone] said to the King of Chǔ:
"If you seek to attack Wèi through Qín,
Qín will surely not listen to Your Majesty.
This would mean your wisdom is confounded by Qín,
and your relations with Wèi will become distant.
If Chǔ and Wèi have resentment,
then Qín becomes powerful.
Therefore it is better for Your Majesty to follow the world,
then attack Qí,
and arrange for convenient lands with Wèi.
Your troops will not be harmed,
your relations will not change,
and what you desire will surely be obtained."
Guǎn Bí ordered Zhái Qiáng to handle matters with Qín
and said to the King of Wèi:
"Bí and Qiáng
are like the people of Jìn and the people of Chǔ.
When the people of Jìn saw the people of Chǔ were in a hurry,
they wore their swords and slowed down;
the people of Chǔ disliked their slowness and hurried them.
Now if Bí enters the guesthouse of Qín,
the guesthouse would not be enough to house him.
When Qiáng enters,
there is no one in Qín to shield him.
Qiáng
is Your Majesty's honored minister,
yet Qín treats him with such severity;
how can this be allowed?"
Chéngyáng Jūn wished for Hán and Wèi to follow Qín,
which the King of Wèi did not find beneficial.
Bái Guī said to the King of Wèi:
"It would be better for Your Majesty to secretly have someone persuade Chéngyáng Jūn, saying:
'If you enter Qín,
Qín will surely detain you
and demand more land from Hán.
If Hán does not listen,
Qín will surely detain you
and attack Hán.
Therefore it is better for you to travel safely and seek a hostage from Qín.'
Chéngyáng Jūn will surely not enter Qín;
then Qín and Hán will not dare to unite,
and Your Majesty will be valued."
Qín captured Níngyì,
and the King of Wèi ordered [someone] to say to the King of Qín:
"If Your Majesty returns Níngyì,
I request to be the first in the world to make a settlement."
[Someone] said to the King of Wèi:
"Your Majesty should not listen.
The King of Wèi sees that the world cannot be relied upon,
therefore he wishes to make a settlement first.
One who has lost Níng
should cede two Níngs to seek a settlement;
for one who has gained Níng,
how can he return Níng?"
Qín withdrew from Hándān,
attacked Wèi,
and took Nìngyì.
Wú Qìng feared that the King of Wèi would make peace with Qín,
and said to the King of Wèi:
“When Qín attacks Your Majesty,
do you know the reason?
Everyone says it is because Your Majesty is near.
Your Majesty is not near Qín;
it is Qín that has moved away.
Everyone says it is because Your Majesty is weak.
Your Majesty is not weaker than the two Zhōu.
The people of Qín left Hándān,
passed the two Zhōu and attacked Your Majesty
because they consider Your Majesty easy to control.
Does Your Majesty also know that weakness invites attack?”
The King of Wèi wanted to attack Hándān.
Jì Liáng heard of this,
returned mid-journey,
with his clothes creased and unpressed
and the dust on his head not removed.
He went to see the King and said:
“Today as I came,
I saw a man on the Dàxíng road
who was facing north while driving his carriage.
He told me:
‘I want to go to Chǔ.’
I said:
‘If you are going to Chǔ,
why are you facing north?’
He said: ‘My horse is excellent.’
I said:
‘Even if the horse is excellent,
this is not the road to Chǔ.’
He said:
‘My supplies are many.’
I said: ‘Even if your supplies are many,
this is not the road to Chǔ.’
He said:
‘My driver is skillful.’
The better these factors are,
the further you will be from Chǔ.
Now Your Majesty’s every move is to achieve hegemony,
and every action is to be trusted by the world.
Relying on the greatness of your kingdom
and the elite quality of your troops
to attack Hándān,
to expand territory and gain a great name,
the more frequent Your Majesty’s movements,
the further you will be from kingship.
It is just like going to Chǔ but traveling north.”
Zhōu Xiāo said to Gōng Tā:
“For my sake, say to the King of Qí
that Xiāo wishes to be his external official.
Let Qí support me in Wèi.”
Gōng Tā said: “That is not possible;
this would show Qí that you are unimportant.
Now, Qí does not use those who do not possess Wèi to harm those who do possess Wèi;
therefore, you would do better to show that you possess Wèi.
You should say:
‘Whatever the King seeks from Wèi,
I request to have Wèi comply.’
Then Qí will surely support you.
This way you will have Qí,
and by having Qí, you will have Wèi.”
Zhōu Zuì was on good terms with Qí,
and Zhái Qiáng was on good terms with Chǔ.
These two men
wished to harm Zhāng Yí in Wèi.
Zhāng Zǐ heard of this,
and so he had his man act as a steward for visitors to overhear what was said and seen.
Consequently, no one dared to harm Zhāng Zǐ.
Zhōu Zuì entered Qí.
The King of Qín was angry
and ordered Yáo Jiǎ to reprimand the King of Wèi.
The King of Wèi, on his behalf, said to the King of Qín:
“The reason Wèi communicates with the world for Your Majesty
is because of Zhōu Zuì.
Now that Zhōu Zuì has fled from me and entered Qí,
Qí will have no communication with the world.
In my humble state's service to Your Majesty,
I am also free from the burden of Qí.
If your great country wishes to use troops urgently,
then just hasten to Zhào.”
Qín and Wèi were allied states.
Qí and Chǔ made a pact and wanted to attack Wèi.
Wèi sent men to seek help from Qín;
their carriage covers were in sight of each other on the road,
but Qín’s rescue did not come.
There was a man of Wèi named Táng Qiě
who was over ninety years old.
He said to the King of Wèi:
“I, your old servant, request to go west to speak to Qín.
May I have the troops set out after me?”
The King of Wèi said: “I respectfully agree.”
Then he prepared a carriage and sent him.
Táng Qiě saw the King of Qín.
The King of Qín said:
“Venerable elder, you have come so far in such a state of exhaustion;
it must have been very hard on you.
Wèi has come to seek help many times,
and I know Wèi’s emergency.”
Táng Qiě replied:
“Since Your Majesty already knows Wèi’s emergency but the rescue has not arrived,
it means Your Majesty’s strategists are incompetent.
Furthermore, Wèi is a state of ten thousand chariots
that calls itself your eastern vassal,
receives your caps and belts,
and offers sacrifices in spring and autumn,
all because it believed Qín’s strength was sufficient to be an ally.
Now the troops of Qí and Chǔ are already at the borders of Wèi;
if Your Majesty’s rescue does not arrive
and Wèi is in desperation, it will cede land and make a pact with Qí and Chǔ.
Even if Your Majesty then wishes to rescue it,
how could you be in time?
This would be losing the Wèi of ten thousand chariots
and strengthening the two enemies, Qí and Chǔ.
I venture to think Your Majesty’s strategists are incompetent.”
The King of Qín sighed and realized his error,
and immediately dispatched troops, reaching Wèi day and night.
When Qí and Chǔ heard of this, they led their troops away.
That the state of Wèi was once again preserved was due to Táng Qiě’s persuasion.
Xìnlíng Jūn killed Jìn Bǐ,
saved Hándān,
defeated the people of Qín,
and preserved the state of Zhào.
The King of Zhào went to the suburbs in person to welcome him.
Táng Qiě said to Xìnlíng Jūn:
“I have heard it said:
‘There are things that cannot be known
and things that cannot not be known;
there are things that cannot be forgotten
and things that cannot but be forgotten.’”
Xìnlíng Jūn said:
“What do you mean?”
He replied:
“That others hate me
is something I cannot not know.
That I hate others
is something that should not be known by them.
That others have done me a kindness
is something I cannot forget.
That I have done a kindness to others
is something I cannot but forget.
Now you have killed Jìn Bǐ,
saved Hándān,
defeated the people of Qín,
and preserved the state of Zhào;
this is a great kindness.
Now the King of Zhào is welcoming you in the suburbs.
When you see the King of Zhào shortly,
I wish for you to forget your deed.”
Xìnlíng Jūn said:
“I, Wújì, respectfully accept your instruction.”
Wèi attacked Guǎn but could not take it.
Sù Gāo was a man of Ānlíng,
and his son was the defender of Guǎn.
Xìnlíng Jūn sent someone to say to the Lord of Ānlíng:
“If you send Sù Gāo to me,
I will appoint him to the rank of Wǔdàfū
and make him a Chíjié Wèi.”
The Lord of Ānlíng said: “Ānlíng
is a small state
and cannot command its people with certainty.
Let the messenger go himself.
I request to have a guide lead the messenger
to Sù Gāo’s place
to relay Xìnlíng Jūn’s command.”
Sù Gāo said:
“That the Lord favors me
is because he wants me to attack Guǎn.
For a father to attack what a son defends
would make people laugh.
If I were to submit to him,
I would be betraying my master.
For a father to teach his son to betray
is also not something the Lord would be pleased with.
I venture to bow twice and decline.”
The messenger reported this to Xìnlíng Jūn.
Xìnlíng Jūn was greatly enraged
and sent a high envoy to Ānlíng, saying:
“The land of Ānlíng
is just like Wèi.
Now I attack Guǎn and cannot take it;
then Qín’s troops will reach me,
and our altars of state will surely be in danger.
I wish for you to bind Sù Gāo alive and deliver him to me.
If you do not deliver him,
I, Wújì, will mobilize an army of one hundred thousand
to march upon the city of Ānlíng.”
Ānlíng Jūn said:
"My late lord Chéng Hóu
received the command of Xiāng Wáng
to guard this land,
and personally received the laws of the Great Treasury (Dàfǔ).
The first chapter of the laws says:
'If a son kills his father,
or a minister kills his ruler,
there is a constant rule of no pardon.
Even if the state grants a general amnesty,
those who surrender cities or fugitive sons may not be included.'
Now Sù Gāo has respectfully resigned from a high position
to preserve the righteousness between father and son,
yet you, my lord, say 'he must be brought here alive.'
This is to make me betray the command of Xiāng Wáng and discard the laws of the Great Treasury.
Even if I were to die, I would never dare to carry it out."
When Sù Gāo heard this, he said:
"Xìnlíng Jūn's character
is fierce and self-willed.
If this refusal is returned to him,
it will surely bring calamity to the state.
I have already preserved my own integrity,
but I have not fulfilled the righteousness of a minister.
How can I allow my lord to suffer trouble from Wèi?"
He then went to the messenger's quarters
and cut his throat to die.
When Xìnlíng Jūn heard of Sù Gāo's death,
he wore plain white mourning clothes and moved out of his quarters.
He sent a messenger to apologize to Ānlíng Jūn, saying:
"Wú Jì
is a petty person;
I was confused in my thinking
and spoke mistakenly to you, my lord.
I dare to bow twice to ask for release from my fault."
The King of Wèi (Wèi Wáng) was fishing in a boat with Lóngyáng Jūn.
Lóngyáng Jūn caught more than ten fish and began to shed tears.
The King said:
"Is there something bothering you?
If so,
why not tell me?"
He replied:
"I would not dare to be uneasy about anything."
The King said: "Then why are you crying?"
He said:
"I am crying because of the fish your Majesty has caught."
The King said: "What do you mean?"
He replied: "When I first caught a fish,
I was very happy.
Later, when I caught even larger ones,
I immediately wanted to discard the ones I had caught before. Now,
despite my lowly and ugly self,
I have been allowed to arrange your Majesty's pillows and mats.
Now my rank has reached that of a lord;
people scurry in my courtyard
and clear the way for me on the road.
Within the four seas,
beautiful people are very numerous;
hearing that I have gained favor with your Majesty,
they will surely lift their skirts and hasten to your Majesty.
I will then be like the fish I caught earlier;
I too will be discarded.
How could I not shed tears?"
The King of Wèi said: "You are mistaken!
If you have such feelings,
why not tell me?"
Thereupon, he issued an order throughout the four borders, saying:
"Anyone who dares to mention beautiful people shall have their clan executed."
From this perspective,
those close to the ruler
are indeed firm in their flattery and fawning;
their self-preservation is complete.
Now, from a thousand lǐ away,
if one wishes to present a beautiful person,
is it certain that the person presented will gain favor?
Even if they gain favor,
is it certain they will be useful to me?
Meanwhile, the close attendants will harbor resentment against each other.
I see calamity,
but I do not see blessing;
I see resentment, but I do not see virtue.
This is not the technique of using wisdom.
Qín attacked Wèi urgently.
Someone said to the King of Wèi (Wèi Wáng):
"Discarding land is not as easy as using it;
dying for it is not as easy as discarding it.
To be able to discard it but not be able to use it,
or to be able to die for it but not be able to discard it—
these are great errors for a person.
Now your Majesty has lost hundreds of lǐ of land
and dozens of cities,
yet the state's troubles are not resolved.
This is your Majesty discarding them,
not using them.
Now Qín's strength
is matchless in the world,
while Wèi's weakness is extreme.
Yet your Majesty uses the state to confront Qín.
Your Majesty is able to die for it but unable to discard it;
this is a double error.
If your Majesty can now use my plan,
diminishing the land will not be enough to harm the state,
and humbling your position will not be enough to distress your person;
you will resolve the trouble and be avenged."
"Within the four borders of Qín,
from the law officials down to the laborers,
everyone is asking:
'Are you with the Lào clan
or with the Lǚ clan?'
Even from the gates of humble alleys
to the halls of the ancestral temples,
it is like this.
Now if your Majesty carves out land to bribe Qín,
let it be credited as the achievement of Lào Ài;
humble yourself to honor Qín,
and do so by following Lào Ài.
If your Majesty supports Lào Ài with your state,
Lào Ài will prevail.
If your Majesty supports the Lào clan with your state,
the Queen Mother (Tàihòu) will be grateful to your Majesty
to the very marrow of her bones.
Your Majesty's relationship will become the highest in the world.
Qín and Wèi have formed alliances a hundred times,
and have deceived each other a hundred times.
Now, by using the Lào clan to befriend Qín and making the alliance the best in the world,
who in the world would not abandon the Lǚ clan to follow the Lào clan?
When the world unites against the Lǚ clan to follow the Lào clan,
then your Majesty's resentment will be avenged."
The King of Qín (Qín Wáng) sent someone to say to Ānlíng Jūn:
"I wish to exchange five hundred lǐ of land for Ānlíng.
Will Ānlíng Jūn grant this to me?"
Ānlíng Jūn said: "The Great King bestows a favor
by exchanging a large territory for a small one;
it is very good.
However, I received this land from the former lord
and wish to guard it to the end;
I do not dare to exchange it."
The King of Qín was not pleased.
Ānlíng Jūn then sent Táng Qiě as an envoy to Qín.
The King of Qín said to Táng Qiě:
"I offered five hundred lǐ of land to exchange for Ānlíng,
but Ānlíng Jūn did not listen to me.
Why?
Furthermore, Qín has extinguished Hán and destroyed Wèi,
yet your lord survives with fifty lǐ of land
because I consider him an elder
and thus have not set my mind on him.
Now I offer ten times the land
to expand your lord's territory,
yet your lord opposes me.
Does he belittle me?"
Táng Qiě replied: "No,
it is not like that.
Ānlíng Jūn received the land from the former lord and guards it;
even for a thousand lǐ, he would not dare to exchange it,
much less just five hundred lǐ."
The King of Qín was furious
and said to Táng Qiě:
"Have you ever heard of the wrath of the Son of Heaven?"
Táng Qiě replied:
"I have never heard of it."
The King of Qín said:
"The wrath of the Son of Heaven
causes a million corpses to lie on the ground
and blood to flow for a thousand lǐ."
Táng Qiě said:
"Has your Majesty ever heard of the wrath of a commoner?"
The King of Qín said:
"The wrath of a commoner
is merely taking off one's cap and going barefoot,
and striking one's head against the ground."
Táng Qiě said:
"That is the wrath of a mediocre man,
not the wrath of a man of spirit. When Zhuān Zhū assassinated Wáng Liáo,
a comet struck the moon;
when Niè Zhèng assassinated Hán Kuǐ,
a white rainbow pierced the sun;
when Yào Lí assassinated Qìng Jì,
a blue hawk struck within the palace hall.
These three men
were all commoners of spirit;
before their wrath was unleashed,
omens of fortune and calamity descended from heaven.
With me, there shall now be four."
If a commoner is driven to rage,
two corpses will lie here
and blood will spill within five paces,
yet the whole world will wear white mourning clothes.
Today is such a day."
He drew his sword and rose.
The King of Qín’s (Qín Wáng) expression faltered,
and he knelt upright to apologize, saying,
"Sit down, Sir. Why come to this?
I understand now.
Even though Hán and Wèi have been destroyed,
the reason Ānlíng survives with only fifty lǐ of land
is solely because it has you, Sir."
After the Sān Jìn had defeated the Zhì lineage,
they were about to divide its territory.
Duàn Guī said to the King of Hán (Hán Wáng),
"In dividing the land, you must take Chénggāo."
The King of Hán said, "Chénggāo
is a place of rocky slopes;
I have no use for it."
Duàn Guī replied,
"Not so.
I have heard that a thickness of one lǐ
can shift the power of a thousand lǐ
because of geographical advantage.
A force of ten thousand men
can destroy three armies
because of the element of surprise.
If Your Majesty follows my words,
then Hán will surely take Zhèng."
The King said, "Excellent."
Consequently, he took Chénggāo.
When it came to Hán taking Zhèng,
it indeed began from Chénggāo.
Dàchéng Wǔ came from Zhào
and said to Shēn Bùhài in Hán,
"If you use Hán to enhance my prestige in Zhào,
I shall use Zhào to enhance your prestige in Hán;
thus you will have two Háns
and I will have two Zhàos."
When Wèi besieged Hándān,
Shēn Bùhài had just entered the service of the King of Hán,
but he did not yet know what the King desired
and feared that his words might not hit the mark with the King.
The King asked Shēn Zǐ,
"With whom should I side?"
He replied,
"This is the key to safety or peril
and a great matter for the state.
I beg to reflect deeply and ponder it with effort."
Then he secretly said to Zhào Zhuó and Hán Cháo,
"You are both the state's eloquent rhetoricians.
As ministers,
if your words are certain to be used,
it is merely a matter of exhausting your loyalty."
The two men each presented their arguments to the King regarding the matter.
Shēn Zǐ secretly observed what pleased the King and then spoke to him;
the King was greatly pleased with him.
Shēn Zǐ requested an official post for his elder cousin,
but Marquis Zhāo (Zhāo Hóu) would not permit it.
Shēn Zǐ showed a look of resentment.
Marquis Zhāo said,
"Is this not what I learned from you?
Should I grant your request
and thereby abandon your Way?
Or should I practice your methods
and thereby reject your request?
You once taught me to follow merit
and observe the order of precedence.
Now you have a request;
which of these should I listen to?"
Shēn Zǐ then withdrew from his quarters to ask for punishment,
saying,
"You are truly the right ruler!"
Sū Qín, forming a Vertical Alliance on behalf of Chǔ, persuaded the King of Hán, saying,
"To the north, Hán has the strongholds of Gǒng, Luò, and Chénggāo;
to the west, it has the passes of Yíyáng and Chángbǎn;
to the east, it has Wǎn, Rǎng, and the Wěi River;
to the south, it has Jìngshān.
Its territory is a thousand lǐ square,
with hundreds of thousands of armored soldiers.
The world's strongest bows and most powerful crossbows
all come from Hán.
The Xīzi, Shǎofǔ Shílì, and Jùlái bows
can all shoot beyond six hundred paces.
The soldiers of Hán can brace with their feet to fire,
shooting a hundred times without pause;
at a distance, they pierce the chest,
and nearby, they strike the heart.
The swords and halberds of Hán soldiers
all come from Míngshān, Tángxī, Mòyáng, and Gěbó.
Dèngshī, Wǎnfíng, Lóngyuān, and Tàì'ē blades
can cleave horses and oxen on land
and strike down swans and geese on water;
facing the enemy, they cut through solid armor.
Armor, shields, leather boots, helmets, iron curtains,
leather thumb rings, and yāoruì bow-guards
are all fully provided.
With the courage of Hán's soldiers,
wearing sturdy armor,
treading powerful crossbows,
and girding sharp swords,
for one man to match a hundred
is not even worth mentioning.
Now, with the strength of Hán
and Your Majesty’s virtue,
if you yet wish to face west and serve Qín,
calling yourself its eastern vassal,
building palaces for its Emperor,
receiving caps and belts from him,
performing sacrifices in the spring and autumn,
and folding your arms in submission;
to shame the state altars and be laughed at by the world,
nothing exceeds this.
Therefore, I wish Your Majesty would consider this maturely.
If Your Majesty serves Qín,
Qín will surely demand Yíyáng and Chénggāo.
If you hand them over now,
next year they will demand even more territory to be ceded.
If you give it,
then you will have no land left to give;
if you do not give it,
you will have wasted your previous efforts and will suffer their wrath later.
Furthermore, Your Majesty's land has a limit,
but Qín's demands have no end.
To meet endless demands
with limited land
is what is called 'trading for resentment and buying disaster';
without even fighting, your territory is already carved away.
I have heard a common saying:
'Better to be a chicken's beak
than a bull's backside.'
Now if Your Majesty faces west with arms folded to serve Qín as a subject,
how is this different from being a bull's backside?
Given Your Majesty's virtue
and the command of Hán's powerful army,
to yet have the reputation of a bull's backside,
I privately feel ashamed on Your Majesty's behalf."
The King of Hán's expression flared with anger;
he bared his arms and gripped his sword,
then sighed toward the heavens and said,
"Though I may die,
I certainly cannot serve Qín.
Now that you, Sir, have instructed me with the teachings of the King of Chǔ (Chǔ Wáng),
I respectfully offer my state to follow you."
Zhāng Yí, on behalf of Qín, spoke in favor of a Horizontal Alliance to the King of Hán, saying:
"The land of Hán is rugged and poor;
situated in the mountains,
the five grains grown there
are nothing but wheat and beans.
What the people eat
is mostly bean rice and pulse-leaf soup;
if there is one year without harvest,
the people cannot even get enough dregs and chaff.
Your territory is less than nine hundred lǐ square,
without even two years' worth of food.
Estimating Your Majesty's troops,
all told they do not exceed three hundred thousand,
and even the grooms and fodder-carriers
are included among them.
Subtracting those who guard the borders, outposts, and forts,
the actual troops are no more than two hundred thousand.
Qín has over a million armored soldiers,
a thousand chariots,
and ten thousand horses.
Brave warriors like tigers,
who jump into battle bareheaded,
piercing through enemies and brandishing halberds,
are too numerous to count.
The excellence of Qín's horses
and the multitude of its war machines
that leap forward and kick back,
covering three xún between strides,
are beyond numbering.
The soldiers of Shāndōng
wear armor and helmets to join the battle,
but the men of Qín discard their armor and go bare-chested to rush the enemy,
holding a severed head in the left hand
and carrying a live prisoner under the right arm.
Comparing Qín soldiers with Shāndōng soldiers
is like comparing Mèng Bèn to a coward;
to use their heavy weight to crush the opponent
is like Wū Huò compared to an infant.
Employing soldiers like Mèng Bèn and Wū Huò
to attack a weak and disobedient state
is no different from dropping a weight of a thousand jūn
onto a bird's egg;
there is certainly no chance of survival.
The feudal lords do not consider their soldiers' weakness
or their lack of food,
but instead listen to the sweet words and fine phrases of the Alliance-makers,
who form cliques to deceive one another,
all saying,
'Follow my plan, and you can become the hegemon of the world.'"
As for those who disregard the long-term interests of the Shèjì,
and listen to momentary rhetoric,
misleading the sovereign,
none are greater than these.
If Your Majesty does not serve Qín,
Qín will send its armored troops to occupy Yíyáng
and cut off Hán's Shàngdì;
if they take Chénggǎo and Yíyáng in the east,
then the palace of Hóngtái
and the gardens of Sānglín
will no longer belong to Your Majesty.
If they block Chénggǎo
and cut off Shàngdì,
then Your Majesty's state will be divided.
Serving Qín first will bring safety;
not serving Qín will bring danger.
To court disaster while seeking fortune,
to have shallow plans while incurring deep resentment,
and to oppose Qín while following Chǔ—
even if one wishes to avoid ruin,
it cannot be done.
Therefore, in planning for Your Majesty,
nothing is better than serving Qín.
What Qín desires
most is to weaken Chǔ,
and none can weaken Chǔ better than Hán.
This is not because Hán is stronger than Chǔ,
but because the terrain makes it so.
If Your Majesty now faces west to serve Qín in attacking Chǔ
for the sake of our humble state,
the King of Qín will surely be pleased.
To attack Chǔ and take its land for oneself,
turning disaster into a means to please Qín—
no plan is more advantageous than this.
For this reason, the King of Qín has sent me to present this letter to Your Majesty’s Royal Scribe,
waiting for a decision."
The King of Hán said:
"I am fortunate that the guest has taught me.
I request to be ranked among your commanderies and counties,
build an imperial palace,
offer sacrifices in spring and autumn,
call myself an Eastern Marchlord,
and surrender Yíyáng."
King Xuān said to Liáo Liú:
"I wish to employ both Gōngzhòng and Gōngshū;
is that possible?"
He replied:
"It is not.
Jìn used the Six Ministers and the state was divided.
Duke Jiǎn used Tián Chéng and Jiān Zhǐ and was assassinated.
Wèi used both Xīshǒu and Zhāng Yí and the lands outside Xīhé were lost.
If Your Majesty now uses both of them,
the one with more power will build his faction internally,
and the one with less power will rely on external authority.
Some ministers build factions internally to dominate their sovereign,
while others form external alliances to split the territory;
then Your Majesty's state will surely be in danger."
Zhāng Yí said to the King of Qí:
"Your Majesty would do better to support Hán Péng
and together with him expel Zhāng Yí from Wèi.
Wèi will then appoint Xīshǒu as Prime Minister;
then Qí and Wèi can discard Hán Péng
and make Gōngshū Prime Minister to attack Qín.
When Gōngzhòng hears of this,
he will certainly not enter Qí.
By supporting you in Wèi,
this will leave you without worries."
Chǔ Zhāo Xiàn was Prime Minister of Hán.
Qín was about to attack Hán,
so Hán dismissed Zhāo Xiàn.
Zhāo Xiàn sent someone to say to Gōngshū:
"It would be better to honor Zhāo Xiàn to solidify the alliance with Chǔ;
Qín will surely say Chǔ and Hán have united."
Qín attacked Xíng,
and Hán sent someone to yield the land of Nányáng.
Once Qín had taken it,
they attacked Xíng again,
so Hán ceded the land of Nányáng.
Qín received the land
and attacked Xíng again.
Chén Zhěn said to the King of Qín:
"When the state's situation is unfavorable, one yields;
when alliances are not close, one cedes land.
Now land has been ceded yet alliances are not close,
and yielding has occurred yet the troops do not stop;
I fear those east of the mountains will have no way to yield or cede land to serve Your Majesty.
Moreover, Your Majesty sought a hundred pieces of gold from Sānchuān and could not get it,
but sought a thousand pieces of gold from Hán,
and obtained it in a single morning.
Now for Your Majesty to attack Hán, this
is to cut off a superior alliance and consolidate your private treasury;
I humbly think Your Majesty should not take this course."
Five states formed an alliance to attack Qín, and the King of Chǔ was the alliance leader;
they could not harm Qín,
and the troops were exhausted and stayed at Chénggǎo.
Wèi Shùn said to the Lord of Shìqiū:
"The five states are exhausted
and will surely attack Shìqiū
to compensate for their military expenses.
If you support me,
I request to stop the world's attack on Shìqiū for you."
The Lord of Shìqiū said:
"Good."
And so he sent him.
Wèi Shùn went south to see the King of Chǔ and said:
"Your Majesty allied five states to attack Qín in the west,
but could not harm Qín.
The world will thus belittle Your Majesty and respect Qín;
therefore, why does Your Majesty not test the alliances?"
The King of Chǔ said:
"How?"
Wèi Shùn said:
"The world's troops are exhausted
and will surely attack Shìqiū to compensate for their military expenses.
Your Majesty should order them not to attack Shìqiū.
If the five states respect Your Majesty,
they will listen to Your Majesty's words and not attack Shìqiū;
if they do not respect Your Majesty,
they will go against Your Majesty's words and attack Shìqiū.
In this way, Your Majesty's weight will surely be made clear."
Therefore the King of Chǔ tested the alliances and Shìqiū was preserved.
Zhèng Qiáng brought eight hundred pieces of gold into Qín
to request an attack on Hán.
Líng Xiàng said to Zhèng Qiáng:
"You use eight hundred pieces of gold to request an attack on another's ally;
Qín will surely not listen to you.
You would do better to make the King of Qín doubt Gōngshū."
Zhèng Qiáng said:
"How?"
He replied:
"Gōngshū's attack on Chǔ
was because Jǐsè was there,
so he said 'Chǔ first'.
Now the King of Chǔ has been ordered to support Jǐsè with a hundred chariots residing in Yángzhái,
and Zhāo Xiàn has been ordered to move and stay with him.
In over ten days,
they have already been noticed.
Moreover, Jǐsè
is the enemy of Gōngshū,
and Zhāo Xiàn
is Gōngshū's man.
When the King of Qín hears of this,
he will surely doubt that Gōngshū is acting for Chǔ."
When Zhèng Qiáng was driving Zhāng Yí out of Qín,
he said that Zhāng Yí's envoy
would surely go to Chǔ.
Therefore he said to the Dàzǎi:
"You detain Yí's envoy,
and I request to go west to plot against Yí in Qín."
He then petitioned the King of Qín saying:
"Zhāng Yí sent someone to hand over the land of Shàngyōng,
so he sent an envoy to pay respects to the King of Qín."
The King of Qín was angry,
and Zhāng Yí fled.
During the campaign of Yíyáng,
Yáng Dá said to Gōngsūn Xiǎn:
"I request to attack Xīzhōu with fifty thousand men for you;
if we take it,
we can use the Jiǔdǐng to suppress Gān Mào.
Otherwise,
if Qín attacks Xīzhōu,
the world will hate it,
and they will rush to save Hán,
then Gān Mào's mission will fail."
Qín besieged Yíyáng,
and Yóu Téng said to Gōngzhòng:
"Why do you not give Zhào the lands of Lìn, Líshí, and Qí
as a pledge for the land of Xǔ?
Then Lóu Huǎn will surely fail.
Gather the troops of Hán and Zhào to face Wèi,
then Lóu Bí will surely fail.
When Hán is united,
Wèi will surely betray Qín,
and Gān Mào will surely fail.
If you support Zhái Qiáng in Qí with Chéngyáng,
Chǔ will surely defeat him.
Wait until Qín surely fails;
if Qín loses Wèi,
Yíyáng will certainly not be captured."
Because of the Yíyáng campaign, Gōngzhòng held a grudge against Gān Mào.
Later,
Qín returned Wǔsuì to Hán.
Afterward,
the King of Qín firmly suspected that Gān Mào had used Wǔsuì to make peace with Gōngzhòng.
Dù Hè said to the King of Qín on behalf of Gōngzhòng:
"Míng wishes to serve Your Majesty through Gān Mào."
The King of Qín was greatly enraged with Gān Mào,
so Chūlǐ Jí was greatly pleased with Dù Liáo.
Qín and Hàn fought at Zhuózé,
and the Hàn clan was in an urgent situation.
Gōngzhòng Míng said to the King of Hàn:
"Allied states cannot be relied upon.
Now Qín's heart desires to attack Chǔ;
it would be better for Your Majesty to use Zhāng Yí to make peace with Qín,
bribe them with a famous city,
and join them in attacking Chǔ.
This is a plan of exchanging one for two."
The King of Hàn said:
"Excellent."
He then prepared for Gōngzhòng's departure,
intending for him to go west to negotiate peace with Qín.
The King of Chǔ heard of this and was greatly terrified.
He summoned Chén Zhěn and told him about it.
Chén Zhěn said:
"Qín has wanted to attack us for a long time.
Now if they also obtain one famous city from Hàn and equip their soldiers,
and Qín and Hàn combine their forces to head south,
this is exactly what Qín has been praying for in their ancestral temples.
Now that they have already obtained it,
Chǔ will certainly be attacked. If Your Majesty
listens to your servant,
prepare to select troops from within the four borders,
proclaim that you are coming to rescue Hàn,
and make the war chariots fill the roads.
Dispatch trusted ministers,
increase the number of their chariots,
and make their gifts substantial,
so as to make Hàn believe Your Majesty is rescuing them.
Even if Hàn cannot listen to us,
Hàn will surely be grateful to Your Majesty,
and will definitely not advance in a 'goose-wing' formation against us.
Thus, Qín and Hàn will not be in harmony.
Even if their troops arrive,
Chǔ will not suffer a great blow.
If they can listen to us and break off their peace with Qín,
Qín will surely be greatly enraged
and harbor deep resentment toward Hàn.
When Hàn receives Chǔ's rescue,
they will surely take Qín lightly.
Taking Qín lightly,
their response to Qín will surely be disrespectful.
This is how we exhaust the troops of Qín and Hàn
and avoid the disaster of Chǔ."
The King of Chǔ was greatly pleased.
He then prepared the selected troops from within the four borders,
proclaimed that he was rescuing Hàn,
dispatched trusted ministers,
increased their chariots,
and made their gifts substantial.
He said to the King of Hàn:
"Although my humble state is small,
we have already raised all our forces.
I hope your great state will follow your will regarding Qín;
my humble state will sacrifice itself for Hàn."
The King of Hàn was greatly pleased
and stopped Gōngzhòng.
Gōngzhòng said:
"This cannot be.
The one who tells us the reality
is Qín;
the one who rescues us with an empty name
is Chǔ.
Relying on Chǔ's empty name
and lightly breaking off with a powerful enemy like Qín
will surely make us the laughingstock of the world.
Furthermore, Chǔ and Hàn are not brotherly states,
nor have they traditionally agreed to plot against Qín.
Qín wanted to attack Chǔ,
so Chǔ used the raising of troops to claim they were rescuing Hàn;
this must be Chén Zhěn's plot.
Moreover, Your Majesty has already sent an envoy to report to Qín;
if we do not go now,
this is deceiving Qín.
To take lightly the disaster of a powerful Qín
and trust the scheming ministers of Chǔ—
Your Majesty will surely regret this."
The King of Hàn did not listen
and subsequently broke off the peace with Qín.
Qín was indeed greatly enraged.
They raised an army and fought the Hàn clan at Ànmén.
Chǔ's rescue did not arrive,
and the Hàn clan was heavily defeated.
It was not that the Hàn clan's troops were weak,
nor that the people were ignorant,
yet the troops were captured by Qín
and their wisdom was mocked by Chǔ,
because they listened excessively to Chén Zhěn
and failed in their strategy with Hàn Míng.
Yán Shuài went to see Gōngzhòng,
but Gōngzhòng would not see him.
Yán Shuài said to Gōngzhòng's usher:
"Gōngzhòng must think Shuài is insincere,
which is why he will not see me.
Gōngzhòng likes the internal harem,
but Shuài said he likes scholars;
Gōngzhòng is stingy with wealth,
but Shuài said he was generous;
Gōngzhòng is without virtue,
but Shuài said he loves righteousness.
From now on,
Shuài will only speak the truth."
Gōngzhòng's usher told this to Gōngzhòng,
and Gōngzhòng hurriedly rose and saw him.
Gōngzhòng of Hàn said to Xiàng Shòu:
"A trapped beast will overturn a chariot.
You have broken Hàn
and humiliated Gōngzhòng.
Gōngzhòng has gathered the state to serve Qín again,
thinking for himself that he would surely be enfeoffed.
Now you have reconciled with Chǔ
and enfeoffed the Lesser Lìngyǐn with Guìyáng.
If Qín and Chǔ unite
and attack Hàn again,
Hàn will surely perish.
Gōngzhòng will personally lead his private followers to fight against Qín;
I hope you consider this carefully."
Xiàng Shòu said:
"I united Qín and Chǔ,
not to oppose Hàn.
You, please announce me to him."
Gōngzhòng said:
"The relations between Qín and Hàn can be united."
The reply was:
"I wish to report to you.
The proverb says:
'Value that which makes the valued person valued.'
Now the King's love and familiarity with you
is not equal to that of Gōngsūn Hǎo;
his estimation of your wisdom and ability
is not equal to that of Gān Mào.
Now these two men
are both unable to be close to affairs,
and you alone decide with the King on national matters;
it is because they have something they lost.
Gōngsūn Hǎo was partial to Hàn,
and Gān Mào was partial to Wèi,
therefore the King did not trust them.
Now Qín and Chǔ are competing for power,
and if you are partial to Chǔ,
this is following the same path as Gōngsūn Hǎo and Gān Mào.
How are you different from them?
People all say Chǔ is full of change,
yet you trust it;
this is for your own prestige.
It would be better for you to plot with the King regarding their fickleness,
and befriend Hàn to prepare for them;
in this way,
there will be no disaster.
The Hàn clan first followed Gōngsūn Hǎo with their state,
and later entrusted the state to Gān Mào;
this Hàn
is your enemy.
Now if you speak of befriending Hàn to prepare against Chǔ,
this is recommending externally without avoiding enemies."
Xiàng Shòu said:
"I very much want to unite with Hàn."
The reply was:
"Gān Mào promised Wǔsuì to Gōngzhòng
and returned the people of Yíyáng;
now if you merely order their return,
it will be very difficult."
Xiàngzǐ said:
"If so, then what should be done?
Wǔsuì ultimately cannot be obtained."
The reply was:
"Why do you not, on behalf of Qín, ask Chǔ for Yǐngchuān for Hàn?
This is Hàn's entrusted land.
If you seek it and get it,
your orders will be followed in Chǔ and you will make Hàn grateful with that land.
If you seek it and do not get it,
then the resentment between Hàn and Chǔ will not be resolved,
and both will turn to Qín.
Qín and Chǔ are competing for power,
and if you go past Chǔ to attack Hàn,
this benefits Qín."
Xiàngzǐ said:
"How so?"
The reply was:
"This is a good matter.
Gān Mào wanted to use Wèi to take Qí;
Gōngsūn Hǎo wanted to use Hàn to take Qí;
now you take Yíyáng to make it your achievement,
gather Chǔ and Hàn to stabilize them,
and punish the crimes of Qí and Wèi;
this is how you make Gōngsūn Hǎo and Gān Mào appear to have done nothing."
Someone said to Gōngzhòng:
"Those who listen to the state
do not necessarily listen to reality.
Therefore the former kings listened to proverbs in the markets.
I wish for you to listen to your servant's words."
You seek neutrality from Qín,
but you have not been able to obtain it.
You favor Gōngsūn Hǎo to cause difficulty for Gān Mào,
and you encourage the Qí army to stop Wèi,
but Chǔ and Zhào are both your enemies.
I fear the state will suffer for this,
and I wish for you to again seek neutrality from Qín.
Gōngzhòng said:
“How shall I do it?”
The reply was:
“The King of Qín believes Gōngsūn Hǎo is a partisan of yours and will not listen to him.
Gān Mào is not on good terms with you and will not speak for you.
Why do you not use Xíng Yuàn to speak with the King of Qín?
Xíng Yuàn is a minister of the King of Qín.
I shall ask him to say to the King of Qín for you:
‘Which is more beneficial to Qín: for Qí and Wèi to be united or separated?
Which is more beneficial to Qín?
Which makes Qín stronger: for Qí and Wèi to be apart or united?
Which makes Qín stronger?’
The King of Qín will surely say:
‘If Qí and Wèi are separated,
then Qín is significant;
if they are united,
then Qín is insignificant.
If Qí and Wèi are apart,
then Qín is strong;
if they are united,
then Qín is weak.’
I will then say:
‘Now if Your Majesty listens to Gōngsūn Hǎo and uses the troops of Hán and Qín to support Qí and attack Wèi,
Wèi will not dare to fight,
but will return land and unite with Qí.
This makes Qín insignificant,
and I consider Gōngsūn Hǎo to be disloyal.
Now if Your Majesty listens to Gān Mào,
and uses the troops of Hán and Qín to occupy Wèi and attack Qí,
Qí will not dare to fight,
but will join with Wèi without even seeking a partition of land.
This makes Qín insignificant,
and I consider Gān Mào to be disloyal.
Therefore, it would be better for Your Majesty to order Hán to remain neutral while attacking Qí.
The King of Qí will claim to rescue Wèi to embolden it;
Qí and Wèi will not listen to each other,
and their armies will remain separated for a long time.
If Your Majesty desires,
then trust Gōngsūn Hǎo with Qí
to take Nányáng for Hán
and exchange Gǔchuān to return;
this was the wish of Huì Wáng.
If Your Majesty desires,
then trust Gān Mào with Wèi
and use the troops of Hán and Qín to occupy Wèi to distance Qí;
this was the wish of Wǔ Wáng.
I believe that ordering Hán to remain neutral to embolden Qí
is Qín's most urgent matter.
Gōngsūn Hǎo is a partisan of Qí and is unwilling to say so;
Gān Mào is of little influence and dares not present the matter.
These two men
are Your Majesty's great worries.
I hope Your Majesty will consider this carefully.’”
Hán Gōngzhòng was the Prime Minister.
The diplomatic relations between Qí and Chǔ favored Qín.
Qín and Wèi met,
intending to be friendly with Qí and sever Qí’s ties with Chǔ.
The King sent Jǐng Lǐ to Qín,
and Jǐng Lǐ participated in the meeting between Qín and Wèi.
The King of Chǔ was angry with Jǐng Lǐ,
fearing that Qí would think Chǔ’s participation in the meeting meant there was a secret plot with Qín and Wèi,
and he intended to punish Jǐng Lǐ.
Someone said to the King of Chǔ:
“I congratulate Jǐng Lǐ for participating in the meeting.
The meeting of Qín and Wèi
was intended to unite Qí and Qín and sever Qí from Chǔ.
Now that Jǐng Lǐ participated in the meeting,
Qí has no reason to believe that Wèi is joining with Qín to attack Chǔ.
Qí also fears that Chǔ has a secret plot with Qín and Wèi,
and will certainly value Chǔ.
Therefore, Jǐng Lǐ’s participation in the meeting
is a great asset to Your Majesty.
If Jǐng Lǐ had not participated in the meeting,
Wèi’s severance of Qí from Chǔ would be clear.
If Qí and Chǔ believe this,
they will certainly think lightly of Your Majesty.
Therefore, it is better for Your Majesty not to punish Jǐng Lǐ,
but to use Wèi
to show Qí that there is a connection with Qín. Qí will then certainly value Chǔ,
and moreover suspect the relationship between Qín and Wèi regarding Qí.”
The King said:
“Agreed.”
Thus he did not punish him but increased his rank.
The King said:
“Before, you said ‘the world is without the Way,’
but now you say
‘you are about to attack Yān’; why is that?”
The reply was: “If one says a horse has great strength, that may be true,
but if one says it can carry a thousand jūn, that is not so. Why is that?
A thousand jūn
is not a burden a horse can bear.
If one says Chǔ is powerful, that may be true,
but if it crosses Zhào and Wèi to wage war in Yān,
how can that be a burden for Chǔ?
Moreover, it is not Chǔ’s responsibility,
yet if Chǔ does it,
this will exhaust Chǔ.
Between a strong Chǔ and an exhausted Chǔ,
which is more convenient for Your Majesty?”
Someone said to the King of Wèi:
“Your Majesty should alert everyone within the four borders;
those who follow Your Majesty,
within ten days,
those whose equipment is not ready shall die.
Your Majesty should then take the pleasure boats and attack from upstream.
I shall go to Chǔ for Your Majesty,
and Your Majesty should wait for me to return
before setting out.”
Chūn Shēn Jūn heard of this
and said to the messenger:
“You go back for me,
and do not see the King.
Within ten days,
a multitude of tens of thousands
is now crossing the border of Wèi.”
The messenger from Qín heard this
and reported it to the King of Qín.
The King of Qín said to the King of Wèi:
“If your great state has an intention,
you must come; this alone is enough.”
Guān Yǎng said to Chūn Shēn:
“Everyone thinks Chǔ is strong,
but you use it as if it were weak.
To me, Guān Yǎng, it is not so.
The former kings
were not attacked for over twenty years.
Now Qín wants to send troops across the passes of Miǎn’ài,
but is not allowed;
it wants to borrow a path through the two Zhōu and bypass Hán to attack Chǔ,
but it is not possible.
Now it is not so.
Wèi will perish sooner or later;
it cannot protect its cities of Xǔ, Yānlíng, and Wǔ,
and will cede them to Qín, moving back a hundred and sixty lǐ.
What I see
is that the day when Qín and Chǔ fight is already here.”
Gōngzhòng repeatedly broke his word to the feudal lords,
and the feudal lords ostracized him.
In the south, he entrusted the state to Chǔ,
but the King of Chǔ would not listen.
Sū Dài said for the King of Chǔ:
“It is better to listen to him but prepare for his betrayal.
When Gōngzhòng betrays,
he usually relies on Zhào to rebel against Chǔ,
or relies on Qí to rebel against Qín.
Now the four states have ostracized him,
and he has nowhere to go;
he is also very worried about this.
This is just when he is like Wěi Shēng.”
Chǔ besieged Yōngshì for five months.
Hán ordered messengers to seek help from Qín,
and their caps and carriages were in sight of one another,
yet the Qín army would not come down from Xiáo.
Hán then ordered Shàng Jìn to go to Qín
and say to the King of Qín:
“Hán's relation to Qín is such that
at rest it serves as a screen,
and in action it serves as the lead in a formation.
Now Hán is already distressed,
yet the Qín army will not come down from Xiáo.
I have heard
that when the lips are gone, the teeth are cold.
I hope Your Majesty will consider this carefully.”
Xuān Tàihòu said:
“Many messengers have come,
but only the words of Shàng Jìn are correct.”
She summoned Shàng Jìn to enter.
Xuān Tàihòu said to Shàng Jìn:
“When I served the late King,
when the late King rested his thigh upon my body,
I found it exhausting;
but when he placed his whole body upon me,
I did not find him heavy.
Why?
Because it was somewhat to my advantage.
Now to assist Hán,
if the troops are not numerous
and the provisions are not abundant,
then it is not enough to save Hán.
To save Hán from its peril
will cost a thousand pieces of gold a day;
is it not possible to make it even slightly to my advantage?”
Shàng Jìn returned with a letter to report to the King of Hán.
The King of Hán sent Zhāng Cuì.
Zhāng Cuì feigned illness
and traveled through only one county each day.
When Zhāng Cuì arrived,
Gān Mào said:
"Hán is in urgent distress,
yet you, sir, have come while ill."
Zhāng Cuì said:
"Hán is not yet in urgent distress,
but it is about to be."
Gān Mào said:
"Qín is a powerful state that knows your King well,
and whether Hán's situation is urgent or not, there is nothing it does not know. Now you say it is not urgent,
is that acceptable?"
Zhāng Cuì said:
"If Hán were in urgent distress, it would have broken away and joined Chǔ.
How would I then dare to come here?"
Gān Mào said:
"Sir, say no more."
Gān Mào went in to speak to the King of Qín, saying:
"Gōng Zhòng relied on receiving Qín's troops,
therefore he dared to resist Chǔ.
Now Yōngshì is besieged,
and if Qín's troops do not descend through Yáo,
this is to be without Hán.
Gōng Zhòng will then bow his head and no longer attend court,
and Gōng Shú will lead the state south to unite with Chǔ.
Once Chǔ and Hán are one,
the Wèi clan will not dare but to comply.
This means Chǔ would be using three states to plot against Qín.
If it is like this, the formation for attacking Qín will be complete.
I do not know whether sitting and waiting to be attacked
is as beneficial as the advantage of attacking others."
The King of Qín said:
"Good."
He indeed sent troops down through Yáo to rescue Hán.
When Chǔ besieged Yōngshì,
Hán ordered Lěng Xiàng to seek rescue from Qín.
Qín sent the envoy Gōngsūn Mèi to enter Hán.
Gōng Zhòng said:
"Do you think Qín is about to rescue Hán?
Or not?"
He replied:
"The King of Qín's words were,
'Please clear the way through Nánzhèng and Lántián to enter and attack Chǔ,
and deploy troops at Sānchuān to wait for you.'
This likely does not match his intentions,
for he has camped his army at Nánzhèng."
Gōng Zhòng said:
"What can be done?"
He replied:
"The King of Qín will surely follow the old strategy of Zhāng Yí.
When King Wēi of Chǔ attacked Liáng,
Zhāng Yí said to the King of Qín:
'If we join with Chǔ to attack Liáng,
Wèi will break and join Chǔ.
Hán is already its ally state,
and so Qín will be isolated.
Therefore, it is better to deploy troops to strengthen Wèi.'
Thereupon they attacked Píshì.
The Wèi clan was strengthened,
King Wēi was angry,
Chǔ and Wèi fought a great battle,
and Qín took the lands outside Xīhé and returned.
Now he will publicly claim to rescue Hán
but secretly befriend Chǔ.
If you rely on Qín and act boldly,
you will surely lightly engage in battle with Chǔ.
Chǔ secretly knows that Qín will not be used,
so it will be easy for them to contend with you.
If you win the battle against Chǔ,
they will then join you in taking advantage of Chǔ,
exchange Sānchuān, and return.
If you do not win the battle against Chǔ,
they will block Sānchuān and defend it,
and you will not be able to be rescued.
I deeply dislike this affair.
Sīmǎ Kāng has gone to Yǐng three times,
and Gān Mào met with Zhāo Xiàn at the border.
Their words say they are collecting seals,
but in reality, there is still an agreement."
Gōng Zhòng was afraid and said:
"Then what can be done?"
He replied:
"You must put Hán first and Qín second,
yourself first and Zhāng Yí second.
By my estimation, it is better to quickly unite the state with Qí and Chǔ.
Qín will surely entrust the state to you to avert the attack.
In this way, the one you keep outside is only Zhāng Yí,
and in reality, you still do not lose Qín."
Gōng Zhòng was to exchange territory for Hán and Wèi.
Gōng Shú disputed this but was not listened to,
and he was about to flee.
Shǐ Tì said to Gōng Shú:
"If you flee,
then the exchange will surely be accomplished.
You will have no excuse to return later,
and it will show the world that you are held in low regard.
It would be better to go along with it.
If the Hán lands are exchanged above,
then it will harm Zhào.
If the Wèi lands are exchanged below,
then it will harm Chǔ.
You should inform Chǔ and Zhào.
Chǔ and Zhào will hate it.
When Zhào hears of it,
they will raise troops and approach Yángcháng.
When Chǔ hears of it,
they will dispatch troops and approach Fāngchéng,
and the exchange will surely fail."
Qì Xuān instructed the King of Hán on how to deal with Qín,
saying:
"Prepare a hundred chariots for Gōng Shú,
speak of it to Chǔ,
and exchange Sānchuān.
Then have Gōng Zhòng say to the King of Qín:
'The talk in Sānchuān is
that the King of Qín will surely take us.
The King of Hán's mind cannot be eased.
Why does your Majesty not try sending Xiāng Zǐ as a hostage to Hán
to let the King of Hán know that your Majesty will not take Sānchuān?'
Then by sending out Xiāng Zǐ, the Crown Prince will feel indebted."
During the campaign of Xiānglíng,
Bì Cháng said to Gōng Shú:
"I suggest not using troops,
and both Chǔ and Wèi will be indebted to your state.
Chǔ wants to establish Prince Gāo
and will surely approach Wèi with troops.
Why do you not send someone to say to Zhāo Zǐ:
'Victory in battle is not certain;
please let me raise troops for you to go to Wèi.'
You will then have an excuse not to fight,
and because of this, Crown Prince Biǎn,
Zhāo Yáng, and the King of Liáng will all be indebted to you."
Gōng Shú sent Féng Jūn to Qín.
Fearing he would be detained,
he taught Yáng Xiàng to persuade the King of Qín, saying:
"To detain Féng Jūn to befriend the ministers of Hán
is not the highest wisdom.
It would be better for you to treat Féng Jūn well
and support him with the resources of Qín.
Féng Jūn will then broaden your Majesty's influence and not listen to Gōng Shú
and will contend with the Crown Prince.
Then your Majesty's favor will be spread
while Hán will be harmed."
Someone said to Gōng Shú:
"You wish to obtain Wǔsuì from Qín, but you do not worry about Chǔ being able to spread its influence beyond the River.
It would be better to send someone to frighten the King of Chǔ
and send someone to seek Wǔsuì from Qín for you.
Say to the King of Chǔ:
'Dispatch a high-ranking envoy to seek Wǔsuì from Qín for Hán.
If the King of Qín listens,
then your orders will be carried out by the ruler of a state of ten thousand chariots.
Hán will obtain Wǔsuì and resent Qín,
and without having to fear Qín, they will join Chǔ.
Hán will then be nothing more than a county of Chǔ.
If Qín does not listen,
then the resentment between Qín and Hán will be deep,
and Hán will ally with Chǔ.'"
Someone said to Gōng Shú:
"When riding in a boat,
if the boat leaks and is not plugged,
the boat will sink.
If you plug the leaky boat
but make light of the waves of Yánghóu,
the boat will capsize.
Now you consider yourself more persuasive than Lord Xuē and make light of Qín;
this is like plugging a leaky boat and making light of the waves of Yánghóu.
I hope you will examine this."
Qí ordered Zhōu Zuì on a mission to Zhèng
to establish Hán Rǎo and depose Gōng Shú.
Zhōu Zuì was worried about this
and said:
"Gōng Shú has a friendship with the Lord of Zhōu.
Now they order me to go to Zhèng
to establish Hán Rǎo and depose Gōng Shú.
The saying goes: 'One who is angry at home shows it in the market.'
Now Gōng Shú will resent Qí
but there is nothing he can do about it,
so he will surely deeply resent me through the Lord of Zhōu."
Shǐ Shè said: "Go on your mission,
and I will ensure that Gōng Shú will certainly value you."
Zhōu Zuì traveled and reached Zhèng,
and Gōng Shú was greatly enraged.
Shǐ Shè went in to see him and said:
"Zhōu Zuì originally did not want to come on this mission,
but I privately forced him to.
Zhōu Zuì's not wanting to come
was for your sake;
and my forcing him to come
was also for your sake."
Gōng Shū said: “I would like to hear your explanation.”
The other replied:
“Zhū Zǐ, a grandee of Qí, had a dog.
The dog was so fierce it could not be shouted at;
if one shouted at it, it would surely bite people.
A guest asked to shout at it.
He stared at it intently and then shouted at it slowly.
The dog did not move.
He shouted at it again,
and the dog then had no intention of biting people.
Now Zhōu Zuì certainly seeks to serve you,
but he has come as an envoy only because he had no choice.
He will present his message with ritual propriety and speak his words slowly.
Zhèng Wáng will surely think that the King of Qí is not in a hurry,
and he will surely not grant the request.
Now if Zhōu Zuì does not come,
someone else certainly will.
The envoy who comes will have no personal ties with you,
and will want to gain favor with Hán Rǎo.
He will surely carry out his mission with haste
and speak with urgency;
then Zhèng Wáng will surely grant it.”
Gōng Shū said: “Good.”
Consequently, he treated Zhōu Zuì with great respect.
As expected, the King did not grant Hán Rǎo's request.
Gōng Shū of Hán and Jǐ Sè were contending for the state.
Zhèng Qiáng went as an envoy for the King of Chǔ to Hán.
He falsely used Xīn Chéng and Yáng Rén to join with the Heir Apparent
in order to contend for the state against Gōng Shū.
Chǔ was angry
and intended to punish him.
Zhèng Qiáng said:
“My falsely giving them to him
was for the sake of the state.
I said:
‘If the Heir Apparent obtains Xīn Chéng and Yáng Rén
to contend for the state against Gōng Shū
and manages to survive,
Wèi will surely press the Hán clan hard.
If the Hán clan is pressed,
they will surely entrust their lives to Chǔ.
Then how would they dare to ask for Xīn Chéng and Yáng Rén back?
If they fight and do not win,
or flee but do not die,
and eventually arrive here,
how would they then dare to speak of land?’”
The King of Chǔ said: “Good.”
And so he did not punish him.
Gōng Shū of Hán and Jǐ Sè were contending for the state.
Zhōng Shù Zǐ Qiáng said to the Crown Prince:
“It would be better to take advantage of the fact that the Qí army has not yet entered
and quickly attack Gōng Shū.”
The Crown Prince said: “I cannot.
Fighting within the capital will surely cause a division.”
The attendant replied: “If the matter does not succeed,
your person will surely be in danger.
How then can you still consider the preservation of the whole state?”
The Crown Prince did not listen.
The Qí army did indeed enter,
and the Crown Prince fled.
Qí Míng said to Gōng Shū:
“Qí has expelled Jǐ Sè,
and Chǔ is pleased with this.
Now Chǔ wishes to be on very good terms with Qí.
Why do you not have the King of Qí say to the King of Chǔ:
‘Will the King, for my sake, expel Jǐ Sè to bring him to ruin?’
If Chǔ listens,
then Qí and Chǔ will be united
and Jǐ Sè will have to flee.
If the King of Chǔ does not listen,
then he has secret designs against Hán.”
Gōng Shū was about to kill Jǐ Sè.
Someone said to Gōng Shū:
“The reason the Crown Prince values you
is that he fears Jǐ Sè.
Now if Jǐ Sè dies,
the Crown Prince will have no worries
and will surely treat you lightly.
The grandees of Hán see that the King is old
and hope the Crown Prince will take power;
they naturally wish to serve him.
If the Crown Prince has no threat from Jǐ Sè abroad
and gathers the grandees internally to support himself,
you will surely be treated lightly.
It would be better not to kill Jǐ Sè
so as to keep the Crown Prince in fear.
The Crown Prince will surely value you for the rest of his life.”
Gōng Shū was about to kill Jǐ Sè.
Sòng Hè said to Gōng Shū on his behalf:
“Jǐ Sè is able to cause trouble
because internally he has the support of his clan elders
and externally he has the support of Qín and Chǔ.
Now if you kill him,
the Crown Prince will have no worries
and will surely treat you lightly.
The grandees of Hán know the King is old and the Crown Prince's position is secure,
so they will surely serve him in secret.
If Qín and Chǔ lack influence in Hán,
they will surely serve Bó Yīng in secret.
Bó Yīng is just another Jǐ Sè.
It would be better for you not to kill him.
Bó Yīng will be afraid
and will surely rely on you for protection.
The grandees of Hán cannot be sure that Jǐ Sè will not return,
so they will surely not dare to support Bó Yīng in causing trouble.
If Qín and Chǔ use Jǐ Sè to block Bó Yīng,
Bó Yīng will have no power from Qín and Chǔ abroad
and no support from the clan elders at home;
he will certainly be unable to cause trouble.
This is to your advantage.”
Someone said to the Lord of Xīn Chéng:
“Gōng Shū and Bó Yīng fear that Qín and Chǔ will bring Jǐ Sè back into the country.
Why do you not request a hostage from Chǔ on behalf of Hán?
If the King of Chǔ listens and sends a hostage to Hán,
then Gōng Shū and Bó Yīng will surely know that Qín and Chǔ are not making Jǐ Sè their priority,
and they will surely align Hán with Qín and Chǔ.
Qín and Chǔ will then use Hán to pressure Wèi;
Wèi will not dare to expand eastward,
and thus Qí will be isolated.
If you then have Qín request a hostage from Chǔ,
and Chǔ does not listen,
then resentment will be established with Hán.
If Hán uses Qí and Wèi to keep an eye on Chǔ,
the King of Chǔ will surely value you.
If you hold the weight of Qín and Chǔ
and build up merit in Hán,
then Gōng Shū and Bó Yīng will surely serve you with the affairs of the state.”
When Hú Yǎn helped Jǐ Sè get out of Chǔ,
he instructed Gōng Zhòng to say to the King of Wèi:
“The Heir Apparent is in Chǔ,
so Hán does not dare to distance itself from Chǔ.
Why do you not try to support Gōngzǐ Jiù
and on his behalf request the return of the Heir Apparent? Then, have someone say to the King of Chǔ:
‘Hán has established Gōngzǐ Jiù and abandoned Jǐ Sè;
thus, the King is holding a useless hostage.
The King would be better off returning Jǐ Sè immediately.
If Jǐ Sè enters Hán,
he will surely use the power of Hán to take revenge on Wèi
and will be grateful to the King.’”
Jǐ Sè fled to Chǔ,
and Chǔ intended to win over Qín to restore him.
Someone said to Mǐ Róng:
“It is Chǔ that would depose Gōng Shū and make Jǐ Sè the Prime Minister.
Now that Jǐ Sè has fled to Chǔ
and Chǔ is winning over Qín to restore him,
on the day Jǐ Sè enters Zhèng,
Hán
will become a mere county of Chǔ.
It would be better for you to have the King of Qín congratulate Bó Yīng on his establishment.
If Hán breaks with Chǔ,
it will surely serve Qín with haste.
If Qín uses Hán to befriend Wèi,
then among Qí and Chǔ, whichever arrives later will be the first to perish.
This is the work of a Hegemon King.”
Lěng Xiàng said to Hán Jiù:
“Jǐ Sè is in exile in Chǔ,
and the King of Chǔ strongly desires to restore him.
He has ordered over a hundred thousand Chǔ troops to be outside Fāng Chéng.
I request that Chǔ be told to build a city of ten thousand households next to Yōng Shì.
Hán will surely raise troops to prevent it,
and you will surely be the general.
You can then use the troops of Chǔ and Hán to support Jǐ Sè and bring him into Zhèng.
When Jǐ Sè manages to enter and feels grateful to you,
he will surely use both Hán and Chǔ to support you.”
Chǔ ordered Jǐng Lǐ to enter Hán.
Hán was also about to send Bó Yīng to Qín as a hostage,
and Jǐng Lǐ was worried about this.
Lěng Xiàng said to Bó Yīng:
“If the Crown Prince enters Qín,
Qín will surely detain the Crown Prince and unite with Chǔ
